Chapter

The two base classes

Everything on screen is driven through one of these two. Learn them first — every page and every component inherits from here.

01

BasePage

src/pages/BasePage.ts · 974 lines

The shared toolbox of browser actions that every Page Object inherits.

An abstract class holding every click, fill, wait and read the framework uses. Your page class extends it and adds only locators and business actions.

Why it existsSo no page class rewrites clicking, waiting, logging, or error reporting.

How you use itsrc/pages/EmployeePage.ts (last line from tests/ui/regression/employee-management.regression.spec.ts)
// src/pages/EmployeePage.ts
export class EmployeePage extends BasePage {
  protected readonly path = '/employees';   // where open() navigates
  public readonly rootIndicator: Locator;   // proves the page rendered

  public async openCreateForm(): Promise<void> {
    await this.click(this.addEmployeeButton);
    await this.formModal.expectOpen();
  }
}

// in a spec
await employeesAs.open();   // navigate, then wait for rootIndicator
open(path?)
Go to the page, then wait until it renders.
waitUntilLoaded()
Waits for rootIndicator, the element proving this page loaded.
click(target, options?)
Clicks an element. Target is a locator or a selector string.
fill(target, value)
Sets an input's value in one shot.
getText(target)
Reads an element's visible text, already trimmed.
downloadFile(target)
Clicks, catches the download, saves it, returns the file path.
acceptDialog(trigger)
Runs your click, then clicks OK on the browser popup.
perform(name, target, action)
Every action goes through one wrapper, so failures say what broke.

Showing the 8 you will use most — the class has 86 members in total.

TipforceClick skips Playwright's safety checks — a force click that passes usually hides a real bug.

02

BaseComponent

src/components/BaseComponent.ts · 77 lines

Base class for one reusable region of a screen: a table, modal, or toast.

A component owns a part of the page and is pinned to a root locator. Pages hold components instead of copying their locators.

Why it existsA header change gets fixed once, not on every page that shows it.

How you use itsrc/components/ToastComponent.ts
// src/components/ToastComponent.ts
export class ToastComponent extends BaseComponent {
  public readonly toasts: Locator;

  constructor(page: Page) {
    super(page, page.locator('#toastRegion'));      // root = the region it owns
    this.toasts = this.root.getByTestId('toast');   // scoped to root
  }

  public async expectSuccess(text: string | RegExp): Promise<void> {
    await expect(this.byVariant('success').filter({ hasText: text }).first()).toBeVisible();
  }
}
super(page, root)
Pass the page and the root element this component owns.
this.root
The locator every element inside the component hangs off.
isVisible(timeout?)
True or false, never throws — safe for if-checks.
waitUntilVisible(timeout?)
Waits for the region to appear, or fails the test.
waitUntilHidden(timeout?)
Waits for the region to go away, like a closing modal.
perform(name, target, action)
Same failure wrapper as BasePage, for your component methods.

Showing the 6 you will use most — the class has 8 members in total.

TipBuild inner locators from this.root, not from page — two copies of the widget on screen will otherwise break the test.

Chapter

Page Objects

One class per screen. A test asks the page to do something; the page knows the buttons.

03

EmployeePage

src/pages/EmployeePage.ts · 217 lines

The employees screen. Create, edit, delete and search records as one-line workflows.

The page object for /employees. It bundles the table, search bar, pagination, two modals and a date picker, then exposes whole workflows on top of them.

Why it existsSo a spec reads as a business workflow (createEmployee) instead of a script of clicks.

How you use ittests/ui/regression/employee-management.regression.spec.ts
test('An employee can be created through the UI', async ({ employeesAs, cleanup }) => {
  const employee = buildEmployee({ templateKey: 'engineer' });

  await employeesAs.open();
  await employeesAs.createEmployee({ ...employee, active: true });

  await employeesAs.searchFor(employee.email);
  await employeesAs.expectEmployeeRow(employee);
  cleanup.employee(await employeesAs.getEmployeeIdByName(employee.name));
});
path = '/employees'
The URL this page owns — where open() goes.
rootIndicator = this.heading
The "Employees" H1 that proves the page rendered.
createEmployee(input)
Opens the form, fills it, saves, waits for the success toast.
updateEmployee(name, changes)
Edits the named row with only the fields you pass.
deleteEmployee(name)
Deletes the named row through the confirmation dialog.
searchFor(email)
Filters the table down to matching rows.
expectEmployeeRow(input)
Asserts the visible row shows the values you submitted.
getEmployeeIdByName(name)
Reads the row's id, usually to clean up via the API.

Showing the 8 you will use most — the class has 39 members in total.

TipForm fields are scoped to the modal on purpose — the filter bar also has a "Department" label, so a page-wide locator would match two elements and fail.

04

DashboardPage

src/pages/DashboardPage.ts · 160 lines

The landing screen after sign-in: KPI tiles, file upload, CSV export and the nav shell.

The page object for /dashboard. It wraps the four metric tiles and reuses the shared header, sidebar and toast components.

Why it existsGives specs one place to read dashboard numbers and drive its actions (upload, export, reset).

How you use ittests/ui/sanity/dashboard.sanity.spec.ts
test.use({ role: 'ADMIN' });   // run under the stored ADMIN session

test('Workforce metrics reflect the directory', async ({ dashboardAs }) => {
  await dashboardAs.open();
  await dashboardAs.expectLoaded();

  const { metrics, total } = await dashboardAs.openAndCaptureSource();
  expect(metrics.totalEmployees).toBe(total);
  expect(metrics.averageSalary).toMatch(/^₹/);
});
this.path = environment.ui.dashboardPath
The URL this page owns (/dashboard) — where open() goes.
rootIndicator = this.heading
The "Dashboard" H1 that proves the page rendered.
getMetrics()
Reads the four KPI tiles as numbers, once they have loaded.
openAndCaptureSource()
Opens the page and also returns the API total it rendered from.
exportEmployeesCsv()
Clicks Export and returns the path of the downloaded file.
confirmWorkspaceReset()
Accepts the browser confirm popup and returns its message.
openEmployeesInNewTab()
Clicks the link and hands you the new tab's Page.
sidebar.navigateTo('Employees')
Shared nav component; header and toast are here too.

Showing the 8 you will use most — the class has 30 members in total.

TipTiles start life as a dash placeholder. Call getMetrics() — it waits for real numbers — instead of reading the tile locators yourself.

05

LoginPage

src/pages/LoginPage.ts · 102 lines

The sign-in screen. Logs you in by role, so passwords never appear in a spec.

The page object for /login. It knows the email, password and Remember me fields, and how to submit them. Its `loginAs` looks the real password up from environment variables.

Why it existsSo a spec can say "sign in as ADMIN" without knowing or hardcoding any password.

How you use ittests/ui/smoke/login.smoke.spec.ts
test('An administrator can sign in', async ({ loginPage, dashboardPage }) => {
  await loginPage.open();            // go to /login, wait for the heading
  await loginPage.loginAs('ADMIN');  // password comes from env, not the spec

  await dashboardPage.expectLoaded();
  expect(await loginPage.hasSessionToken()).toBe(true);
});
this.path = environment.ui.loginPath
The URL this page owns (/login) — where open() goes.
rootIndicator = this.heading
The element that proves the page rendered; open() waits for it.
open()
Goes to /login and waits for the Sign in heading.
loginAs('ADMIN')
Signs in as a role, pulling that role's password from the environment.
login(email, password)
Signs in with given credentials, then waits for the dashboard URL.
attemptInvalidLogin(email, password)
Submits bad credentials and returns the error text shown.
expectLoaded()
Asserts the form is visible, editable and its button enabled.
hasSessionToken()
True when a login token is sitting in browser storage.

Showing the 8 you will use most — the class has 18 members in total.

TipNever type a password into a spec. Use loginAs(role) — the secret is resolved from env vars or CI secrets.

06

ProfilePage

src/pages/ProfilePage.ts · 49 lines

A small read-only page showing who is signed in: name, email and role.

The page object for /profile. Three text fields, one getter and one assertion helper — nothing on it changes anything.

Why it existsLets a test confirm a stored session really belongs to the user it claims.

How you use itsrc/pages/ProfilePage.ts
// a spec gets one from the `profileAs` fixture: new ProfilePage(authenticatedPage)
public async getDetails(): Promise<ProfileDetails> {
  await expect(this.email).not.toHaveText('—'); // wait out the placeholder
  return {
    name: await this.getText(this.name),
    email: await this.getText(this.email),
    role: await this.getText(this.role),
  };
}
path = '/profile'
The URL this page owns — where open() goes.
rootIndicator = this.heading
The "My profile" H1 that proves the page rendered.
open()
Goes to /profile and waits for that heading.
getDetails()
Returns name, email and role as a plain object.
expectRole('ADMIN')
Asserts the role shown on screen matches.
header.userName
Shared header component; sidebar is available too.

Showing the 6 you will use most — the class has 10 members in total.

TipFields render an em dash until the API answers. getDetails() waits that out, so use it rather than reading the locators directly.

Chapter

Components

Parts of a screen that show up in more than one place. Each only looks inside its own box.

07

TableComponent

src/components/TableComponent.ts · 218 lines

Reads and asserts on a table by column name instead of cell position.

A wrapper around one table on the page. You ask for rows and cells by header text, and it finds them for you. It is scoped to a root locator (by default the element with test id `employee-table`), so it only ever looks inside that one table — another table on the same screen is invisible to it.

Why it existsSo no page object has to rewrite row counting, cell reading, sorting and empty-state checks.

How you use itsrc/pages/EmployeePage.ts and tests/ui/regression/employee-management.regression.spec.ts
// how the page builds it (src/pages/EmployeePage.ts)
this.table = new TableComponent(page, {
  testId: 'employee-table',
  rowTestId: 'employee-row',
  emptyState: this.emptyState,
});

// how a test uses it (employee-management.regression.spec.ts)
await employeesAs.searchFor(created.email);
await employeesAs.table.expectRowMatching({
  Name: created.name,
  Designation: 'Principal SDET',
  Department: 'Engineering',
});
table.rows
Locator for every body row. Pair it with toHaveCount().
await table.getRowCount()
How many rows are showing right now.
await table.expectRowMatching({ Name: 'Asha' })
Fails unless some row matches your header-to-value object.
await table.getColumnValues('Department')
Every value in one column, top to bottom.
await table.getCell(0, 'Email')
Text of one cell, picked by row number and column name.
table.rowByText('Asha Rao')
Locator for the first row containing that text.
await table.clickRowAction('Asha Rao', 'Edit')
Clicks a named button inside the matching row.
await table.sortByColumn('Name')
Clicks the header; returns 'ascending' or 'descending'.

Showing the 8 you will use most — the class has 24 members in total.

TipexpectRowMatching matches on substrings, so 'Ann' will pass against a row holding 'Anna'. Assert with the full value when you need an exact match.

08

PaginationComponent

src/components/PaginationComponent.ts · 103 lines

Moves between pages, changes page size, and reads the summary as numbers.

The pager under a table. Its root is the `.pagination` box, so its Previous, Next and page-size controls are always the ones belonging to that pager. getState() turns "Page 2 of 4 - 37 employees" into { page: 2, totalPages: 4, totalRecords: 37 }.

Why it existsPaging is click-then-wait; these methods wait for the summary line to change so your test does not race the UI.

How you use ittests/ui/regression/employee-management.regression.spec.ts
// tests/ui/regression/employee-management.regression.spec.ts
await employeesAs.pagination.setPageSize(data.pagination.smallPageSize);
const state = await employeesAs.pagination.getState();
expect(state.page).toBe(1);
expect(await employeesAs.pagination.isFirstPage()).toBe(true);

await employeesAs.pagination.goToNextPage();
expect((await employeesAs.pagination.getState()).page).toBe(2);
await employeesAs.pagination.goToPreviousPage();
await pagination.getState()
Returns { page, totalPages, totalRecords } read from the summary.
await pagination.goToNextPage()
Clicks Next and waits for the page number to go up.
await pagination.goToPreviousPage()
Clicks Previous and waits for the page number to go down.
await pagination.goToPage(3)
Steps forward or back until that page is shown.
await pagination.setPageSize(5)
Picks rows-per-page and waits for page 1.
await pagination.isFirstPage()
True when the Previous button is disabled.
await pagination.isLastPage()
True when the Next button is disabled.

Showing the 7 you will use most — the class has 11 members in total.

TipgetState() only understands summaries shaped like "Page 2 of 4 - 37 employees". If the app reworded that line, getState() throws rather than returning wrong numbers - fix the regex, not the test.

09

DatePickerComponent

src/components/DatePickerComponent.ts · 99 lines

The calendar widget — picks a date by its ISO string.

A wrapper around the custom calendar: a text input, a trigger button, and a popup with month, year, and day controls.

Why it existsPicking a date means opening a popup and changing two dropdowns before clicking a day — one method hides all of that.

How you use itsrc/pages/EmployeePage.ts
// src/pages/EmployeePage.ts
this.joiningDatePicker = new DatePickerComponent(page);

// inside fillEmployeeForm:
if (input.joiningDate !== undefined)
  await this.joiningDatePicker.selectDate(input.joiningDate);

// tests/ui/regression/employee-management.regression.spec.ts
const employee = buildEmployee({ overrides: { joiningDate: '2023-07-14' } });
await employeesAs.createEmployee({ ...employee, active: true });
selectDate('2023-07-14')
Opens the calendar, picks that date, checks the input.
selectToday()
Picks today and returns it as an ISO string.
selectMonthAndYear('July', 2023)
Moves the calendar to a month and year, picks no day.
selectRange(endPicker, startIso, endIso)
Fills a start and an end picker as one range.
getValue()
Reads the date currently sitting in the input.
clear()
Empties the input and fires a change event.
open()
Shows the popup. selectDate already does this for you.

Showing the 7 you will use most — the class has 22 members in total.

TipDates must be ISO 'YYYY-MM-DD' — the day button is found by that exact string, so '7/14/2023' will never match.

10

SidebarComponent

src/components/SidebarComponent.ts · 92 lines

The left nav rail — clicks links and opens the mobile menu for you.

A wrapper around the primary navigation. On narrow screens the rail hides behind a menu button, and this class opens it before doing anything.

Why it existsSo one spec runs unchanged on desktop, tablet, and mobile — the component absorbs the layout difference, not the test.

How you use ittests/ui/sanity/dashboard.sanity.spec.ts
// tests/ui/sanity/dashboard.sanity.spec.ts
for (const item of data.navigationItems) {
  await dashboardAs.open();
  await dashboardAs.sidebar.navigateTo(item.label);
  await expect(dashboardAs.rawPage).toHaveURL(new RegExp(`${item.path}$`));
  await dashboardAs.sidebar.expectActiveItem(item.label);
}
navigateTo('Employees')
Opens the menu if needed, clicks the link, waits for the page.
ensureVisible()
Opens the collapsed drawer. Safe to call any number of times.
expectActiveItem('Employees')
Asserts which nav item is highlighted as the current page.
getActiveItem()
Returns the label of the highlighted nav item.
getItemLabels()
Returns the text of every nav link.
expectAvailable()
Asserts nav is reachable, inline or behind the menu button.
link('Profile')
Locator for one nav link, matched by exact text.

Showing the 7 you will use most — the class has 18 members in total.

TipDo not click menuToggle yourself — navigateTo, getItemLabels, and getActiveItem all call ensureVisible() first, so clicking it again can close the drawer you just opened.

11

ModalComponent

src/components/ModalComponent.ts · 85 lines

Wraps one dialog so you can read it, click its buttons, and close it.

One dialog box on the page, found by its role="dialog" or by a test id you pass in. Everything it looks for — the title, the close button, the error line — is searched only inside that dialog, never in the page behind it.

Why it existsEvery modal in the app opens, closes and shows errors the same way, so that logic is written once.

How you use itsrc/pages/EmployeePage.ts
// src/pages/EmployeePage.ts
this.confirmModal = new ModalComponent(page, { root: page.getByTestId('confirm-modal') });

public async deleteEmployee(employeeName: string): Promise<void> {
  await this.table.clickRowAction(employeeName, 'Delete');
  await this.confirmModal.expectOpen();
  await this.confirmModal.root.getByTestId('confirm-accept').click();
  await this.confirmModal.expectClosed();
}
new ModalComponent(page, { root: page.getByTestId('employee-modal') })
Point it at one dialog; without options it uses role="dialog".
await modal.expectOpen()
Waits until the dialog is visible, or fails.
await modal.expectClosed()
Waits until the dialog is gone, or fails.
expect(modal.title).toHaveText('Add employee')
Locator for the dialog's heading.
await modal.clickButton('Save')
Clicks a button in the dialog by its visible name.
await modal.cancel()
Clicks Cancel and waits for the dialog to close.
await modal.close()
Clicks the X and waits for the dialog to close.
await modal.getErrorMessage()
The inline validation text, or null when there is none.

Showing the 8 you will use most — the class has 12 members in total.

TipIf a screen can render two dialogs, a bare `new ModalComponent(page)` matches both and Playwright throws a strict-mode error. Pass a `root` or a `name`, as EmployeePage does for its form and confirm dialogs.

SearchComponent

src/components/SearchComponent.ts · 79 lines

The search box and department filter — types, filters, and waits for results.

A wrapper around the filter bar at the top of the employee list. It owns the search input, the department dropdown, and the clear button.

Why it existsThe app's search is debounced, so tests need to wait for the results request instead of guessing a sleep time.

How you use itsrc/pages/EmployeePage.ts
// src/pages/EmployeePage.ts
this.search = new SearchComponent(page);

await this.search.search(term);              // fills the box, waits for GET /employees?
await this.search.filterByDepartment(department);
await this.search.clearFilters();            // also asserts the box is empty
search(term)
Types the term, waits for the results request to finish.
filterByDepartment('Engineering')
Picks a department, waits for the list to reload.
clearFilters()
Clicks clear and checks the box is empty again.
getSearchTerm()
Reads what is currently typed in the search box.
getAvailableDepartments()
Returns every option label in the department dropdown.
input
Raw locator for the search box, for your own asserts.

Showing the 6 you will use most — the class has 16 members in total.

TipNever add a sleep after search() — it already waits for the network. If your screen calls a different URL, pass requestFragment in the constructor options or the wait will time out.

13

ToastComponent

src/components/ToastComponent.ts · 65 lines

Waits for pop-up notifications and checks their text without any sleeps.

The toast area of the app. Its root is the `#toastRegion` box, so it only sees toasts rendered there — page text that happens to say "Saved" will never fool it.

Why it existsToasts appear late and vanish on a timer, so these assertions retry instead of you guessing a wait time.

How you use ittests/ui/regression/employee-management.regression.spec.ts
// tests/ui/regression/employee-management.regression.spec.ts
await test.step('Confirming removes it from the directory', async () => {
  await employeesAs.deleteEmployee(created.name);
  await employeesAs.toast.expectSuccess('Employee deleted');
  await employeesAs.expectEmployeeAbsent(created.name);
});

// the failure case, same file
await employeesAs.toast.expectError('Save failed');
await toast.expectSuccess('Employee created')
Fails unless a success toast with that text appears.
await toast.expectError('Save failed')
Fails unless an error toast with that text appears.
await toast.waitForMessage('Reset cancelled')
Waits for a toast with that text and returns its full text.
toast.latest
Locator for the most recent toast.
toast.byVariant('warning')
Locator for all toasts of one kind.
await toast.getVisibleMessages()
Text of every toast on screen right now.
await toast.waitUntilCleared()
Waits until no toasts remain. Do this before a screenshot.

Showing the 7 you will use most — the class has 8 members in total.

TipgetVisibleMessages() reads whatever is on screen at that instant and does not wait, so calling it straight after a click often returns an empty array. Use waitForMessage() or expectSuccess() to wait.

Chapter

Talking to the API

Tests that skip the browser and call the server directly — for fast setup, and for testing the API itself.

15

ApiClient

src/api/clients/ApiClient.ts · 296 lines

One HTTP client for every API call: URL, headers, auth, retries, parsing.

A thin wrapper around Playwright's request context. You call get/post/put/patch/delete with a path and options, and get back a parsed response object with status, data, error and durationMs.

Why it existsSo no test ever hand-builds a URL, header or Authorization token.

How you use ittests/api/regression/employee-negative.api.spec.ts
test('An invalid token is rejected', async ({ apiClient }) => {
  const response = await apiClient
    .withToken('tkn_not-a-real-session-token')
    .get(API_ROUTES.employees.root);

  verify(response).hasStatus(HTTP_STATUS.UNAUTHORIZED).isFailure(API_ERROR_CODES.unauthorized);
});
get(path, { query, pathParams, skipAuth })
Sends a GET. Options fill :id placeholders and query strings.
post(path, { body })
Sends a POST with a JSON body.
patch(path, { body })
Sends a PATCH. put and delete work the same way.
delete(path, { pathParams })
Sends a DELETE; a 204 comes back as an empty success.
setAuthToken(token)
Adds Bearer token to every later call. Never logged.
clearAuthToken()
Forgets the token, so later calls go out unauthenticated.
withToken(token)
Returns a copy signed in as someone else.
client.isAuthenticated
True when a token is currently set.

Showing the 8 you will use most — the class has 10 members in total.

TipwithToken() returns a NEW client - the shared one keeps its old token, which is exactly what you want in role tests.

16

ResponseValidator

src/api/validators/ResponseValidator.ts · 210 lines

Chain readable assertions on one API response, then unwrap the data.

You never write new ResponseValidator(). You call verify(response) and chain checks - every method returns this, so they read like a sentence. Each failure message names the endpoint and prints the body.

Why it existsSo one failed assertion tells you which call broke and why.

How you use ittests/api/smoke/platform.api.spec.ts
const response = await authApi.health();

verify(response)
  .hasStatus(HTTP_STATUS.OK)
  .isJson()
  .isSuccessful()
  .matchesSchema(healthSchema)
  .respondedWithin(budgets.maxResponseTimeMs)
  .hasProperty('status', 'UP');
hasStatus(200)
Checks the HTTP status code.
isSuccessful()
Checks it is a 2xx and the envelope says success.
isFailure('NOT_FOUND')
Checks it is an error envelope, optionally with that code.
hasProperty('user.role', 'ADMIN')
Checks a field on data. Dot paths work.
isArray({ minLength: 1 })
Checks data is an array of the right size.
matchesSchema(employeeSchema)
Checks the shape of data against a JSON schema.
respondedWithin(1500)
Fails if the call took longer than that many milliseconds.
unwrap()
Ends the chain and returns the typed data.

Showing the 8 you will use most — the class has 19 members in total.

TipAwait the request first - verify() takes a finished response, not a promise. Put unwrap() last when you need the data afterwards.

17

EmployeeApi

src/api/services/EmployeeApi.ts · 128 lines

Employee CRUD plus the setup and cleanup helpers tests lean on.

Two kinds of methods live here. Plain CRUD (list, create, update, remove) that returns a response you assert on, and lifecycle helpers (createOrThrow, deleteIfExists) built for test setup and teardown.

Why it existsSo specs seed and clean up data fast, without touching the UI.

How you use ittests/api/regression/employee-crud.api.spec.ts
const created = await adminEmployeeApi.createOrThrow(buildEmployee());
cleanup.employee(created.id);

const response = await adminEmployeeApi.update(created.id, {
  salary: 1_999_000,
  status: 'INACTIVE',
});

verify(response)
  .hasStatus(HTTP_STATUS.OK)
  .isSuccessful()
  .hasProperty('status', 'INACTIVE');
list({ search, department, page, pageSize })
Lists employees with search, filter, sort and paging.
getById(id)
Fetches one employee.
create(payload)
Creates one; returns the response so you can assert failures.
createOrThrow(payload)
Creates one for setup; throws loudly if the API refuses.
createMany(payloads)
Creates several in order; returns the created records.
update(id, { salary })
PATCHes some fields. replace() does a full PUT.
deleteIfExists(id)
Teardown-safe delete; an already-gone record is not an error.
waitUntilSearchable(email)
Polls the list until a new record shows up.

Showing the 8 you will use most — the class has 13 members in total.

TipUse create() when the failure IS the test, and createOrThrow() for setup - a broken precondition should not surface later as a confusing assertion failure.

18

AuthApi

src/api/services/AuthApi.ts · 70 lines

Log in, check who you are, log out, and ping the health endpoint.

The service for everything about sessions. Its most-used method signs in as a role and hands the token to the client so later calls are authenticated.

Why it existsSo tests say "log in as ADMIN" instead of posting credentials themselves.

How you use ittests/api/smoke/platform.api.spec.ts
test('The token identifies the caller', async ({ authApi }) => {
  await authApi.authenticateClientAs('ADMIN');
  const me = await authApi.me();

  verify(me).hasStatus(HTTP_STATUS.OK).isSuccessful().hasProperty('role', 'ADMIN');
});
authenticateClientAs('ADMIN')
Logs in as a role and stores the token on the client.
loginAs('EMPLOYEE')
Same login, but returns the session without storing the token.
login({ username, password })
Raw login. Returns the response instead of throwing.
me()
Who does the current token belong to?
logout()
Ends the session and clears the stored token.
health()
Is the environment up? Runs without any token.

TipUse login() when you expect failure (it returns a 401 response) and loginAs()/authenticateClientAs() when you expect success (they throw if login fails).

19

UserApi

src/api/services/UserApi.ts · 21 lines

Read-only lookups for the user directory and department list.

A three-method service over the users endpoints. Mostly used to check that non-admins are refused, and to look up a user by email.

Why it existsEmployees and users are different things; this covers the user side.

How you use ittests/api/regression/employee-negative.api.spec.ts
test('Listing users requires ADMIN', async ({ authApi, userApi }) => {
  await authApi.authenticateClientAs('EMPLOYEE');

  verify(await userApi.list())
    .hasStatus(HTTP_STATUS.FORBIDDEN)
    .isFailure(API_ERROR_CODES.forbidden);
});
list()
All users. ADMIN only - other roles get 403.
findByEmail(email)
One user by email, or undefined. Case-insensitive.
departments()
The list of department names.

TipfindByEmail fetches the whole list and filters in memory, so do not call it in a loop.

20

BaseApiService

src/api/services/BaseApiService.ts · 19 lines

The 19-line parent every API service extends: a client plus a logger.

An abstract class that stores the ApiClient you pass in as this.client and makes a logger named after your subclass. That is all it does.

Why it existsSo each service can focus on its endpoints instead of plumbing.

How you use itsrc/api/services/UserApi.ts
export class UserApi extends BaseApiService {
  public async list(): Promise<ApiResponse<AuthenticatedUser[]>> {
    return this.client.get<AuthenticatedUser[]>(API_ROUTES.users.list);
  }

  public async departments(): Promise<ApiResponse<string[]>> {
    return this.client.get<string[]>(API_ROUTES.departments);
  }
}
new MyApi(client)
Hand it the ApiClient the service should call through.
this.client.get(path)
The client, for use inside your service methods.
this.log.info('created', { id })
Logger already tagged with your class name.
service.apiClient
Public access to the client, for tests sharing a token.

TipA service is only as logged-in as the client you gave it - that is why the fixtures ship both employeeApi (anonymous) and adminEmployeeApi.

Chapter

Errors and logging

When something breaks, these decide what you get told.

21

Logger

src/utils/Logger.ts · 71 lines

Prints timestamped, scoped log lines and hides secrets automatically.

One line per event: time, level, scope, message, JSON payload. Goes to the console and to logs/run-<id>.log.

Why it existsSo you can read the story of a failed run instead of scattering console.log calls.

How you use itsrc/pages/LoginPage.ts
// src/pages/BasePage.ts - every page object builds its own scoped logger
this.log = createLogger(new.target.name);

// src/pages/LoginPage.ts
this.log.info('signing in', { role, environment: this.environment.name });

// 2026-05-01T09:12:44.301Z | INFO  | LoginPage | signing in {"role":"admin","environment":"qa"}
log.info(message, payload?)
normal progress, one line per meaningful event
log.debug(message, payload?)
detail you only want when digging in
log.warn(message, payload?)
something odd but the run continues
log.error(message, payload?)
something failed; goes to stderr
log.action('click', 'Submit button')
logs an 'action -> target' line at debug level
await log.step('save employee', fn)
times an async block and logs the duration
log.child({ test: title })
same logger, scope narrowed further
createLogger('EmployeePage')
factory for a logger named after your module

TipLocally the level is DEBUG, in CI it is INFO - set LOG_LEVEL=DEBUG to see debug lines in CI.

22

SoftAssertions

src/utils/AssertionUtils.ts · 27 lines

Collects several failed checks and fails the test once, at the end.

A small collector. Each failed check is stored as a message; assertAll then fails with the whole list.

Why it existsSo one report shows every broken expectation instead of stopping at the first.

How you use itsrc/utils/AssertionUtils.ts
// src/utils/AssertionUtils.ts
public check(condition: boolean, message: string): void {
  if (!condition) this.failures.push(message);
}

public assertAll(label = 'Soft assertions'): void {
  expect(
    this.failures,
    `${label} recorded ${this.failures.length} failure(s):\n  ${this.failures.join('\n  ')}`,
  ).toEqual([]);
}
soft.check(rows > 0, 'table was empty')
records a message when the condition is false
await soft.checkAsync(() => assertVisible(x), 'no badge')
runs a normal assertion, catches its failure instead
soft.failureCount
how many checks have failed so far
soft.assertAll('employee row')
fails the test with every collected message

TipNothing fails until you call assertAll - forget it and a broken test passes green.

23

FrameworkError

src/utils/FrameworkError.ts · 20 lines

The base error for every framework failure: a message plus readable context.

An Error that prints a labelled context block under the message. Every other framework error extends it.

Why it existsSo a failure tells you what was happening when it broke, not just that it broke.

How you use itsrc/utils/FileUtils.ts
// src/utils/FileUtils.ts
throw new FrameworkError(
  'Unable to create directory',
  { operation: 'ensureDirectory', target: directory },
  error,
);

// what the test report shows:
// FrameworkError: Unable to create directory
//   operation: ensureDirectory
//   target: reports/extent
//   cause: EACCES: permission denied, mkdir 'reports/extent'
new FrameworkError(message, context, cause?)
message, a context object, and the original error
err.context.target
the context object, still readable in code
err.message
your message plus one indented line per context key
err.name
the subclass name, e.g. UiActionError
err.cause
the original error, kept when you pass one

TipAlways pass the original error as the third argument, or you lose the real cause.

24

EnvironmentConfigurationError

config/environment.config.ts · 6 lines

Thrown when the environment is misconfigured: bad TEST_ENV, missing file, missing credentials.

A plain Error subclass used only while resolving an environment. It is not part of the FrameworkError family.

Why it existsConfig problems should stop the run immediately with a fix-it message, not halfway through a test.

How you use itconfig/environment.config.ts
// config/environment.config.ts
export function resolveEnvironmentName(raw = process.env.TEST_ENV): EnvironmentName {
  const candidate = (raw ?? 'dev').trim().toLowerCase();
  if (!VALID_ENVIRONMENTS.includes(candidate as EnvironmentName)) {
    throw new EnvironmentConfigurationError(
      `Unknown TEST_ENV "${raw ?? ''}". Expected one of: ${VALID_ENVIRONMENTS.join(', ')}.`,
    );
  }
  return candidate as EnvironmentName;
}
new EnvironmentConfigurationError(message)
message only, no context object
err.name
always 'EnvironmentConfigurationError'

TipMissing logins raise this too: set the username and password env vars named in config/environments/<env>.json.

25

UiActionError

src/utils/FrameworkError.ts · 1 lines

Thrown when a click, fill or wait on the page fails.

A FrameworkError for UI failures. Page objects and components wrap every action and throw this.

Why it existsA raw Playwright timeout does not say which page object or element gave up.

How you use itsrc/components/TableComponent.ts
UiActionError: Column not found
  operation: getColumnIndex
  target: Salary
  page: TableComponent
  url: http://localhost:3100/employees
  actual: available columns: Name, Email, Department
new UiActionError(message, context, cause?)
inherited unchanged from FrameworkError
err.context.url
page, element and URL captured at failure time
err.name
always 'UiActionError', handy inside a catch

TipYou rarely throw this yourself: BasePage.perform already wraps your actions and throws it.

26

ApiRequestError

src/utils/FrameworkError.ts · 1 lines

Thrown when an HTTP call fails, times out, or returns an unreadable body.

A FrameworkError for API failures, thrown by ApiClient and the API services.

Why it existsTies a broken request to its method, URL, environment and number of attempts.

How you use itsrc/api/services/AuthApi.ts
ApiRequestError: API login failed
  operation: loginAs
  target: admin
  environment: qa
  expected: HTTP 200 with a token
  actual: HTTP 401 INVALID_CREDENTIALS
new ApiRequestError(message, context, cause?)
inherited unchanged from FrameworkError
err.context.attempts
method, URL, timeout and retry count
err.name
always 'ApiRequestError'

TipA failing status usually comes back as a normal response: check it with assertStatus, do not expect a throw.

27

TestDataError

src/utils/FrameworkError.ts · 1 lines

Thrown when a JSON test dataset is missing, unreadable, or missing keys.

A FrameworkError raised by JsonReader and the data factories when test data will not load.

Why it existsPoints you at the exact file it looked for and what it found instead.

How you use itsrc/utils/JsonReader.ts
TestDataError: Test dataset not found
  operation: resolveDataset
  target: employees
  expected: test-data/common/employees.json
  available: logins, departments
new TestDataError(message, context, cause?)
inherited unchanged from FrameworkError
err.context.expected
the file path it wanted, plus what exists
err.name
always 'TestDataError'

TipRead the 'available' line first: the answer is usually a typo in the dataset name.

28

ValidationError

src/utils/FrameworkError.ts · 1 lines

Thrown when data breaks its contract: bad schema, or a response with no payload.

A FrameworkError raised by the schema validator and a few assertion helpers.

Why it existsStops code from working on a payload that is not the shape it promised.

How you use itsrc/api/validators/SchemaValidator.ts
ValidationError: Payload failed schema validation
  operation: ensureSchema
  target: EmployeeResponse
  actual: email: must match format "email"
new ValidationError(message, context, cause?)
inherited unchanged from FrameworkError
err.context.actual
every schema violation, listed in one string
err.name
always 'ValidationError'

TipIn a test use assertSchema (fails the test); in a service use ensureSchema (throws this).

Chapter

The report

Playwright calls this class as tests run. It collects results and writes the HTML report.

29

ExtentReporter

src/reporting/ExtentReporter.ts · 335 lines

Playwright calls these hooks as tests run; we collect results and write an HTML report.

A Playwright reporter. Playwright calls onBegin, onTestEnd and onEnd while the suite runs, and this class saves each result. At the end it writes index.html, report.json and a latest.html shortcut.

Why it existsSo every run leaves one shareable folder with results, screenshots, videos and traces inside it.

How you use itplaywright.config.ts
reporter: [
  ['list', { printSteps: false }],
  ['html', { outputFolder: PATHS.playwrightReport, open: 'never' }],
  ['json', { outputFile: `${PATHS.jsonReport}/results.json` }],
  ['junit', { outputFile: `${PATHS.junitReport}/results.xml` }],
  ...(frameworkConfig.extentEnabled ? [['./src/reporting/ExtentReporter.ts'] as [string]] : []),
],
new ExtentReporter()
Picks a timestamped folder under reports/extent/ for this run.
onBegin(config, suite)
Run starts: save the config, create the attachments folder.
onTestEnd(test, result)
One test finished: turn it into a report row.
await onEnd(result)
Run over: count totals, write the HTML and JSON.

TipA run that executed nothing (typo in --project, --list) leaves latest.html showing the previous run — check its date before trusting the numbers.

Chapter

Sending results elsewhere

Optional. Set the right environment variables and results also go to Slack, Jira, Zephyr or Sauce Labs.

30

JiraNotifier

src/integrations/jira/JiraNotifier.ts · 497 lines

Comments on the Jira issues your failing tests tag, once per issue.

Groups a run's failures by the @PROJ-123 keys in test titles and posts one comment per issue. Same contract as every integration: isEnabled() / disabledReason() / publish().

Why it existsSo a red run updates the tickets people are already watching.

How you use itsrc/reporting/ExtentReporter.ts (tag example from README.md)
// A test names its issue in its own title:
test('Checkout rejects an expired card @PROJ-123 @regression', async () => { /* … */ });

// src/reporting/ExtentReporter.ts — the reporter publishes once the run is done
const integrations = await publishIntegrations({
  model: { summary, environment, tests },
  reportDir: this.reportDir,
  ...(process.env.REPORT_URL ? { reportUrl: process.env.REPORT_URL } : {}),
});
notifier.name
'Jira' — the row label in the report
isEnabled()
Needs JIRA_ENABLED=true plus all four credential variables
disabledReason()
Names the exact variable that is missing
await publish({ model, reportDir })
Comments, then returns published, skipped or failed
new JiraNotifier(fakeEnv)
Pass your own env object to test it

TipLeave JIRA_CREATE_ISSUE_ON_FAILURE off on per-commit runs — a recurring failure files a fresh bug every build.

31

JiraClient

src/integrations/jira/JiraClient.ts · 434 lines

A tiny Jira REST client: comment on an issue, create one, check credentials.

Three calls against Jira Cloud's REST API v3. It handles the auth header, per-call timeouts and turning Jira's error bodies into one readable line.

Why it existsSo the notifier can write to Jira without hand-rolling fetch, auth and error text.

How you use itsrc/integrations/jira/JiraNotifier.ts
const client = new JiraClient({
  baseUrl: settings.baseUrl,
  email: settings.email,
  apiToken: settings.apiToken,
  timeoutMs: PER_CALL_TIMEOUT_MS,
});

await client.verifyCredentials(remainingMs());
await client.addComment(issueKey, adfDocument(commentLines(issueKey, tests, context)), remainingMs());
new JiraClient({ baseUrl, email, apiToken })
Builds the auth header once; add cloudId for scoped tokens
await client.verifyCredentials()
Checks the token works before any write
await client.addComment('QA-12', adfDocument(lines))
Adds one comment; the body must be ADF
await client.createIssue({ project, issuetype, summary })
Files a new issue and returns its key
client.browseUrl('QA-12')
Builds the human link to an issue
adfDocument(['first line', 'second line'])
Helper: turns plain lines into Jira's rich-text format

TipComment and issue bodies must be ADF — a plain string there is the 400 you will hit first.

32

SlackNotifier

src/integrations/slack/SlackNotifier.ts · 342 lines

Posts one Slack message per test run, only when SLACK_WEBHOOK_URL is set.

Sends a run summary to a Slack channel through an incoming webhook — one message per run, never one per failing test. Like every integration it answers three things: isEnabled() (is it configured?), disabledReason() (why not), publish() (do the work).

Why it existsSo the team hears the suite went red without opening the report.

How you use itsrc/integrations/index.ts
// src/integrations/index.ts — how the reporter runs every notifier
const FACTORIES = [() => new SlackNotifier(), () => new JiraNotifier()];

for (const integration of instantiate()) {
  if (!integration.isEnabled()) {
    results.push(skipped(integration.name, integration.disabledReason()));
    continue;
  }
  results.push(await integration.publish(context));
}
notifier.name
The label 'Slack' used in logs and the report
isEnabled()
True only when SLACK_WEBHOOK_URL is set and not blank
disabledReason()
One line saying why nothing was posted
await publish({ model, reportDir })
Posts the summary and returns a result; never throws
new SlackNotifier({ notifyOn: 'always' })
Override the env vars: webhookUrl, notifyOn, reportUrl, timeoutMs

TipGreen runs stay quiet by default; the code reads SLACK_NOTIFY_ON=always (not the README's SLACK_NOTIFY).

33

ZephyrNotifier

src/integrations/zephyr/ZephyrNotifier.ts · 285 lines

Turns a finished run into Zephyr executions, one per tagged test.

The Zephyr end of the reporter. It reads @PROJ-T123 tags off your tests, creates a cycle for the run, then posts one execution per key.

Why it existsSo results land in Zephyr automatically instead of someone copying statuses across by hand.

How you use itsrc/integrations/index.ts
const integration = new ZephyrNotifier();

if (!integration.isEnabled()) {
  results.push(skipped(integration.name, integration.disabledReason()));
} else {
  results.push(await integration.publish(context));
}
// every path returns a row: published | skipped | failed. publish() never throws.
notifier.name
Always "Zephyr Scale"; shown in logs and the report.
isEnabled()
True only when the flag, token and project key are all set.
disabledReason()
One line naming the env vars that are missing.
publish(context)
Sends every tagged test's result; returns a row, never throws.
new ZephyrNotifier({ env, logger })
Both optional — inject env so a test can drive it.

TipTag your test @PROJ-T42 or it is skipped. A key is never guessed, because a wrong one writes onto someone else's test case.

34

SauceNotifier

src/integrations/sauce/SauceNotifier.ts · 284 lines

Finds this run's Sauce Labs jobs and links the newest in the report.

A read-only Sauce integration. It searches your account's recent jobs for the one stamped with SAUCE_BUILD_NAME and puts a link to the newest match in the report.

Why it existsSo the report can point at the Sauce jobs that produced it, without changing anything on Sauce.

How you use itsrc/integrations/sauce/SauceNotifier.ts
const build = sauceBuildName();
if (build === undefined) {
  return this.result(
    'skipped',
    'SAUCE_BUILD_NAME is not set, so this run cannot be told apart from other jobs.',
    startedAt,
  );
}
return await this.linkBuild(context, credentials, region, build, startedAt);
notifier.name
Always "Sauce Labs".
isEnabled()
True when username, access key and a valid region are set.
disabledReason()
Says which piece of Sauce config is missing or wrong.
publish(context)
Looks up the jobs and returns a row with a job link.

TipSet SAUCE_BUILD_NAME and pass the same value to `saucectl run --build` — without it the lookup is skipped rather than guessing at recent jobs.

35

ZephyrClient

src/integrations/zephyr/ZephyrClient.ts · 215 lines

Thin REST wrapper over the three Zephyr Scale calls a finished run needs.

A small typed wrapper around fetch for Zephyr Scale Cloud. It creates a test cycle, posts one execution per test, and lists the status names a project accepts.

Why it existsKeeps the API token, timeouts and error handling in one place instead of scattered fetch calls.

How you use itsrc/integrations/zephyr/ZephyrNotifier.ts
const client = new ZephyrClient({ token: settings.token, baseUrl: settings.baseUrl });

const created = await client.createTestCycle({
  projectKey: settings.projectKey,
  name,
  description,
});

await client.createTestExecution(toExecutionInput(target, settings, created.key));
new ZephyrClient({ token, baseUrl })
Holds the token; rejects a non-https base URL right away.
createTestCycle(input)
Makes the run's cycle and returns its QA-R42 key.
createTestExecution(input)
Records one test's result into that cycle.
listExecutionStatuses(projectKey)
Lists the status names this project accepts, like Pass or Fail.

TipNever re-send an execution. POST /testexecutions appends a row, so a retry doubles the result with no undo.

36

ZephyrApiError

src/integrations/zephyr/ZephyrClient.ts · 11 lines

The one error type every ZephyrClient call throws when something goes wrong.

An Error subclass that also carries the failed endpoint and an HTTP status. Every failure from ZephyrClient — network, HTTP, or bad JSON — arrives in this same shape.

Why it existsSo callers handle one error type instead of telling fetch, parse and HTTP failures apart themselves.

How you use itsrc/integrations/zephyr/ZephyrClient.ts
// nothing reached Zephyr -> status 0
throw new ZephyrApiError(`no complete response within ${this.timeoutMs}ms`, endpoint, 0, error);

// Zephyr answered with an error -> the status is theirs
if (!ok) throw new ZephyrApiError(describeHttpFailure(status, text), endpoint, status);

// err.message reads: "POST /testexecutions: HTTP 404 - project, cycle or test case not found"
err.status
HTTP code, or 0 when the request never left the process.
err.endpoint
Which call failed, e.g. "POST /testexecutions".
err.name
Always "ZephyrApiError" — how you spot it in a catch.
new ZephyrApiError(message, endpoint, status, cause?)
Prefixes the message with the endpoint so logs say where.

Tipstatus === 0 means your side broke — bad config, timeout, unreachable host. Any other number came from Zephyr.

37

JiraApiError

src/integrations/jira/JiraClient.ts · 10 lines

The error JiraClient throws when a Jira call fails, carrying the HTTP status.

A plain Error with one extra field: status. Its message is written to fit on one line of a report.

Why it existsSo a caller can tell a rejected token (401) from a network failure (0).

How you use itsrc/integrations/jira/JiraNotifier.ts
try {
  await client.verifyCredentials(remainingMs());
} catch (error) {
  const rejected = error instanceof JiraApiError && error.status === 401;
  return {
    status: 'failed',
    detail: rejected
      ? `Jira credentials were rejected: ${describe(error)}`
      : `Jira credential check failed: ${describe(error)}`,
  };
}
error.status
HTTP code, or 0 when no response arrived
error.message
One line: status, hint, and Jira's own error text
error.name
Always the string 'JiraApiError'
error instanceof JiraApiError
Narrow an unknown catch before reading status

Tipstatus 0 means the request got no answer at all — the write may still have gone through.

Handbook

Quick start

Four commands from a fresh clone to a passing suite and an open report. The framework ships its own application to test, so nothing external needs to exist.

npm ci
Installs dependencies. Node 20 or newer; the project is ESM.
npm run prepare:browsers
Downloads the browser builds this Playwright version pins. npm ci alone is not enough.
npm test
Runs the api and chromium projects — 60 tests, about 35 seconds.
npm run report:open
Opens the report for the run that just finished.
What you should see. The reference app starts on port 4321, global setup signs in as three roles and caches their sessions, then 60 tests run in parallel.

No .env is needed for dev — it is the only environment with allowInsecureDefaults on, so the sandbox credentials are used when the variables are absent. Every other environment refuses to guess and names the two variables it wants.

Handbook

Running tests

Three dimensions compose freely: which project (where it runs), which tag (what kind of test), and which environment (what it targets).

By scope

npm test
npm run test:api
Browserless, 29 tests.
npm run test:full
All nine projects, 249 tests.

By tag

npm run test:smoke
npm run test:regression
npm run test:critical

By environment

npm run test:qa
npm run test:prod
Production is smoke-only and read-only.

By browser

npm run test:firefox
npm run test:mobile

Narrowing down

npx playwright test tests/ui/smoke/login.smoke.spec.ts
npx playwright test --grep "An administrator can sign in"
npx playwright test --last-failed
Watch out for test:headed. It is --headed --grep @e2e, so it runs only the end-to-end test. To watch anything else, pass --headed yourself.

Debugging

npm run test:ui-mode
Playwright UI mode — the best way to explore a failure.
npm run test:debug
Handbook

Writing tests

Every spec has the same shape: one import, a describe block, an optional role, and tests that read as business intent.

The rules

  • Import only from @fixtures/index.
  • Put tags in the title — they drive --grep and the report.
  • Declare the persona with test.use({ role }).
  • Register anything you create with cleanup.employee(id).
  • No locators, no HTTP, no waitForTimeout.

Choosing fixtures

  • loginPage — a plain page; you drive the login.
  • dashboardAs / employeesAs — already signed in.
  • adminEmployeeApi — authenticated setup and teardown.
  • employeeApi — the unauthenticated client, for 401 tests.

The assertion chain

Every check returns this so it chains, and every failure names the endpoint. unwrap() ends the chain and hands back the typed payload.

verify(): entry point2
NameSignatureWhat it does
verify export function verify<T>(response: ApiResponse<T>): ResponseValidator<T> Starts an assertion chain over a response — the way every API assertion begins.→ ResponseValidator<T>
ResponseValidator constructor(response: ApiResponse<T>) The chainable validator class; normally reached through verify() rather than constructed directly.→ ResponseValidator<T>
verify(): status and envelope6
NameSignatureWhat it does
hasStatus public hasStatus(expected: number): this Asserts an exact HTTP status, printing a payload preview when it differs.→ this
hasStatusIn public hasStatusIn(expected: readonly number[]): this Asserts the status is one of several acceptable codes.→ this
isSuccessful public isSuccessful(): this Asserts both a 2xx status and `success: true` in the envelope.→ this
isFailure public isFailure(expectedCode?: string): this Asserts an error envelope is present, optionally pinning the exact error code.→ this
hasErrorMessageContaining public hasErrorMessageContaining(fragment: string | RegExp): this Asserts the error message contains a substring or matches a regular expression.→ this
hasValidationErrorForField public hasValidationErrorForField(field: string): this Asserts the validation error details name the offending field.→ this
verify(): headers2
NameSignatureWhat it does
hasHeader public hasHeader(name: string, expected?: string | RegExp): this Asserts a response header exists, optionally that it contains a string or matches a pattern.→ this
isJson public isJson(): this Shorthand for asserting a content-type header containing application/json.→ this
verify(): body properties2
NameSignatureWhat it does
hasProperty public hasProperty(path: string, expected?: unknown): this Asserts a dot-path property on `data` is defined, and optionally equals a value.→ this
hasPropertyOfType public hasPropertyOfType(path: string, type: 'string' | 'number' | 'boolean' | 'object'): this Asserts a dot-path property on `data` has a given JavaScript type.→ this
verify(): arrays and paging3
NameSignatureWhat it does
isArray public isArray(options: { readonly length?: number; readonly minLength?: number } = {}): this Asserts `data` is an array, optionally with an exact or minimum length.→ this
everyItem public everyItem(predicate: (item: unknown) => boolean, description: string): this Asserts every item satisfies a predicate and reports the first offender by value.→ this
hasPaginationMeta public hasPaginationMeta(): this Asserts the response carries a pagination meta block.→ this
verify(): performance1
NameSignatureWhat it does
respondedWithin public respondedWithin(budgetMs: number): this Asserts the call finished inside a response-time budget, reporting the actual duration.→ this

Handbook

Fixtures

Every spec imports its test and expect from a single entry point, @fixtures/index, and receives its dependencies by destructuring them from the test callback's first argument. Behind that one import sit four chained fixture layers — base -> pages -> api -> auth — each extending the one before it, so a fixture in a later layer can depend on anything declared earlier. The layers are built on Playwright's own test, so the built-in fixtures (page, browser, context, request, plus testInfo as the second callback argument) remain available alongside the framework's. Fixtures marked worker-scoped are resolved once per worker process and shared by every test it runs; the rest are created fresh for each test and torn down after it, pass or fail.

Entry point (src/fixtures/index.ts)3
NameSignatureWhat it does
test export { authTest as test } from './auth.fixture'; The only `test` a spec should import — it carries every fixture from all four layers.→ the fully-chained `authTest` (base + pages + api + auth)
expect export { expect } from '@playwright/test'; Re-exported so a spec needs only one import line for both `test` and `expect`.→ Playwright's `expect`
baseTest / pageTest / apiTest / authTest export { baseTest, type BaseTestFixtures, type BaseWorkerFixtures, type TestDataAccessor } from './base.fixture'; export { pageTest, type PageObjectFixtures } from './page.fixture'; export { apiTest, type ApiFixtures, type ApiWorkerFixtures, type CleanupTracker } from './api.fixture'; export { authTest, type AuthFixtures, type AuthOptions } from './auth.fixture'; Exported for anyone extending the framework with a further layer; specs use `test` instead.→ each layer's test object plus its fixture interfaces
Base layer (src/fixtures/base.fixture.ts)6
NameSignatureWhat it does
environment readonly environment: ResolvedEnvironment; The resolved target environment: `ui.baseUrl`, `api.baseUrl`, timeouts, retries, plus `credentialsFor(role)`, `apiKey()` and `isEnabled(feature)`.→ ResolvedEnvironment — worker scope
execution readonly execution: FrameworkExecutionConfig; How the run behaves rather than what it targets: `isCi`, `headless`, `slowMoMs`, `workers`, `retries`, `logLevel`, `logToFile`, `extentEnabled`, `reuseAuthState`, `startReferenceApp`, `referenceAppPort`, `verboseApiLogging`, `runId`.→ FrameworkExecutionConfig — worker scope
testData readonly testData: TestDataAccessor; Typed accessor for the JSON datasets under `test-data/`, with the environment override merged over the common baseline.→ TestDataAccessor — test scope
testData.get get<K extends TestDataName>(name: K): TestDataRegistry[K]; Accepts exactly four dataset names — `'login'`, `'employees'`, `'dashboard'`, `'api'` — and returns that dataset fully typed (anything else is a compile error).→ the dataset's own type — LoginTestData | EmployeeTestData | DashboardTestData | ApiTestData
log readonly log: Logger; Structured, secret-masking logger with `debug` / `info` / `warn` / `error` / `action(action, target, payload?)` / `step(description, operation)` / `child(scope)`.→ Logger — test scope, scoped to this test's title
runContext readonly runContext: void; Runs automatically on every test and annotates the report with `environment`, `project` and `ui-base-url`; never destructure it.→ void — test scope, `{ auto: true }`

NameSignatureWhat it does
loginPage readonly loginPage: LoginPage; Drives the sign-in screen — the one place the suite logs in through the UI (`open()`, `loginAs(role)`, `expectLoaded()`, `signInButton`, `forgotPasswordLink`).→ LoginPage — test scope, built on the plain `page`
dashboardPage readonly dashboardPage: DashboardPage; The landing screen on an unauthenticated page — use it after a UI login in the same test.→ DashboardPage — test scope, built on the plain `page`

profilePage readonly profilePage: ProfilePage; The profile screen on an unauthenticated page — use it after a UI login in the same test.→ ProfilePage — test scope, built on the plain `page`
API layer (src/fixtures/api.fixture.ts)11
NameSignatureWhat it does
apiRequestContext readonly apiRequestContext: APIRequestContext; The raw Playwright request context every client is built on, created against `environment.api.baseUrl` and disposed when the worker ends; rarely destructured directly.→ APIRequestContext — worker scope
apiClient readonly apiClient: ApiClient; The unauthenticated HTTP client — the starting point for auth tests and 401/negative scenarios (`get`, `post`, `withToken`, `clearAuthToken`, `isAuthenticated`).→ ApiClient — test scope, unauthenticated
authApi readonly authApi: AuthApi; Authentication endpoints: `health()`, `login(credentials)`, `me()`, and `authenticateClientAs(role)` which signs the shared `apiClient` in as that role.→ AuthApi — test scope, on the unauthenticated `apiClient`
userApi readonly userApi: UserApi; User endpoints on the unauthenticated client — pair with `authApi.authenticateClientAs(role)` to test a non-admin role's access.→ UserApi — test scope, on the unauthenticated `apiClient`
employeeApi readonly employeeApi: EmployeeApi; Employee endpoints on the unauthenticated client — use it for 401 and role-permission scenarios, not for setup.→ EmployeeApi — test scope, on the unauthenticated `apiClient`
adminApiClient readonly adminApiClient: ApiClient; A separate client authenticated as ADMIN before the test and token-cleared afterwards; the default for setup, seeding and raw admin-level requests.→ ApiClient — test scope, already signed in as ADMIN
adminEmployeeApi readonly adminEmployeeApi: EmployeeApi; The employee service you use for real work: creating fixtures data, reading records back and tearing them down (`create`, `createOrThrow`, `getById`, `list`, `remove`, `deleteIfExists`, `deleteAll`).→ EmployeeApi — test scope, on `adminApiClient`
adminUserApi readonly adminUserApi: UserApi; User endpoints with admin rights, for setup and verification that requires elevated access.→ UserApi — test scope, on `adminApiClient`
cleanup readonly cleanup: CleanupTracker; Registers records created during a test so teardown removes them via `adminEmployeeApi.deleteAll(...)`, even when the test fails.→ CleanupTracker — test scope
cleanup.employee employee(id: string): void; Registers one employee id for deletion after the test; duplicate ids are ignored.→ void
cleanup.trackedEmployeeIds readonly trackedEmployeeIds: readonly string[]; A copy of the ids currently registered — useful for asserting what the test created.→ readonly string[]
Auth layer (src/fixtures/auth.fixture.ts)6
NameSignatureWhat it does
role readonly role: UserRole; // declared as role: ['ADMIN', { option: true }] Selects which persisted session backs `authenticatedPage` and the `*As` Page Objects. Set it with `test.use({ role: 'ADMIN' })` at file or describe level. Valid values: 'ADMIN' | 'MANAGER' | 'EMPLOYEE' | 'STUDENT' | 'MENTOR'.→ UserRole — an option, not a value fixture; defaults to 'ADMIN'
authenticatedContext readonly authenticatedContext: BrowserContext; A browser context loaded with the stored session for the selected `role`, closed after the test; destructure it when you need context-level control (cookies, extra pages).→ BrowserContext — test scope
authenticatedPage readonly authenticatedPage: Page; A page already signed in as `role`, with no UI login paid for per test; use it for raw Playwright work against an authenticated session.→ Page — test scope
dashboardAs readonly dashboardAs: DashboardPage; The dashboard already signed in as `role` — the normal way to test the landing experience.→ DashboardPage — test scope, bound to `authenticatedPage`
employeesAs readonly employeesAs: EmployeePage; The employee directory already signed in as `role`; exposes `rawPage` for interception and request assertions.→ EmployeePage — test scope, bound to `authenticatedPage`
profileAs readonly profileAs: ProfilePage; The profile screen already signed in as `role`.→ ProfilePage — test scope, bound to `authenticatedPage`
`loginPage`, `dashboardPage`, `employeePage` and `profilePage` are built on the plain Playwright `page`, which carries no session. Opening `dashboardPage` without signing in first lands on the login screen.
For an already-signed-in screen use the auth-layer twins — `dashboardAs`, `employeesAs`, `profileAs` — together with `test.use({ role: '...' })`. Reserve the plain Page Objects for specs that deliberately exercise the login flow.
`role` is declared as a Playwright option (`role: ['ADMIN', { option: true }]`), not an ordinary fixture, so it cannot be assigned inside a test body.
Set it with `test.use({ role: 'MANAGER' })` at file or `describe` level, before the tests that need it. Omit it and the default `'ADMIN'` applies.
`UserRole` allows `'ADMIN' | 'MANAGER' | 'EMPLOYEE' | 'STUDENT' | 'MENTOR'`, but global setup only pre-creates sessions for `ROLES_TO_AUTHENTICATE = ['ADMIN', 'MANAGER', 'EMPLOYEE']`, and only for roles the current environment actually defines credentials for.
`contextForRole` regenerates a missing session on demand, so a single-spec run still works; if the role has no credentials in that environment it throws a `FrameworkError` reading "Stored session is unavailable". Add the role's credential source to the environment JSON before using it.
`authApi`, `userApi` and `employeeApi` all wrap the SAME unauthenticated `apiClient` instance. Calling `authApi.authenticateClientAs('EMPLOYEE')` silently authenticates `employeeApi` and `userApi` too, so ordering within a test changes behaviour.
Use the `admin*` fixtures (`adminApiClient`, `adminEmployeeApi`, `adminUserApi`) for setup and seeding — they are a separate client, signed in as ADMIN and token-cleared in teardown. Keep the shared client for deliberate auth and negative scenarios, and call `apiClient.clearAuthToken()` when you need it clean.
`cleanup` only knows how to delete employees — its sole method is `employee(id)`, and teardown calls `adminEmployeeApi.deleteAll(...)`. Records of any other type, and employees you never registered, survive the test.
Call `cleanup.employee(id)` immediately after each create, in the same `test.step` that creates it, so a later failure still leaves the id registered.
`runContext` is an automatic fixture (`{ auto: true }`) typed `void`. Destructuring it into a test gives you nothing useful and only obscures the intent.
Leave it out of the destructure — it runs on every test regardless and pushes the `environment`, `project` and `ui-base-url` annotations for the report.
`environment`, `execution` and `apiRequestContext` are worker-scoped, so they are resolved once per worker and shared across every test it runs. `apiRequestContext` fixes its `baseURL` to `environment.api.baseUrl` at creation.
Treat them as read-only run configuration. If you need a request context pointed somewhere else, build one in the test rather than expecting the fixture to change.
`testData.get(...)` accepts exactly four names — `'login'`, `'employees'`, `'dashboard'`, `'api'` — because `TestDataName` is `keyof TestDataRegistry`. A misspelled name is a compile error, not a runtime lookup failure.
To add a dataset, extend `TestDataRegistry` in `src/types/TestData.ts` with its typed shape and add the matching JSON under `test-data/`; `get` picks up the new key and its return type automatically.
Importing `test` from `@playwright/test` instead of the framework entry point yields the bare Playwright test object, and every framework fixture in the destructure becomes undefined.
Always `import { expect, test } from '@fixtures/index';` — the alias `@fixtures/*` maps to `src/fixtures/*` in tsconfig.json.
Handbook

BasePage

BasePage is the abstract class every Page Object extends; it holds every reusable browser interaction in the framework and knows nothing about a specific application screen. A subclass supplies only two things — a path and a rootIndicator — plus its own locators and business-level actions, and inherits roughly eighty ready-made interactions grouped into navigation, clicks, input, dropdowns, checkbox/radio, element state, data extraction, mouse, file transfer, browser interaction (dialogs/tabs), frames, screenshots, scrolling, network interception and storage. Every action goes through the protected perform helper, which logs action -> target at DEBUG and, on failure, re-throws a UiActionError carrying the operation, target, page class, URL, environment and timeout — so a CI failure is debuggable from the log alone. Actions accept a Target, which is either a Playwright Locator or a selector string, and rely on Playwright's auto-waiting: there are no arbitrary sleeps anywhere in this layer.

`path` is `protected abstract readonly`, so it cannot be initialised inline when its value comes from the environment — `this.environment` does not exist until `super(page)` has run.
Declare it as `protected readonly path: string;` and assign it in the constructor after `super(page)` (as LoginPage and DashboardPage do). Only a hard-coded path such as `protected readonly path = '/profile';` can use an inline initialiser.
`rootIndicator` is `public abstract readonly` and is what `open()`, `waitUntilLoaded()` and `isLoaded()` wait on. Forgetting to assign it, or pointing it at something that renders before the page is really ready, makes `open()` return too early.
Assign it in the constructor to a locator that only exists on the loaded screen — every page in the repo sets `this.rootIndicator = this.heading;` where heading is a `getByRole('heading', ...)`.
`selectByLabel`, `selectByValue` and `selectByIndex` pass `{ timeout: options.timeout }` straight through, so with no explicit `options.timeout` the timeout is `undefined` and Playwright's own default applies — unlike every other action, which falls back to `this.environment.timeouts.action`.
Pass an explicit `{ timeout }` to the select* methods when a screen needs the environment timeout honoured.
`isVisible`, `isHidden` and `isLoaded` swallow their errors and default to `DEFAULT_TIMEOUTS.shortPoll` (5 000 ms). They do not go through `perform`, so a failure produces no log line and no `UiActionError` — a false `false` looks identical to a genuinely absent element.
Use them only for conditional flows. For anything the test asserts on, use `waitForVisible` / `waitForHidden` (which throw a `UiActionError`) or a web-first `expect(locator).toBeVisible()`.
`clickAndWaitForNavigation` defaults `urlPattern` to `/.*/`, and `page.waitForURL` resolves immediately when the current URL already matches — so with no pattern the wait can settle on the pre-click URL rather than the destination.
Pass `{ urlPattern: '**/employees' }` (or a RegExp for the destination) whenever the navigation target matters.
`getText`, `getAttribute` and `getInputValue` silently operate on `.first()`, while `getAllTexts` and `getCount` operate on every match. A selector matching several nodes therefore returns the first one without any strict-mode error.
Scope the locator precisely (the repo scopes form fields to the modal root, e.g. `form.getByLabel('Full name')`) rather than relying on `.first()` semantics.
The screenshot helpers derive their file name from the `name` argument only — `reports/screenshots/<name>.png`, `<name>-full.png`, `<name>-element.png` — so two calls with the same name in different tests overwrite each other.
Include the test or scenario in the name. Also remember these return a Buffer for report attachment; they are not visual-regression assertions (use Playwright snapshots for that).
`mockJsonResponse` and `abortRequests` register page routes that survive for the rest of the test and leak into later navigations in the same page.
Call `await page.clearRoutes()` once the assertion is done — every network regression test in the repo ends that way.
`perform` is `protected` on `BasePage`, and `BaseComponent` declares its own separate `perform` with a different, narrower signature — `protected async perform<T>(operation: string, target: string, action: () => Promise<T>): Promise<T>` (no `options`, target must be a string). The two are unrelated classes; `BaseComponent` does not extend `BasePage`.
Inside a Page Object use the four-argument `perform(operation, target, action, options)`; inside a Component use the three-argument form. Neither is callable from a spec — a test reaches raw Playwright through the `rawPage` getter instead.
`frameByName` and `getFrame` are synchronous, and `getCurrentUrl` is synchronous too; awaiting them is harmless but reads as if they were async, and `frameByName` throws a `UiActionError` rather than returning null when no frame matches.
Call them without `await`, and wrap `frameByName` in a check only if a missing frame is an expected state.
Handbook

Components

The component library is the framework's Component Object Model: BaseComponent is an abstract root that scopes a component to a single root Locator, and eight concrete components (Header, Sidebar, Table, Modal, Toast, Pagination, Search, DatePicker) each own one region of the UI. Every component takes the Playwright Page as its first constructor argument and derives all of its internal locators from this.root, so a markup change is fixed in one file no matter how many screens render that region. Page objects compose components as public readonly properties instead of re-declaring their locators — EmployeePage alone composes seven of the eight. Everything is re-exported from the barrel src/components/index.ts, alongside the option and result types (TableOptions, TableRowData, ModalOptions, ToastVariant, PaginationState, SearchOptions, DatePickerOptions).

`rowByColumnValue` looks like `row` and `rowByText` but is async — it resolves the column index first. Writing `table.rowByColumnValue('Name', x).click()` calls a method on a Promise.
Await it: `const row = await table.rowByColumnValue('Name', x);`. Only `row(index)` and `rowByText(text)` return a Locator synchronously.
`latest` on ToastComponent is a getter, not a method, so `toast.latest()` throws "is not a function".
Use `toast.latest` with no parentheses.
`sortByColumn` returns a string, not void — the value is the raw `aria-sort` attribute ('ascending' / 'descending', or 'none' when absent), not 'asc' / 'desc'.
Map it before passing to `isColumnSorted`, which takes `'asc' | 'desc'`: `isColumnSorted('Name', first === 'ascending' ? 'asc' : 'desc')`.
`getColumnIndex` (and therefore `getCell`, `getColumnValues`, `rowByColumnValue`) matches the header by case-insensitive *full equality*, not substring. A header of 'Employee Name' will not match 'Name'.
Pass the whole header text. When it throws, the UiActionError's `actual` field lists every available column — read it rather than guessing.
`expectRowMatching` compares values with `includes`, so it is a substring match, and it lowercases the header keys. A partial value passes, and a stale expectation can match the wrong row.
Pass values specific enough to be unambiguous. For exact-count assertions combine with `expectRowCount`.
Both SidebarComponent and HeaderComponent expose a `menuToggle` for test id 'menu-toggle', but Sidebar's is resolved from `page` (global) while Header's is scoped to `header.app-header`.
They are not interchangeable. If the app ever renders two menu toggles, `sidebar.menuToggle` will hit strict-mode ambiguity while `header.menuToggle` stays scoped — prefer the page-level `sidebar.ensureVisible()` / `navigateTo()` which handle the collapse for you.
SearchComponent's methods each await a network response whose URL contains `requestFragment` (default `'/employees?'`). Reused on a screen that issues a different request, `search` / `filterByDepartment` / `clearFilters` hang until the navigation timeout.
Pass `requestFragment` in the SearchOptions for that screen, e.g. `new SearchComponent(page, { requestFragment: '/departments?' })`.
ToastComponent and SidebarComponent and HeaderComponent take only `(page)` — their roots ('#toastRegion', navigation named 'Primary', 'header.app-header') are hardcoded and cannot be overridden.
If a second toast region or header appears, the component needs a code change; do not try to pass an options object as a second argument.
`PaginationComponent`'s second parameter is a bare `root?: Locator`, unlike Table/Modal/Search/DatePicker which take an options object. Passing `{ root }` silently yields a wrong root.
Call it positionally: `new PaginationComponent(page, page.getByTestId('grid-pagination'))`.
`getState` parses the summary text with the regex /Page\s+(\d+)\s+of\s+(\d+).*?(\d+)\s+\w+/i. If the summary line's wording changes, every pagination method fails, since goToNextPage/goToPreviousPage/goToPage all call it.
Keep the summary in the 'Page <n> of <n> · <total> records' shape; the thrown UiActionError reports both the expected format and the actual text.
`goToPage` walks one page at a time, calling `getState` after every step — jumping to page 40 issues 40 clicks and 40 parses.
For deep pages, prefer `setPageSize` to shrink the page count, or navigate by URL, and reserve `goToPage` for short hops.
`TableComponent.emptyState` is `Locator | undefined` — it exists only if it was passed in the options. `expectEmpty` then silently skips the empty-state assertion and `isEmpty` falls back to a row count.
Pass `emptyState` in TableOptions (as EmployeePage does) whenever you want the empty panel actually asserted.
`ModalComponent.getErrorMessage` returns `null` when the error element is hidden, so `expect(await modal.getErrorMessage()).toContain(...)` throws on null rather than failing informatively.
Assert visibility first — `await expect(modal.errorMessage).toBeVisible()` — then read the text, which is the pattern EmployeePage uses.
`DatePickerComponent.selectRange` needs a second, separately-constructed DatePickerComponent for the end date; it does not find an end field inside its own root.
Construct both pickers (each with its own root/testId) and call `startPicker.selectRange(endPicker, startIso, endIso)`.
`selectMonthAndYear` takes a month *name* and resolves it via `MONTH_NAMES.indexOf(monthName)`. An unrecognised or differently-cased name yields index -1 and a selectOption failure.
Pass a name exactly as listed in `MONTH_NAMES` (src/utils/DateUtils.ts). `selectDate` takes an ISO `YYYY-MM-DD` string instead and is the safer default.
`BaseComponent.perform` is `protected`, so the logging/error-enrichment wrapper is unavailable to tests and page objects — raw Locator calls made outside a component lose the UiActionError context.
Add the interaction as a method on the component rather than reaching through `component.root` from a spec.
`BaseComponent.isVisible()` swallows the timeout and returns false, so a genuinely broken selector reads as 'not visible' rather than failing.
Use `waitUntilVisible()` when absence should fail the test; keep `isVisible()` for branching.
Handbook

Page Objects

The framework ships four concrete Page Objects, all extending BasePage and all delivered to specs as fixtures (loginPage, dashboardPage, employeePage, profilePage) — a spec never constructs one by hand. Each declares two things BasePage requires: a path it navigates to via open(), and a rootIndicator locator that open() waits for before handing control back. Beyond raw locators, each page exposes business-level workflows (loginAs, createEmployee, exportEmployeesCsv, getDetails) plus expect* assertion helpers, so tests read as user journeys rather than DOM scripts. Everything is re-exported from the barrel src/pages/index.ts.
