Barrel exports (src/pages/index.ts)2
NameSignatureWhat it does
index.ts exports export { BasePage, type ActionOptions, type ClickOptions, type Target, type TypeOptions } from './BasePage'; export { LoginPage } from './LoginPage'; export { DashboardPage, type DashboardMetrics } from './DashboardPage'; export { EmployeePage, type EmployeeFormInput } from './EmployeePage'; export { ProfilePage, type ProfileDetails } from './ProfilePage'; The single import surface for Page Objects and their public types.
PageObjectFixtures export interface PageObjectFixtures { readonly loginPage: LoginPage; readonly dashboardPage: DashboardPage; readonly employeePage: EmployeePage; readonly profilePage: ProfilePage; } The fixture names a spec destructures to get ready-made Page Objects — no spec constructs one itself.
Only two of the four pages get their path from environment config. LoginPage sets `this.path = this.environment.ui.loginPath` and DashboardPage sets `this.path = this.environment.ui.dashboardPath` (both "/login" and "/dashboard" in config/environments/dev.json, qa.json, uat.json and prod.json). EmployeePage and ProfilePage hardcode `protected readonly path = '/employees'` and `= '/profile'`.
Changing the login or dashboard route is a config edit; changing the employees or profile route means editing the class. If you need a one-off destination, `BasePage.open(pathOverride?: string)` accepts an explicit path.
`path` is `protected` on BasePage (`protected abstract readonly path: string`), so a spec cannot read `employeePage.path` to build a URL.
Call `await page.open()` to navigate, or `await page.open('/some/other/path')` for an override. `rootIndicator` is public, so you can assert on it directly.
`LoginPage.errorMessage` is deliberately narrowed to `page.getByRole('main').getByRole('alert')` because the toast region also publishes `role="alert"`. Asserting on a bare `getByRole('alert')` will hit two elements in strict mode.
Use `loginPage.errorMessage` / `expectErrorMessage()` for the inline form error and `loginPage.toast` for the transient notification — they are different elements.
Every EmployeePage form locator (`nameInput`, `emailInput`, `departmentSelect`, `designationInput`, `salaryInput`, `activeCheckbox`, `saveButton`) is scoped to `this.formModal.root`, so none of them resolve while the dialog is closed. `departmentSelect` additionally uses `{ exact: true }` because the filter bar renders its own "Department" label.
Call `openCreateForm()` or `openEditForm(name)` before touching a form field, or use the `createEmployee` / `updateEmployee` workflows which do it for you.
`fillEmployeeForm` drives the department field via `selectByValue(this.departmentSelect, input.department)`, i.e. the option's `value` attribute — not its visible label.
Pass the option value the app uses for `department`; the factory-built payloads in `@data/factories` already carry the right form.
`createEmployee` and `updateEmployee` assert their own success toasts ("Employee created", "Employee updated"), but `deleteEmployee` only waits for the confirm modal to close — it asserts no toast.
After `deleteEmployee(name)`, assert the outcome yourself: `await employeePage.toast.expectSuccess('Employee deleted')` and/or `await employeePage.expectEmployeeAbsent(name)`, as the lifecycle spec does.
`getEmployeeIdByName` throws rather than returning null when the row lacks the attribute: `Employee row "<name>" is missing its data-employee-id attribute`.
Make sure the row is actually rendered first (search/filter to it), and treat the throw as a real defect in the table markup, not a lookup miss.
`attemptInvalidCreate` returns `(await this.formModal.getErrorMessage()) ?? ''` — an empty string, not null, when the modal exposes no message text.
Assert on content (`expect(message).toContain(...)`) rather than truthiness, since '' is a valid return.
Both getters wait past a placeholder dash, but they are different characters: `getMetrics()` waits for `totalEmployeesMetric` to stop reading '–' (en dash) and `ProfilePage.getDetails()` waits for `email` to stop reading '—' (em dash).
Don't copy one placeholder string into the other page's assertion. Prefer calling `getMetrics()` / `getDetails()`, which already encode the correct wait.
`getMetrics()` coerces three tiles with `Number(...)` but leaves `averageSalary` as raw text (a ₹-prefixed string in DashboardMetrics).
Compare `averageSalary` as a string or with a regex (`expect(metrics.averageSalary).toMatch(/^₹/)`); only totalEmployees, departments and active are numeric.
`openAndCaptureSource()` calls `this.open()` itself, after arming a `waitForResponse` for the GET `/employees` call — so it navigates, it does not read the page you are already on. If the payload has no `meta.total` it returns `total: -1`.
Let it do the navigation (calling it after a `beforeEach` open just re-navigates, which is fine), and treat `total === -1` as "the response carried no meta.total", not as a real count.
LoginPage, DashboardPage and EmployeePage each define their own `expectLoaded()`; ProfilePage does not, and BasePage declares no such method.
On ProfilePage, rely on `open()` (which waits for `rootIndicator`) plus `expectRole()` / `getDetails()` — calling `profilePage.expectLoaded()` will not compile.
`profilePage` is wired as a fixture in src/fixtures/page.fixture.ts but no spec under tests/ currently uses it.
There is no in-repo usage example to copy; base new ProfilePage tests on the class API (`open()`, `getDetails()`, `expectRole()`) rather than searching for a precedent.
Credentials are never passed as literals from a spec — LoginPage resolves them with `this.environment.credentialsFor(role)` and `UserRole` is a closed union: `'ADMIN' | 'MANAGER' | 'EMPLOYEE' | 'STUDENT' | 'MENTOR'`.
Use `loginAs('ADMIN')` and configure the secret in the environment/CI. Reserve `login(username, password)` and `submitCredentials(...)` for negative cases where the literal is the point.
Handbook

API layer

The API layer has three tiers a test touches. ApiClient is the only thing that speaks HTTP — it resolves the base URL from the active environment, substitutes :name path parameters, attaches the bearer token or API key, retries idempotent calls, and parses every reply into a uniform ApiResponse<T>. Domain services (AuthApi, EmployeeApi, UserApi) sit on top so specs never assemble raw paths, and they add test-lifecycle helpers such as createOrThrow, waitUntilSearchable and deleteIfExists. Assertions go through verify(response), a fluent ResponseValidator<T> whose eighteen methods chain — status, envelope, headers, dot-path properties, array rules, response-time budgets and JSON-Schema contracts — each failure naming the method, URL and a payload preview. Tests obtain all of these ready-made from the fixtures in src/fixtures/api.fixture.ts (apiClient, authApi, employeeApi, adminApiClient, adminEmployeeApi, adminUserApi, userApi, cleanup) rather than constructing them by hand.

A non-2xx response does not throw. `adminEmployeeApi.getById('nope')` resolves normally with status 404, so a test that only awaits the call and never asserts will pass silently.
Always route the result through `verify(response)` and assert a status. Use the service's `*OrThrow` variants (`createOrThrow`, `loginAs`) when a failure should abort setup instead of being asserted.
`matchesSchema` validates `response.data`, while `matchesEnvelopeSchema` validates `response.body`. Passing `errorEnvelopeSchema` to `matchesSchema` checks the wrong object and fails confusingly.
Use `matchesEnvelopeSchema(errorEnvelopeSchema)` for failures and `matchesSchema(employeeSchema)` for payloads. Pagination meta lives in neither — assert it with `assertSchema(response.meta, paginationMetaSchema, 'pagination meta')`.
`unwrap()` asserts `data` is defined, so calling it after a DELETE fails: a 204 is parsed into the synthetic envelope `{ success: true }` with no `data` at all.
For deletes assert `response.status` against `HTTP_STATUS.NO_CONTENT` (or use `deleteIfExists`, which returns a boolean) and do not call `unwrap()`.
`hasProperty(path, expected)` treats an `expected` of `undefined` as "only check the property exists", so you cannot use it to assert a field is absent or undefined.
Use `satisfies((data) => data?.field === undefined, 'field must be absent')` for absence checks, or assert on `response.data` directly with `expect`.
POST and PATCH are not retried. `IDEMPOTENT_METHODS` is `['GET', 'HEAD', 'OPTIONS', 'PUT', 'DELETE']`; everything else gets exactly one attempt, so a transient 503 on a create fails the test immediately.
Pass `maxAttempts` in `RequestOptions` for that specific call when the endpoint is genuinely safe to retry — never blanket-enable it for creates, or you will get duplicate records.
`body` is JSON-stringified but `rawBody` is sent as raw bytes, and `rawBody` wins when both are supplied. Playwright would otherwise re-serialise a string body and silently repair the malformed payload a negative test is trying to send.
Use `rawBody` only for malformed-payload tests, and never pass both in the same call.
Query values that are `undefined` or the empty string are dropped from the URL, so `list({ search: '' })` sends no `search` parameter and returns the whole directory rather than nothing.
To exercise an empty-value parameter, build the request through `apiClient.get(path, { query: ... })` with a non-empty sentinel, or assert against the full-list behaviour you actually get.
An unresolved `:name` placeholder throws `ApiRequestError` from `buildUrl` before any request is made, which reads like a network failure in the log.
Supply every placeholder in `pathParams`. Prefer the service methods and `API_ROUTES.employees.byId(id)`, which build the path for you and URL-encode the id.
`withToken(token)` returns a brand-new client; it does not mutate the one you called it on. Chaining `apiClient.withToken(t)` and then reusing `apiClient` still uses the original (or no) token.
Capture the result — `const asManager = apiClient.withToken(token)` — or use `authApi.authenticateClientAs(role)` when you want the shared client itself re-bound.
`skipAuth: true` strips both the `Authorization` and the `x-api-key` headers, so it silently defeats `useApiKey: true` if you set both.
Pick one: `skipAuth` for unauthenticated negative tests, `useApiKey` for key-based auth.
Compiled schemas are cached by `schema.title ?? JSON.stringify(schema)`. Two different schemas that share a `title` resolve to the first one compiled, so the second silently validates against the wrong contract.
Give every schema in `src/api/models/schemas.ts` a unique `title`, and never copy a schema object while leaving its title unchanged.
`paginationMetaSchema` sets `additionalProperties: false`, unlike the other schemas which allow extras. A new field added to the meta block by the API breaks the contract test.
Update `paginationMetaSchema` deliberately when the meta contract changes — the failure is the schema doing its job, not a flaky test.
`deleteIfExists` returns `false` for both "already gone" (404) and "the API refused" (anything else, which only logs a warning). A protected record looks identical to a missing one.
Use `remove(id)` and assert the status when the outcome of the delete is what is under test; reserve `deleteIfExists` for teardown, where being lenient is the point.
`employeeApi` (unauthenticated) and `adminEmployeeApi` are different fixtures over different clients. Calling `authApi.authenticateClientAs(role)` re-binds the token on the shared `apiClient`, which changes what `employeeApi` and `userApi` do for the rest of the test.
Use `adminEmployeeApi` / `adminApiClient` for setup and seeding, and the plain `employeeApi` / `apiClient` for 401 and role-restriction scenarios — as the negative suite does.
`waitUntilSearchable` casts the poll result to `Employee`; if the record never appears, `pollUntil` throws rather than returning `undefined`.
Treat it as a hard precondition, or call `findByEmail` yourself when you need to assert that a record is genuinely absent.

Worked examples from the repository 13

Handbook

Utilities & data

The framework's shared helpers live as ten standalone modules under src/utils/ — there is no barrel file, so every import names the module directly through the @utils/* path alias (e.g. import { parseCsv, readTextFile } from '@utils/FileUtils'). Functional values never live in a spec: they come from JSON under test-data/, read through JsonReader, which layers test-data/<env>/<name>.json over test-data/common/<name>.json and returns the result typed against the TestDataRegistry in src/types/TestData.ts. Inside a test the usual door is the testData fixture (testData.get('employees')), which calls readTestData with the active environment already applied; outside a test (module scope, global setup, factories) call readTestData directly. Records that get written to the application are never hand-typed either — src/data/factories/EmployeeFactory.ts combines a JSON template with unique runtime values from RandomUtils/DateUtils so parallel workers cannot collide, and everything it creates carries the pwauto prefix so cleanup can find it.

Constants users touch5
NameSignatureWhat it does
TEST_DATA_PREFIX const TEST_DATA_PREFIX = 'pwauto' Prefix stamped onto every record the suite creates (via uniqueId/uniqueEmail) so cleanup can find its own data.→ string
PATHS const PATHS = { root, config, environments, testData, storage, authState, reports, extentReport, playwrightReport, jsonReport, junitReport, screenshots, videos, traces, testResults, logs, downloads, uploads, snapshots } as const Where the utils read and write: `PATHS.testData` = <repo>/test-data, `PATHS.uploads` = <repo>/test-data/files, `PATHS.downloads` = <repo>/reports/downloads.→ readonly record of absolute paths

DEFAULT_TIMEOUTS const DEFAULT_TIMEOUTS = { test: 60_000, action: 15_000, navigation: 30_000, expect: 10_000, api: 20_000, shortPoll: 5_000 } as const The fallbacks WaitUtils uses when `options.timeout` is omitted: shortPoll for waitForCondition/waitForFunction/waitForStableValue, navigation for waitForApiResponse/waitForNetworkIdle.→ readonly record of milliseconds
How do I add a new dataset? Dropping a JSON file into test-data/common/ is not enough — `readTestData('myThing')` and `testData.get('myThing')` will not compile, because both are keyed to TestDataRegistry.
Four steps, in this order. (1) Create `test-data/common/<name>.json` with the baseline values. (2) In `src/types/TestData.ts`, add an exported interface describing that shape (all `readonly`) and add `readonly <name>: <Name>TestData;` to `TestDataRegistry` — `TestDataName` widens automatically. (3) Optionally add `test-data/<env>/<name>.json` (env is one of dev | qa | uat | prod, matching `EnvironmentName`) containing only the keys that differ. (4) Optionally add an `assertDatasetKeys('<name>', ['...top-level keys...'], { environment: environment.name })` call in `global-setup.ts` alongside the existing login/employees/api calls, so a malformed file fails the run before a browser launches. Then read it with `testData.get('<name>')` inside a test, or `readTestData('<name>')` at module scope. If you genuinely do not want a registry entry, `readJson<T>('<name>')` is the untyped escape hatch — but you must supply T yourself and you lose the compile-time guarantee.
How do I add a new factory? Writing `src/data/factories/ThingFactory.ts` alone leaves `import { buildThing } from '@data/factories'` unresolved.
(1) Add the dataset first (previous gotcha) — a factory reads its template values from JSON, never from literals in the factory. (2) Create `src/data/factories/<Thing>Factory.ts` following EmployeeFactory exactly: a private `dataset()` helper calling `readTestData('<name>', { environment: resolveEnvironmentName() })` from `config/environment.config`; a private selector that throws `TestDataError` listing the valid keys when a key is unknown; and an exported `build<Thing>(options: BuildOptions = {})` that spreads template fields, layers unique values from `@utils/RandomUtils` (`uniqueName`, `uniqueEmail`, `uniqueId`) and `@utils/DateUtils` (`toIsoDate`, `addDays`), and spreads `...options.overrides` LAST. (3) Re-export it from `src/data/factories/index.ts` — that barrel is what `@data/factories` resolves to, and it is a hand-maintained explicit export list, not a `export *`. Add the type export too (`type BuildOptions`).
`import { assertVisible } from '@utils'` (or any barrel import) fails — there is no `src/utils/index.ts`.
Import each module by file: `import { parseCsv, readTextFile } from '@utils/FileUtils'`, `import { waitForApiResponse } from '@utils/WaitUtils'`. The `@utils/*` alias is declared in tsconfig.json paths. Note the factories DO have a barrel (`@data/factories`), so the two areas behave differently.
Every helper in AssertionUtils.ts is currently unused — no spec or page object in the repo imports assertVisible, assertStatus, assertMatchesSubset or SoftAssertions. A guide that presents them as the house style would contradict every real test.
The established pattern for API assertions is the fluent validator: `verify(response).hasStatus(HTTP_STATUS.CREATED).isSuccessful().matchesSchema(employeeSchema).hasProperty('email', payload.email).unwrap()` from `@api/validators`; for UI it is Playwright's own `expect(locator).toBeVisible()`. Document AssertionUtils as available helpers (SoftAssertions and assertMatchesSubset are genuinely useful for multi-field checks), not as the default path.
Datasets are cached per process, so editing a JSON file between runs inside a single Playwright process, or calling readJson twice with different environments, does not behave the way people expect.
The cache key is `${environment ?? 'none'}::${datasetName}` — note that `readTestData('api')` with no options and `readTestData('api', { environment: 'qa' })` are two different cache entries reading different merged content. Pass `{ fresh: true }` to bypass the cache for one read, or call `clearCache()`. Inside a test always go through the `testData` fixture, which always supplies the active environment.
An environment override that touches an array silently discards the common file's array — deepMerge replaces arrays, it does not concatenate them.
Only objects are merged key-by-key. To add one template in qa you must restate the entire `templates` array in `test-data/qa/employees.json`. The existing overrides are all object-valued (`pagination`, `search`, `performance`) precisely for this reason. If both `common` and `<env>` files are absent, `readJson` throws TestDataError listing `availableDatasets()`; if only the env file exists, it is used with an empty base.
`buildEmployee()` always generates a fresh name and email, so a test that needs to reuse an existing identity (e.g. a PUT that must not change the email) gets a different value than it expects.
Pass `overrides`, which is spread last and wins over everything: `buildEmployee({ templateKey: 'financeAnalyst', overrides: { email: created.email } })`. Also note `joiningDate` is always set to 30 days ago and `salary` comes from the template unless you pass `randomSalary: true` — and beware that `BuildOptions.randomSalary` is a boolean flag, while `randomSalary()` in `@utils/RandomUtils` is the function that produces the number. Same word, two things.
`withRetry` looks like it retries by default. It does not — an operation wrapped in it fails on the first error unless the caller opts in.
The defaults are `maxAttempts: 1` and `retryOn: () => false` (retry nothing). You must supply both: `withRetry(op, { maxAttempts: 3, retryOn: (error) => error instanceof ApiRequestError, description: 'GET /employees' })`. This is deliberate — retries must not mask defects. When more than one attempt runs, the thrown error is a `FrameworkError` whose context carries an `attempts` array with every failure message; the single-attempt case re-throws the original error untouched.
`createUploadFixture` writes into the repository, not a temp directory, and that directory is not gitignored.
It resolves to `PATHS.uploads`, i.e. `<repo>/test-data/files/`. `test-data/files/offer-letter.txt` and `id-proof.txt` currently sitting in the repo are exactly the residue of the dashboard sanity test ('signed offer letter' / 'identity document'). Expect generated fixtures to show up as untracked-or-modified files after a UI run; `saveDownload` by contrast writes to `reports/downloads`, which IS gitignored.
`daysBetween(from, to)` mutates both arguments — it calls `setHours(0,0,0,0)` on each Date in the subtraction, so the caller's Date objects come back normalised to midnight.
Pass copies if you still need the original times: `daysBetween(new Date(a), new Date(b))`. By contrast `addDays`/`addMonths`/`addYears` are safe — they clone internally and return a new Date.
`toFileStamp` and the other DateUtils formatters disagree about timezone, which shows up as an off-by-one day near midnight.
`toIsoDate`, `toDisplayDateTime` and `parseIsoDate` all work in LOCAL time (getFullYear/getMonth/getDate), matching the application's date fields. `toFileStamp` is UTC because it is `date.toISOString()` with `:` and `.` replaced by `-`. Use toIsoDate for anything that goes into a payload or a date picker, toFileStamp only for filenames.
`maskValue` returns `unknown`, not the input type, so assigning its result to a typed variable will not compile.
The signature is `maskValue<T>(value: T, seen = new WeakSet<object>()): unknown` — the generic constrains the input only. Cast at the call site, or (better) just pass the result straight into a logger/JSON.stringify the way Logger and ApiClient do. Also note `maskValue` returns a redacted deep clone rather than mutating, collapses cycles to the string `'[Circular]'`, and reduces an Error to `{ name, message }` — so a masked Error loses its stack.
`Logger.child()` takes a `LogScope`, but `LogScope` is not exported from Logger.ts, so you cannot annotate a variable with it.
Pass an object literal — the shape is `{ test?: string; module?: string }`. The exports from `@utils/Logger` are exactly `Logger` (class), `logger` (the shared framework-scoped instance) and `createLogger(module, test?)`. In a test, prefer the `log` fixture, which is already `createLogger(<file title>, <test title>)`.
`waitForCondition` appears to hang on a predicate that always throws, and `parseCsv` mangles exported values containing commas.
waitForCondition swallows predicate exceptions and keeps polling until the deadline, then throws `UiActionError` with the last exception attached as the cause — so a permanently broken predicate costs the full timeout (default 5000ms via DEFAULT_TIMEOUTS.shortPoll). Give it a `description` so the failure names what you were waiting for. parseCsv is a naive `split(',')` per line with trimming and blank-line removal; it is documented as assuming exports contain no quoted commas, so do not use it on arbitrary user-generated CSV.

Helper scripts (scripts/)4
NameSignatureWhat it does
scripts/clean.mjs #!/usr/bin/env node — no arguments Removes 13 generated paths (reports/playwright, reports/extent, reports/json, reports/junit, reports/screenshots, reports/videos, reports/traces, reports/downloads, reports/run-context.json, test-results, playwright-report, logs, storage/auth), then recreates logs, storage/auth and reports with a .gitkeep so the tracked skeleton survives. Resolves the repo root from its own file URL, not process.cwd().→ Console log per removed target plus a final count; always exit 0
scripts/verify-framework.mjs #!/usr/bin/env node — no arguments Runs five steps in cheapest-first order via spawnSync with inherited stdio — TypeScript (`npm run typecheck`), ESLint (`npm run lint`), Prettier (`npm run format:check`), API suite (`npx playwright test --project=api`), UI smoke (`npx playwright test --project=chromium --grep @smoke`). It does not stop at the first failure; every step runs and the verdict is printed at the end. Uses `shell: process.platform === 'win32'` so npm/npx resolve on Windows.→ A `verification summary` table (PASS/FAIL + seconds per step); exit 1 if any step failed, else 0
scripts/open-extent-report.mjs #!/usr/bin/env node — no arguments Opens reports/extent/latest.html in the default browser. It reads reports/extent/latest.json for a `passed / failed / flaky / skipped (passRate%)` line but treats that as best-effort — a truncated JSON warns and still opens the report. The report path is converted with pathToFileURL and the opener is spawned WITHOUT a shell (`open` on darwin, `cmd /c start "" <url>` on win32, `xdg-open` elsewhere), specifically so a checkout under a path containing spaces still opens; the child is detached, unref'd, and has an 'error' listener so a missing opener prints a message instead of throwing.→ Prints the last-run summary line and `Opening <path>`; exit 1 when reports/extent/latest.html is missing or the opener cannot launch
scripts/write-sauce-config.mts #!/usr/bin/env node — no arguments; imports SAUCECTL_CONFIG, saucectlRunCommand, toSaucectlYaml from ../src/integrations/sauce/SauceConfig.ts Regenerates the saucectl YAML from the typed SAUCECTL_CONFIG object so the file saucectl reads and the config the framework reasons about cannot drift. The emitted file names SAUCE_USERNAME / SAUCE_ACCESS_KEY but never contains a credential — saucectl resolves them from the environment at run time.→ Writes .sauce/config.yml; prints `wrote <path>`, the suite names, and the `saucectl run …` command to use
CLI flags the scripts rely on16
NameSignatureWhat it does
--project=<name> playwright test --project=api --project=chromium (repeatable) The primary selector. Repeat it to union projects (`test`, `test:mobile`, `test:all-browsers`); omit it and all nine projects run.→ Restricts the run to the named projects declared in playwright.config.ts
--grep <tag> playwright test --project=api --project=chromium --grep @smoke The suite selector. Tags are appended to test titles from the TAGS constant, so `--grep @smoke` is a title match, not Playwright's `tag:` option.→ Runs only tests whose title matches the expression
--update-snapshots playwright test --project=visual --update-snapshots Used only by `test:visual:update` — the deliberate re-baseline path.→ Writes new baseline PNGs instead of failing on a mismatch
--headed playwright test --headed --grep @e2e Used by `test:headed`. It overrides the config's `headless` value for the run; the HEADLESS env var is the config-level equivalent.→ Launches visible browser windows for the run
--debug cross-env PWDEBUG=1 playwright test --debug --workers=1 Used by `test:debug`, always paired with PWDEBUG=1 and `--workers=1`.→ Opens the Playwright Inspector and pauses before each action
--workers=1 playwright test --debug --workers=1 Only `test:debug` sets it. Otherwise workers come from the WORKERS env var, defaulting to 2 on CI and `min(6, cpus/2)` locally.→ Forces serial execution, overriding frameworkConfig.workers
--last-failed playwright test --last-failed Used by `test:failed`; depends on the previous run's results still being on disk.→ Re-runs only the tests that failed in the previous run
--ui playwright test --ui Used by `test:ui-mode`. Not to be confused with `test:ui`, which is the UI test *scope*.→ Opens Playwright UI mode
<path filter> playwright test --project=chromium tests/ui A positional filter, used by `test:ui` (tests/ui), `test:hybrid` (tests/hybrid) and `test:contract` (tests/api/contract). It is a substring match on the file path, not a glob.→ Restricts the run to spec files whose path contains the argument
--with-deps playwright install --with-deps Used by `prepare:browsers`; the OS dependency step is what makes it work on a bare CI image.→ Installs browser binaries plus their OS-level dependencies
--noEmit tsc --noEmit Used by `typecheck` — this repo never compiles TypeScript to disk.→ Type errors only; no JavaScript output
--fix eslint . --fix Used by `lint:fix`.→ Applies auto-fixable rule violations in place
--write / --check prettier --write "**/*.{ts,mts,js,mjs,json,md,yml}" | prettier --check "…" `format` uses `--write`, `format:check` uses `--check` — same glob, different intent.→ `--write` rewrites files; `--check` only reports and exits non-zero
--experimental-strip-types node --experimental-strip-types scripts/write-sauce-config.mts Used by `sauce:config` so the generator can import SauceConfig.ts without a build step.→ Runs the .mts file directly by stripping its type annotations
--config <path> saucectl run --config .sauce/config.yml Used by `test:sauce`.→ Points saucectl at the generated suite definition
--region / --build / --tunnel-name saucectl run --region <region> --config .sauce/config.yml [--build "<name>"] [--tunnel-name "<name>"] The command SauceConfig.ts considers canonical: `--region` is passed explicitly because saucectl documents only SAUCE_USERNAME, SAUCE_ACCESS_KEY and SAUCECTL_INSTALL_BINARY as environment inputs; `--build` and `--tunnel-name` are added only when SAUCE_BUILD_NAME / SAUCE_TUNNEL_NAME are set.→ The command string returned by saucectlRunCommand(env)

edge { name: 'edge', testIgnore: UI_TEST_IGNORE, use: { ...devices['Desktop Edge'], ...sharedUse, channel: 'msedge' } } Opt-in only — it uses the `msedge` channel, so it needs Edge on the runner and is never selected by default.→ UI + hybrid run on the installed Microsoft Edge
tablet-ipad { name: 'tablet-ipad', testIgnore: UI_TEST_IGNORE, use: { ...devices['iPad (gen 7)'], ...sharedUse, viewport: VIEWPORTS.tablet, isMobile: false } } The target of `npm run test:tablet`.→ UI + hybrid run under tablet emulation at 834x1112
mobile-chrome { name: 'mobile-chrome', testIgnore: UI_TEST_IGNORE, use: { ...devices['Pixel 7'], ...sharedUse } } Half of `npm run test:mobile`.→ UI + hybrid run under Pixel 7 emulation
mobile-safari { name: 'mobile-safari', testIgnore: UI_TEST_IGNORE, use: { ...devices['iPhone 14'], ...sharedUse } } The other half of `npm run test:mobile`.→ UI + hybrid run under iPhone 14 emulation
visual { name: 'visual', testDir: './tests/visual', use: { ...devices['Desktop Chrome'], ...sharedUse, viewport: VIEWPORTS.laptop, launchOptions: { ...sharedUse.launchOptions, args: ['--force-device-scale-factor=1'] } } } Isolated baselines. It pins `--force-device-scale-factor=1` so the host's display scaling cannot shift a 1440px viewport to 1441 and fail every baseline.→ Screenshot comparison against tests/visual/__screenshots__
Five scripts select no project at all — `test:full` (`playwright test`), `test:headed`, `test:debug`, `test:ui-mode` and `test:failed`. They therefore fan out across all nine projects, including `edge`, which uses `channel: 'msedge'` and fails on a machine without Microsoft Edge, and the emulation projects.
Narrow them at the call site: `npm run test:headed -- --project=chromium --grep "@critical"`. The README uses exactly this form.
Extra arguments passed to an npm script are swallowed unless you separate them. `npm run test:debug tests/ui/smoke/login.smoke.spec.ts` does not filter anything.
Insert `--` before your own arguments: `npm run test:debug -- tests/ui/smoke/login.smoke.spec.ts`. The same applies to `npm run trace -- test-results/<test>/trace.zip`, which otherwise opens nothing because `playwright show-trace` needs a positional path.
`saucectl` is not a devDependency. `npm run test:sauce` fails with a command-not-found on a fresh checkout even after `npm install`.
Install it separately first — `npm install -g saucectl` — then run `npm run sauce:config` and `npm run test:sauce`.
`npm run test:sauce` is `saucectl run --config .sauce/config.yml` — it omits `--region`, while `saucectlRunCommand()` in SauceConfig.ts deliberately passes it because saucectl's own documented default is the US data centre and Sauce credentials are per data centre (an EU key answers 401 against `api.us-west-1`).
The generated `.sauce/config.yml` does carry `sauce.region: "eu-central-1"`, so the default path works; if you override the region, pass it on the command line too — run the exact string `npm run sauce:config` prints under "Run it with:".
`sauce:config` runs `node --experimental-strip-types`, but `engines` in package.json only requires `node >= 20.0.0`. Type stripping is not available in every Node release that satisfies that range, so the script can fail with an unknown-option error on an otherwise "supported" Node.
Run it on a Node version that supports `--experimental-strip-types` (Node 22.6+ / 24). The rest of the framework is unaffected — this flag is used by this one script only.
`npm run clean` deletes `storage/auth`, which holds the authenticated sessions the suites reuse.
Nothing to do — the next run recreates them in global setup, which signs in as ADMIN, MANAGER and EMPLOYEE. It costs one extra login round per role. Note that `clean` never touches `tests/visual/__screenshots__`, so baselines are safe.
The bundled reference app auto-starts only when `startReferenceApp` is true, which requires the environment to be named `dev` AND its `ui.baseUrl` to contain the reference-app port. `npm run test:qa`, `test:uat` and `test:prod` therefore start nothing.
Those environments are expected to point at a deployed target. To run the sandbox against a non-dev config, start it yourself with `npm run demo-app` (or set `START_REFERENCE_APP`), and check that `config/environments/<env>.json` points at `http://127.0.0.1:4321`.
`npm run report` is `playwright show-report reports/playwright` — a path relative to the current working directory, so it shows nothing (or the wrong report) if you run it from a subdirectory.
Run it from the repository root. `npm run report:open` has no such issue: scripts/open-extent-report.mjs resolves the root from its own file URL rather than process.cwd().
`npm run report:open` exits 1 with "No Extent report found" when `reports/extent/latest.html` is missing — which is also the case if the Extent reporter was switched off for the run (`extentEnabled` comes from the `EXTENT_REPORT` env var, defaulting to true).
Run a suite first (`npm run test:smoke`), and make sure `EXTENT_REPORT` is not set to a falsy value. The Playwright HTML report (`npm run report`) is always written regardless.
`test:ui` (`--project=chromium tests/ui`) is easily confused with `test:ui-mode` (`--ui`). One is a scope, the other is Playwright's interactive UI application.
Remember the shape: anything ending in `-mode` is interactive tooling; `test:ui` is the browser test scope, mirroring `test:api` and `test:hybrid`.
`--grep @smoke` matches against the test *title*. Tags come from the `TAGS` constant and are interpolated into titles (`test(`The service reports healthy ${TAGS.smoke} ${TAGS.critical}`, …)`), not declared through Playwright's `tag:` option — so grepping for a tag that no title carries silently runs zero tests and still exits 0 in some configurations.
Use a tag that exists in src/constants/TestConstants.ts: `@smoke @sanity @regression @e2e @api @ui @hybrid @contract @negative @critical @security @visual @a11y @data-driven @flaky-watch`. Check the reported test count before trusting a green run.
`npm run test:visual:update` rewrites every baseline PNG under `tests/visual/__screenshots__/<project>/<spec>/`, including ones that changed for reasons you did not intend.
Run it only after a deliberate redesign and review the image diff in the PR. If a baseline fails locally but passes in CI, suspect display scaling — the `visual` project pins `--force-device-scale-factor=1` for exactly this reason, and running visual tests headed can still perturb rendering.
`npm run test:prod` looks like the other environment scripts but is not equivalent: it appends `--grep @smoke`.
That restriction is intentional — production runs smoke only. If you need something else against prod, spell it out yourself with `cross-env TEST_ENV=prod npx playwright test …` and think about what you are executing against a live system.
Browsers are not installed by `npm install`. A UI script fails on a fresh checkout with a missing-executable error.
Run `npm run prepare:browsers` once. `npm run test:api` is the exception — the `api` project declares `metadata: { requiresBrowser: false }` and global setup skips browser work when only that project is selected, so the API suite works before any download.
Handbook

Troubleshooting

Every error the framework raises carries an operation, a target, what it expected, what it got and a hint. Search this catalogue by the message you are staring at.

Error types7
NameSignatureWhat it does
FrameworkError export class FrameworkError extends Error { public readonly context: ErrorContext; constructor(message: string, context: ErrorContext, cause?: unknown) } The base class for every framework-raised failure — read the indented block under the headline for the operation, target, page, url and environment that produced it.→ an Error whose `message` is the summary, the rendered context block, and ` cause: <original message>`; `cause` is also set as the native Error cause when it was an Error
ErrorContext export interface ErrorContext { readonly operation: string; readonly target?: string; readonly page?: string; readonly expected?: string; readonly actual?: string; readonly environment?: string; readonly url?: string; readonly [key: string]: unknown } The shape of the debugging block printed under every framework error; `operation` is the only required key and the index signature is how extra keys like `hint`, `timeout`, `attempts` and `available` get in.→ n/a (interface)
UiActionError export class UiActionError extends FrameworkError {} A UI interaction failed (click, fill, wait) — thrown by BasePage, BaseComponent and WaitUtils.→ n/a (class)
ApiRequestError export class ApiRequestError extends FrameworkError {} An API call failed at the transport level or returned an unusable payload — thrown by ApiClient and AuthApi.→ n/a (class)
TestDataError export class TestDataError extends FrameworkError {} A JSON dataset is missing, unreadable or does not match its declared shape — thrown by JsonReader and EmployeeFactory.→ n/a (class)
ValidationError export class ValidationError extends FrameworkError {} A validation helper detected a contract breach and refused to continue (as opposed to asserting).→ n/a (class)
EnvironmentConfigurationError export class EnvironmentConfigurationError extends Error { constructor(message: string) } Configuration is wrong or incomplete; note it does NOT extend FrameworkError, so there is no context block — the whole diagnosis is in the message.→ a plain Error with `name === 'EnvironmentConfigurationError'`
Startup: environment resolution4
NameSignatureWhat it does
Unknown TEST_ENV "". Expected one of: dev, qa, uat, prod. export function resolveEnvironmentName(raw = process.env.TEST_ENV): EnvironmentName `TEST_ENV` is set to something outside `['dev','qa','uat','prod']` (a typo, or `staging`); fix the value or use one of the `test:dev|qa|uat|prod` npm scripts, which set it via cross-env.→ throws EnvironmentConfigurationError (never returns)
Environment file not found: <file> function readDefinition(name: EnvironmentName): EnvironmentDefinition `config/environments/<TEST_ENV>.json` does not exist — the message prints the absolute path it looked for, so copy an existing environment file to that name.→ throws EnvironmentConfigurationError (never returns)
Environment file <file> is not valid JSON: <parser message> function readDefinition(name: EnvironmentName): EnvironmentDefinition The environment JSON has a syntax error (a trailing comma is the usual one); the underlying JSON.parse message is appended verbatim with the offending position.→ throws EnvironmentConfigurationError (never returns)
Environment file <file> is missing required keys: <missing> function assertDefinitionShape(definition: EnvironmentDefinition, file: string): void One of `name`, `ui.baseUrl`, `api.baseUrl`, `timeouts`, `retries` is absent from the environment file — the message lists exactly which, so add them and re-run.→ throws EnvironmentConfigurationError (never returns)
Startup: credentials2
NameSignatureWhat it does
Role "<role>" is not configured for environment "<env>". Add it to config/environments/<env>.json. credentialsFor(role: UserRole): Credentials A test or fixture asked for a role that has no entry under `roles` in that environment's JSON — the fix is spelled out in the message itself.→ throws EnvironmentConfigurationError (never returns)
Credentials for role "<role>" are unavailable in environment "<env>". Set <USERNAME_ENV> and <PASSWORD_ENV> in your .env file or CI secrets. See .env.example. credentialsFor(role: UserRole): Credentials The role is declared but the env vars named by `usernameEnv`/`passwordEnv` are empty and no sandbox fallback applies; the message prints the two variable names you actually need to set. Sandbox defaults are only used when the environment file sets `allowInsecureDefaults` and supplies `sandboxUsername`/`sandboxPassword`.→ throws EnvironmentConfigurationError (never returns)
Startup: global setup3
NameSignatureWhat it does
Target environment is not reachable async function waitForEnvironment(baseUrl: string, budgetMs = 60_000): Promise<void> The health endpoint (`<api.baseUrl>/health`) did not answer 200 within 60s of one-second polling; the context carries `expected: HTTP 200 from <url>`, `actual` (the last HTTP status or socket error) and the hint "Check TEST_ENV, UI_BASE_URL/API_BASE_URL, VPN access, or whether the reference app is running."→ throws FrameworkError (never returns)
Unable to launch a browser for session setup async function launchSessionBrowser(): Promise<Browser> Playwright's browser binaries are not installed on this machine; the hint says "Run \"npm run prepare:browsers\" (or \"npx playwright install chromium\"). API-only runs (--project=api) do not need this."→ throws FrameworkError wrapping the chromium.launch() failure
assertDatasetKeys export function assertDatasetKeys(datasetName: string, requiredKeys: readonly string[], options: ReadOptions = {}): void Global setup fail-fasts on the three datasets before any browser starts: `login` needs `validUsers, invalidScenarios, ui`; `employees` needs `templates, departments, validation`; `api` needs `endpoints, performance, negative`.→ throws TestDataError('Test dataset is missing required keys') when any key is absent
Test data (JsonReader)8
NameSignatureWhat it does
Test dataset not found export function readJson<T>(datasetName: string, options: ReadOptions = {}): T Neither `test-data/common/<name>.json` nor `test-data/<env>/<name>.json` exists; the context prints `expected` (both paths it tried) and `available` — the full list from `availableDatasets()` — so a typo in the dataset name is obvious.→ throws TestDataError (never returns)
Unable to read test-data file function parseFile<T>(filePath: string): T `readFileSync` failed on a file that `existsSync` said was there — usually a permission problem or a file removed mid-run; `target` is the absolute path.→ throws TestDataError wrapping the fs error
Test-data file is not valid JSON function parseFile<T>(filePath: string): T A dataset under `test-data/` has a syntax error; the original parser message (with position) arrives as the `cause` line.→ throws TestDataError wrapping the JSON.parse error
Test-data path not found export function readPath<T>(datasetName: string, path: string, options: ReadOptions = {}): T A dot/bracket path such as `readPath('login', 'ui.submitLabel')` hit an `undefined` segment; `actual` reports `"<walked.path>" is undefined`, naming the exact segment that broke rather than returning undefined.→ throws TestDataError (never returns)
Test-data path is not traversable export function readPath<T>(datasetName: string, path: string, options: ReadOptions = {}): T A path segment tried to descend into a scalar (e.g. `ui.title.length` where `title` is a string); `actual` reports `stopped at "<walked.path>"`.→ throws TestDataError (never returns)
Test dataset is missing required keys export function assertDatasetKeys(datasetName: string, requiredKeys: readonly string[], options: ReadOptions = {}): void A dataset exists but lacks top-level keys; context shows `expected` (all required keys) and `actual: missing: <list>`. Almost always seen during global setup, before any test runs.→ throws TestDataError (never returns)
availableDatasets export function availableDatasets(): string[] The list the "Test dataset not found" error prints; call it directly when you want to know what names are valid.→ sorted dataset names discovered under `test-data/common`, or `[]` when that directory is absent
clearCache export function clearCache(): void Datasets are cached per process keyed by `<environment>::<name>`; clear the cache (or pass `{ fresh: true }`) when you edit a JSON file inside a long-lived process.→ void
Filesystem (FileUtils)5
NameSignatureWhat it does
Unable to create directory export function ensureDirectory(directory: string): string `mkdirSync` failed — a read-only workspace, or a file already occupying that path; `target` is the directory it tried to create.→ throws FrameworkError wrapping the mkdir error
Unable to write file export function writeTextFile(filePath: string, contents: string): string Writing a report, run-context or fixture file failed; `writeJsonFile` funnels through here too, so report-writing failures surface with this message.→ throws FrameworkError wrapping the write error
File not found export function readTextFile(filePath: string): string | export function fileSizeBytes(filePath: string): number Both helpers pre-check existence and throw the same message; tell them apart by the `operation` key — `readTextFile` vs `fileSizeBytes`.→ throws FrameworkError (never returns)
Unable to remove path export function remove(target: string): void `rmSync(target, { recursive: true, force: true })` failed — an already-absent target is fine, so this means a locked or in-use file (common on Windows when a browser still holds a session file).→ throws FrameworkError wrapping the rm error
Unable to save download export function saveDownload(fileName: string, data: Buffer | string): Promise<string> The write stream to `reports/downloads/<basename>` errored; the rejection is asynchronous, so `await` it or the failure surfaces as an unhandled rejection.→ a rejected Promise carrying FrameworkError; on success resolves to the absolute path under `reports/downloads`
UI failures (BasePage)3
NameSignatureWhat it does
UI action "<operation>" failed protected async perform<T>(operation: string, target: Target | undefined, action: () => Promise<T>, options: ActionOptions = {}): Promise<T> The single wrapper behind every BasePage action; the context gives `operation` (click, fill, …), `target` (the locator or your `description`), `page` (the Page Object class name), `url`, `environment` and the `timeout` in force — and the Playwright timeout text arrives as the `cause` line.→ throws UiActionError wrapping the original Playwright error
Frame not found public frameByName(nameOrUrlFragment: string): Frame No frame matched by name or URL fragment; `actual` lists every frame URL currently on the page (`frames: <url>, <url>`), which is normally enough to spot the right fragment.→ throws UiActionError (never returns)
safeUrl private safeUrl(): string Why a failure raised after the page or context closed shows `url: (page closed)` instead of losing the whole error.→ `this.page.url()`, or the literal `'(page closed)'` if reading it throws
UI failures (BaseComponent)2
NameSignatureWhat it does
Component action "<operation>" failed protected async perform<T>(operation: string, target: string, action: () => Promise<T>): Promise<T> The component-level twin of BasePage.perform; `page` here is the component class name (e.g. `TableComponent`), which is how you tell a component failure from a page failure at a glance. Note it takes no options and reports no `timeout` key.→ throws UiActionError wrapping the original error
isVisible public async isVisible(timeout = DEFAULT_TIMEOUTS.shortPoll): Promise<boolean> The deliberate exception to "never swallow": it catches the wait failure and returns false, so use it for branching and `waitUntilVisible` when you want the diagnostic error.→ `true` / `false` — never throws
API failures (ApiClient)4
NameSignatureWhat it does
Unresolved path parameter private buildUrl(path: string, options: RequestOptions): string A `:name` placeholder survived substitution because `pathParams` had no matching key; `expected` names it exactly — `a value for ":<name>" in pathParams`.→ throws ApiRequestError (never returns)
Retryable status received private async send<T>(method: HttpMethod, path: string, options: RequestOptions): Promise<ApiResponse<T>> An internal signal, not a final error: a 429/500/502/503 on a call with retries left is thrown so `withRetry` backs off. You normally see it only as an `attempts` entry inside a later "API request failed". Retries apply to GET/HEAD/OPTIONS/PUT/DELETE only — POST and PATCH get a single attempt unless you pass `maxAttempts`.→ throws ApiRequestError inside the retry loop (usually not seen directly)
API request failed private async send<T>(method: HttpMethod, path: string, options: RequestOptions): Promise<ApiResponse<T>> The transport gave up: connection refused/reset, socket hang up or timeout. Context carries `operation: '<METHOD> request'`, the masked `target` URL, `environment`, the `timeout` used and the `attempts` count; the cause chain lists each attempt's message.→ throws ApiRequestError wrapping the retry/transport failure
API response was not valid JSON private async parse<T>(raw: APIResponse, method: HttpMethod, url: string, durationMs: number): Promise<ApiResponse<T>> The server answered but the body would not parse — nearly always an HTML error page or proxy interstitial. `actual` shows the first 300 characters of the body and `status` the HTTP code, which identifies the offender immediately. A 204 or an empty body is handled, not an error.→ throws ApiRequestError wrapping the JSON.parse error
API failures (AuthApi)1
NameSignatureWhat it does
API login failed public async loginAs(role: UserRole): Promise<LoginResponse> Credentials resolved but the login endpoint rejected them; `expected: 'HTTP 200 with a token'` and `actual: 'HTTP <status> <errorCode>'`. This is what breaks the `adminApiClient` fixture and, through it, every API test in the file.→ throws ApiRequestError (never returns)
API assertions (ResponseValidator)8
NameSignatureWhat it does
verify export function verify<T>(response: ApiResponse<T>): ResponseValidator<T> Entry point for every API assertion; its failures are Playwright `expect` failures, not FrameworkErrors, so they carry no context block — the diagnosis is in the message text instead.→ ResponseValidator<T> for chaining
<METHOD> <url> expected HTTP <n> but received <n>. Body: <first 500 chars> public hasStatus(expected: number): this Every ResponseValidator message is prefixed by `label` (`${method} ${url}`), and the ones that can be ambiguous append `payloadPreview` — the first 500 characters of the response body — so you see the server's own error without re-running.→ throws the Playwright expect failure with this message
<METHOD> <url> envelope was not successful: <payload> public isSuccessful(): this Two separate checks: first that the HTTP status was 2xx (`expected a 2xx, received <status>`), then that `body.success === true`. A 200 carrying `success:false` fails on the second message, which is the giveaway that the transport was fine and the business call was not.→ throws the Playwright expect failure
<METHOD> <url> is missing data.<path>. Body: <payload> public hasProperty(path: string, expected?: unknown): this A dot path into `response.data` resolved to undefined — the printed body tells you whether the field was renamed or the payload was nested differently. With `expected` supplied, a present-but-different value fails as `data.<path> mismatch` instead.→ throws the Playwright expect failure
<METHOD> <url> expected a validation error for "<field>", got <details> public hasValidationErrorForField(field: string): this The API returned an error but `error.details` did not include an entry whose `field` matches; the raw `details` array is printed so you can see the field names the server actually used.→ throws the Playwright expect failure
<METHOD> <url> took <n>ms, budget <n>ms public respondedWithin(budgetMs: number): this The performance guard; `durationMs` is measured by ApiClient around the whole retry loop, so a slow first attempt plus a retry counts against the budget.→ throws the Playwright expect failure
<METHOD> <url> carried no data. Body: <payload> public unwrap(): T You unwrapped a response whose `data` was absent — check the envelope shape in the printed body before assuming the endpoint is broken.→ the payload `T`, or throws the Playwright expect failure
<label> data did not match its JSON Schema:\n <path> <message> public matchesSchema(schema: JsonSchema): this Contract failure; Ajv runs with `allErrors: true`, so every violation is listed one per line as ` <instancePath or (root)> <message>`. `matchesEnvelopeSchema` is the same check against the whole envelope, labelled `<label> envelope`.→ throws the Playwright expect failure via assertSchema
Sessions and authentication5
NameSignatureWhat it does
Unable to establish an authenticated session export async function createStorageState(browser: Browser, role: UserRole): Promise<string> The scripted UI sign-in for a role did not complete; context carries `target: <role>`, `environment`, the `url` the page was sitting on when it failed and `expected: 'successful UI sign-in'`, with the real locator/timeout error as the cause. Usually wrong credentials or a changed login screen.→ throws FrameworkError wrapping the underlying UI failure
Stored session is unavailable async function contextForRole(browser: Browser, role: UserRole): Promise<BrowserContext> The storage-state file was still missing after an on-demand `createStorageState` retry; `expected` prints the absolute path it wanted. Deleting `storage/auth/` and re-running lets global setup regenerate it.→ throws FrameworkError (never returns)
storageStatePath export function storageStatePath(role: UserRole): string Where a role's session lives; the name is built by `authStateFileName(role, environment)` and is environment-scoped, so switching TEST_ENV never reuses another environment's session.→ absolute path `storage/auth/<env>.<role lowercased>.v1.json`
hasFreshStorageState export function hasFreshStorageState(role: UserRole): boolean Explains the "it logged in again for no reason" case: `MAX_STATE_AGE_MS` is 45 * 60 * 1000, so a session older than 45 minutes is re-minted.→ true only when the file exists, `REUSE_AUTH_STATE` is on, and its mtime is under 45 minutes old
clearStorageStates export function clearStorageStates(roles: readonly UserRole[]): void Global teardown calls this for ADMIN, MANAGER, EMPLOYEE, STUDENT, MENTOR unless `KEEP_AUTH_STATE` is `1|true|yes`, because the files carry live tokens — which is why `storage/auth/` is empty after every run.→ void
Diagnostics: logging9
NameSignatureWhat it does
createLogger export function createLogger(module: string, test?: string): Logger Every framework area builds one at import time (`createLogger('ApiClient')`, `createLogger('global-setup')`); the module name is the third field of every log line, so it is how you filter the log.→ a Logger scoped to that module (and test title)
Logger.write private write(level: LogLevel, message: string, payload?: unknown): void Defines the line format: `${timestamp} | ${level.padEnd(5)} | ${scopeParts || 'framework'} | ${safeMessage}${safePayload}` — ISO timestamp, level, `module | test` scope, then the message and a JSON payload. Both message and payload go through `maskString`/`maskValue` first, so any secret reads `***REDACTED***`.→ void
Logger.action public action(action: string, target: string, payload?: unknown): void Emits `<action> -> <target>` at DEBUG. Every BasePage and BaseComponent interaction calls it, so raising the level to DEBUG gives you a step-by-step trail of what the test clicked before it failed.→ void
Logger.step public async step<T>(description: string, operation: () => Promise<T>): Promise<T> Wrap a block to get its duration in the log without changing how its failure propagates.→ the operation's value; logs `<description> (<n>ms)` at DEBUG, or `<description> failed after <n>ms` at ERROR and re-throws untouched
configuredLevel const configuredLevel: LogLevel = LOG_LEVELS.includes(frameworkConfig.logLevel) ? frameworkConfig.logLevel : 'INFO' An unrecognised LOG_LEVEL silently falls back to INFO rather than failing — valid values are exactly `DEBUG`, `INFO`, `WARN`, `ERROR` from `LOG_LEVELS`.→ the active threshold; anything below it is dropped by weight (DEBUG 10, INFO 20, WARN 30, ERROR 40)
logLevel logLevel: (process.env.LOG_LEVEL as LogLevel | undefined) ?? (isCi ? 'INFO' : 'DEBUG') How you raise verbosity: `LOG_LEVEL=DEBUG npx playwright test --grep "@smoke"`. Local runs are already DEBUG; CI defaults to INFO, so set LOG_LEVEL=DEBUG on the CI job to get the action trail.→ LogLevel
verboseApiLogging verboseApiLogging: bool(process.env.VERBOSE_API_LOGGING, !isCi) Gates request/response *bodies* in the ApiClient log lines (`-> GET <url>` / `<- 200 GET <url> (123ms)`). Off by default on CI — set `VERBOSE_API_LOGGING=true` there, and remember the bodies still need LOG_LEVEL=DEBUG to be emitted at all.→ boolean (accepts `1|true|yes|on`)
logToFile logToFile: bool(process.env.LOG_TO_FILE, true) Enables the file sink at `logs/run-<runId>.log`. If the directory cannot be created the logger prints `[Logger] file logging disabled: <message>` once and keeps going on console only; a later write failure prints `[Logger] file sink stopped: <message>`.→ boolean
runId runId: process.env.RUN_ID ?? new Date().toISOString().replace(/[:.]/g, '-') Computed per process, so each Playwright worker writes its own `logs/run-<timestamp>.log`. Set `RUN_ID` to collapse a whole run into one file.→ string used as the log file name and reported in teardown
Diagnostics: artifacts8
NameSignatureWhat it does
sharedUse screenshot: 'only-on-failure' as const, video: 'retain-on-failure' as const, trace: 'retain-on-failure' as const Diagnostics are captured only for failing tests, so a green run produces nothing to open. These three are spread into the browser projects only — the `api` project overrides `use` entirely and gets none of them.→ n/a (config object spread into the UI projects)
outputDir outputDir: PATHS.testResults Where Playwright writes the failure artifacts: `test-results/<test folder>/` holds `trace.zip`, the video and the failure screenshot. Open a trace with `npx playwright show-trace test-results/<test>/trace.zip` (or `npm run trace <path>`).→ n/a (config)
snapshotPathTemplate snapshotPathTemplate: '{testDir}/__screenshots__/{projectName}/{testFileName}/{arg}{ext}' Visual baselines live beside their spec under `tests/visual/__screenshots__/`, deliberately separate from failure screenshots; re-baseline with `npm run test:visual:update`.→ n/a (config)
takeScreenshot public async takeScreenshot(name: string): Promise<Buffer> A screenshot you ask for explicitly — it lands in `reports/screenshots/`, NOT in `test-results/`, and is not attached to the Playwright report. Siblings: `fullPageScreenshot` writes `<name>-full.png`, `elementScreenshot` writes `<name>-element.png`.→ the PNG buffer, and writes `reports/screenshots/<name>.png`
PATHS export const PATHS = { root, config, environments, testData, storage, authState, reports, extentReport, playwrightReport, jsonReport, junitReport, screenshots, videos, traces, testResults, logs, downloads, uploads, snapshots } as const The one place every artifact location is defined: `logs/`, `reports/extent`, `reports/playwright`, `reports/json`, `reports/junit`, `reports/screenshots`, `reports/downloads`, `test-results/`, `storage/auth`.→ absolute paths resolved from the constants file, not from `process.cwd()`
REQUIRED_DIRECTORIES export const REQUIRED_DIRECTORIES: readonly string[] = [PATHS.authState, PATHS.extentReport, PATHS.screenshots, PATHS.downloads, PATHS.logs] The directories global setup guarantees exist via `ensureFrameworkDirectories` before a run starts — which is why these five reappear after `npm run clean`.→ n/a (constant)
collectAttachments private collectAttachments(test: TestCase, result: TestResult): ExtentAttachment[] How screenshots, videos and traces reach the Extent report: each attachment is copied next to the report and typed by whether its name contains `screenshot`, `video` or `trace`. A copy failure prints `[ExtentReporter] could not copy attachment <name>: <message>` to stderr and the run continues.→ ExtentAttachment[] copied into `<reportDir>/attachments/`
reportDir this.reportDir = resolve(PATHS.extentReport, `run-${toFileStamp(new Date())}`) Each run gets a timestamped folder under `reports/extent/`, plus `reports/extent/latest.html` and `latest.json` pointing at the newest one. Open with `npm run report:open` (Extent) or `npm run report` (Playwright HTML).→ n/a (field)
Diagnostics: retries2
NameSignatureWhat it does
<description> failed after <n> attempt(s) export async function withRetry<T>(operation: () => Promise<T>, options: RetryOptions = {}): Promise<T> Wraps a retried operation's final failure so you can see every attempt, not just the last. Before each retry it also logs `<description> failed, retrying in <n>ms` at WARN — grepping the log for `retrying in` shows flakiness the report hides.→ throws FrameworkError whose context includes `attempts: string[]` — one `attempt N: <message>` entry per try
Polled value never satisfied the condition export async function pollUntil<T>(operation: () => Promise<T>, until: (value: T) => boolean, options: RetryOptions & { readonly intervalMs?: number } = {}): Promise<T> Eventual consistency never arrived; `attempts` is the cap that was used (default 5) and `actual` is the last value seen, truncated to 500 characters.→ throws FrameworkError (never returns)
Common UI timeouts (WaitUtils)4
NameSignatureWhat it does
Timed out waiting for condition throws UiActionError with { operation: 'waitForCondition', target: description, expected: 'predicate to return true', timeout } A custom polled predicate never returned true inside the budget (default `DEFAULT_TIMEOUTS.shortPoll`, 5s); pass `description` so the error names what you were waiting for.→ throws UiActionError, wrapping the last predicate error as the cause
Timed out waiting for API response export async function waitForApiResponse(page: Page, urlFragment: string, options: WaitOptions & { readonly status?: number } = {}): Promise<Response> No response matched the URL fragment (and optional status) within the navigation timeout; `target` is the fragment and `expected` is `status <n>` or `any response`, so a fragment typo is easy to spot.→ throws UiActionError (never returns)
Page never reached network idle export async function waitForNetworkIdle(page: Page, options: WaitOptions = {}): Promise<void> Something keeps requesting — polling, a websocket, analytics. Prefer waiting on the specific response instead of idling the page.→ throws UiActionError (never returns)
Value never stabilised export async function waitForStableValue<T>(read: () => Promise<T>, options: WaitOptions & { readonly stableForMs?: number } = {}): Promise<T> A debounced value kept changing for the whole budget; raise the timeout or lower `stableForMs` (default 300).→ throws UiActionError with `expected: no change for <n>ms`

Users go looking for traces and videos in `reports/traces` and `reports/videos` because `PATHS.traces` and `PATHS.videos` exist in FrameworkConstants — and find them empty.
Nothing writes to those two constants; grep confirms they are declared and never referenced. Playwright's `outputDir` is `PATHS.testResults`, so failure traces, videos and screenshots all land under `test-results/<test folder>/`. Open a trace with `npx playwright show-trace test-results/<test>/trace.zip`.
`--project=api` runs produce no trace, video or failure screenshot at all.
The `api` project sets `use: { baseURL: environment.api.baseUrl }` and does not spread `sharedUse`, so it inherits none of the `screenshot`/`video`/`trace` settings. Diagnose API failures from the log (`LOG_LEVEL=DEBUG VERBOSE_API_LOGGING=true`) and from the ApiRequestError context instead.
`logs/` fills with hundreds of files and no single file holds the whole run.
`runId` defaults to `new Date().toISOString()` computed per process, so global setup, each worker and teardown each open their own `logs/run-<timestamp>.log`. Set `RUN_ID=<something>` for the run and every process appends to one file.
Setting `LOG_LEVEL=DEBUG` on CI still shows no API request/response bodies.
Two independent switches gate them. `verboseApiLogging` defaults to `!isCi` (off on CI) and only controls whether bodies are attached; the line itself is emitted at DEBUG. Set both: `LOG_LEVEL=DEBUG VERBOSE_API_LOGGING=true`.
A misspelled `LOG_LEVEL` (e.g. `debug` lowercase, or `TRACE`) appears to be ignored.
`configuredLevel` falls back to `'INFO'` when the value is not in `LOG_LEVELS`, silently. Use exactly `DEBUG`, `INFO`, `WARN` or `ERROR`.
Screenshots taken with `takeScreenshot()` do not appear in the Playwright HTML report or the Extent report.
They are written directly to `reports/screenshots/<name>.png` by BasePage, not registered as a Playwright attachment. Only Playwright's own failure artifacts get collected by `ExtentReporter.collectAttachments`. Use `testInfo.attach` if you need one in the report.
A configuration failure produces a bare error with no operation/target/url block, unlike every other framework error.
`EnvironmentConfigurationError extends Error`, not `FrameworkError`. It is thrown while `config/environment.config.ts` loads — before Playwright starts — so the whole diagnosis is in the message string, and no run, report or log file is produced.
`Stored session is unavailable` right after a previous green run.
Global teardown calls `clearStorageStates` for ADMIN, MANAGER, EMPLOYEE, STUDENT, MENTOR on every run unless `KEEP_AUTH_STATE` is `1|true|yes`, because the files hold live tokens. Re-run so global setup regenerates them, or set `KEEP_AUTH_STATE=true` locally.
A role logs in again mid-session even though `storage/auth/<env>.<role>.v1.json` exists.
`hasFreshStorageState` requires the file to be under `MAX_STATE_AGE_MS` (45 * 60 * 1000) old AND `frameworkConfig.reuseAuthState` to be true. A run longer than 45 minutes, or `REUSE_AUTH_STATE=false`, re-mints the session.
An API test fails with `API request failed` and it is unclear whether the call was even retried.
Retries only apply to `IDEMPOTENT_METHODS` (`GET, HEAD, OPTIONS, PUT, DELETE`) unless you pass `maxAttempts`, and only for 429/500/502/503 or a connection error matching `/ECONNRESET|ECONNREFUSED|socket hang up|timeout/i`. Read the `attempts` key in the error context — it lists `attempt N: <message>` for each try — and grep the log for the WARN line `<description> failed, retrying in <n>ms`.
A failing assertion on an API response gives no operation/target/url context block.
ResponseValidator failures are Playwright `expect` failures, not FrameworkErrors. Their diagnostic value is the message prefix `${method} ${url}` plus `payloadPreview` — the first 500 characters of the response body. If you need a thrown, context-carrying error instead, use `ensureSchema` (ValidationError) rather than `matchesSchema`.
The Extent report is missing after a run, or `latest.html` shows an older run.
Two separate causes. A CLI `--reporter=` flag overrides the configured reporter list entirely — run without it, or keep `EXTENT_REPORT=true`. Separately, when zero tests executed (a global-setup failure, `--list`, a grep that matched nothing) the reporter deliberately refuses to overwrite `latest.html` and prints `no tests were executed (run status: <status>) — reports/extent/latest.html still points at the previous run`.
Opening a copied `reports/extent/latest.html` shows broken screenshot/video/trace links.
`latest.html` lives one directory above the attachments and is rendered with the run folder as an asset prefix. Move or zip the whole `reports/extent/` tree, or open `reports/extent/run-<stamp>/index.html` directly — that copy resolves attachments relative to itself.
Secrets are expected in the log but every token reads `***REDACTED***`, making a token-related failure hard to confirm.
This is intentional: `Logger.write` passes both message and payload through `maskString`/`maskValue`, and `ApiClient` masks headers and URLs. The list of masked keys is `SENSITIVE_KEYS` in `src/constants/FrameworkConstants.ts` and the replacement is `MASKED_VALUE`. Verify auth by the HTTP status and the `actual` field of `API login failed`, not by reading the token.
`npm run clean` appears to have deleted the visual baselines.
It does not — `scripts/clean.mjs` removes `reports/*`, `test-results`, `playwright-report`, `logs` and `storage/auth`, and explicitly leaves `tests/visual/__screenshots__` alone. It also recreates `logs`, `storage/auth` and `reports` with a `.gitkeep`, which is why those folders reappear immediately.
Global setup fails on a dataset key before any test runs, and the failure looks unrelated to the test being debugged.
`assertDatasetKeys` runs three fail-fast checks in global setup: `login` (`validUsers, invalidScenarios, ui`), `employees` (`templates, departments, validation`), `api` (`endpoints, performance, negative`). The `actual: missing: <list>` line names the key; add it to `test-data/common/<name>.json` or the environment override.
A UI error shows `url: (page closed)` and looks like a framework bug.
`BasePage.safeUrl()` returns the literal `'(page closed)'` when `page.url()` throws. It means the failure was raised after the page or context was disposed — look at the fixture teardown order, not at the locator.
A `Retryable status received` error appears in the log and is mistaken for the real failure.
It is an internal control-flow signal thrown inside `withRetry` so the client backs off on a 429/500/502/503. The user-facing error is the `API request failed` that follows, whose `attempts` array contains this message as one entry.

The two base classes

2 classes · 85 methods

BasePage

src/pages/BasePage.ts
The two base classes— (abstract root class; implements no interface)974 ln6 props81 methods

BasePage is the single home for every reusable browser interaction in the framework: navigation, clicks, typing, dropdowns, checkboxes, element-state probes, text/attribute extraction, mouse work, uploads and downloads, native dialogs, tabs, iframes, screenshots, scrolling, network interception and localStorage reads. It knows nothing about any application screen — subclasses add only locators and business workflows. Its file header states the three conventions it enforces: Playwright auto-waiting is the only waiting strategy (no sleeps), every action logs `action -> target` at DEBUG and wraps failures in a UiActionError carrying operation/target/page/URL, and every action accepts either a Locator or a selector string. docs/ARCHITECTURE.md explains the size deliberately: 'BasePage is large on purpose' — a finite, shared interaction vocabulary centralised once so teams do not reinvent `clickAndWaitForNavigation` slightly differently and turn the differences into flakiness.

OwnsOwn every generic browser interaction, uniformly logged and uniformly wrapped in a debuggable UiActionError, so that no Page Object or spec ever calls raw Playwright.
Constructor
constructor(page: Page)
Properties6
Fields6
pro page: Page The Playwright page every action runs against; readonly, assigned in the constructor.
pro log: Logger Logger created with `createLogger(new.target.name)`, so it is named after the concrete subclass (e.g. 'LoginPage'), not 'BasePage'.
pro environment: ResolvedEnvironment Result of `getEnvironment()`; supplies `ui.baseUrl`, `timeouts.action`, `timeouts.navigation`, `name` and `credentialsFor(role)`. Assigned before any subclass field initialiser runs.
pro path: string ABSTRACT — the application path this page owns (e.g. '/employees'). Used by navigate(). A subclass supplies it either as an initialiser (EmployeePage: `protected readonly path = '/employees'`) or by assigning from the environment in its constructor (LoginPage: `this.path = this.environment.ui.loginPath`).
pub rootIndicator: Locator ABSTRACT, public readonly — an element whose presence proves this page is rendered. Used by waitUntilLoaded() and isLoaded(). Every existing page assigns it to its main heading.
pub rawPage: Page (get accessor) Getter returning the underlying Playwright page, 'for the rare case a caller needs raw access'. Specs use it for waitForRequest and toHaveScreenshot.
Methods81
internals4
pro protected locator(target: Target): Locator Normalises a Target into a Locator: a string becomes `this.page.locator(string)`, a Locator is returned unchanged.
pro protected describe(target: Target, fallback?: string): string Builds the human label used in logs and errors: `fallback ?? (typeof target === 'string' ? target : String(target))`.
pro protected async perform<T>(operation: string, target: Target | undefined, action: () => Promise<T>, options: ActionOptions = {}): Promise<T> The wrapper behind every action: logs `operation -> label` at DEBUG, awaits the callback, and on failure re-throws a UiActionError with operation, target, page (constructor name), url, environment and timeout, preserving the cause. Never swallows an error.
pri private safeUrl(): string Returns page.url(), or the literal '(page closed)' when reading the URL throws — so error construction can never fail.
navigation9
pub public async navigate(pathOverride?: string, options: ActionOptions = {}): Promise<void> Goes to `environment.ui.baseUrl` + path (this.path unless overridden), waitUntil 'domcontentloaded', navigation timeout. Does not wait for rootIndicator.
pub public async open(pathOverride?: string): Promise<this> navigate() then waitUntilLoaded(), returning `this` for chaining. The method specs actually call.
pub public async waitUntilLoaded(options: ActionOptions = {}): Promise<void> Waits for rootIndicator to reach state 'visible' using the navigation timeout.
pub public async isLoaded(timeout = DEFAULT_TIMEOUTS.shortPoll): Promise<boolean> True when rootIndicator becomes visible within the timeout; catches and returns false. Never throws, for conditional flows.
pub public async reload(): Promise<void> page.reload({ waitUntil: 'domcontentloaded' }).
pub public async goBack(): Promise<void> page.goBack({ waitUntil: 'domcontentloaded' }).
pub public async goForward(): Promise<void> page.goForward({ waitUntil: 'domcontentloaded' }).
pub public getCurrentUrl(): string Synchronous page.url(). Not wrapped by perform — no logging, no error enrichment.
pub public async getTitle(): Promise<string> page.title(). Not wrapped by perform.

pub public async click(target: Target, options: ClickOptions = {}): Promise<void> Clicks with the action timeout; honours force (default false), clickCount (default 1), and optional position and modifiers.
pub public async doubleClick(target: Target, options: ClickOptions = {}): Promise<void> locator.dblclick() with the action timeout. Ignores force/clickCount/position/modifiers from ClickOptions.
pub public async rightClick(target: Target, options: ClickOptions = {}): Promise<void> locator.click({ button: 'right' }) with the action timeout.
pub public async forceClick(target: Target, options: ClickOptions = {}): Promise<void> Delegates to click() with force: true, bypassing actionability checks. The doc comment warns it is only for elements an overlay legitimately covers.
pub public async clickByText(text: string, options: ClickOptions & { readonly exact?: boolean } = {}): Promise<void> Clicks `page.getByText(text, { exact: options.exact ?? false }).first()`, logging description `text="…"`.
pub public async clickAndWaitForNavigation(target: Target, options: ClickOptions & { readonly urlPattern?: string | RegExp } = {}): Promise<void> Promise.all of page.waitForURL(urlPattern ?? /.*/, navigation timeout, waitUntil 'domcontentloaded') and the click (action timeout).
pub public async clickAndWaitForResponse(target: Target, urlFragment: string, options: ClickOptions = {}): Promise<Response> Clicks and returns the first response whose URL includes urlFragment; the wait uses the navigation timeout, the click the action timeout.
