Those subclasses are instantiated only in fixtures — src/fixtures/page.fixture.ts (loginPage, dashboardPage, employeePage, profilePage) and src/fixtures/auth.fixture.ts (dashboardAs, employeesAs, profileAs bound to the authenticated page) — and specs receive them ready-made. Inherited methods are called both inside the subclasses (LoginPage.submitCredentials uses fill/check/click; DashboardPage uses uploadMultipleFiles, downloadFile, acceptDialog, dismissDialog, switchToNewTab, interactWithFrame, getText, getAllTexts; EmployeePage uses clearAndFill, selectByValue, setChecked, click) and directly from specs (tests/ui/regression/network.regression.spec.ts uses mockJsonResponse/abortRequests/clearRoutes/rawPage; tests/ui/sanity/dashboard.sanity.spec.ts uses open/closeTab/rawPage; tests/hybrid/employee-hybrid.spec.ts and tests/ui/regression/employee-management.regression.spec.ts use reload; tests/visual/login.visual.spec.ts uses open and rawPage). Exported from the barrel src/pages/index.ts together with its Target/ActionOptions/ClickOptions/TypeOptions types.

Worth knowing18
  • `path` and `rootIndicator` are the only two members a subclass MUST supply. Both supply patterns in the repo are valid because the BasePage constructor assigns `this.environment` before any subclass field initialiser runs: EmployeePage/ProfilePage use an initialiser (`protected readonly path = '/employees'`), LoginPage/DashboardPage assign in the constructor from config (`this.path = this.environment.ui.loginPath`).
  • The logger is created with `createLogger(new.target.name)`, so log lines are tagged with the CONCRETE subclass name ('LoginPage', 'EmployeePage'), never 'BasePage'.
  • Delegating methods log under the delegate's operation name, so grepping a log for them finds nothing: forceClick logs 'click'; clickByText logs 'click' with description `text="…"`; pressEnter/pressTab log 'press'; handlePopup logs 'switchToNewTab'.
  • Boolean probes are deliberately inconsistent. isLoaded, isVisible and isHidden bypass perform() — they swallow the timeout, return false, and produce no log line and no UiActionError. isEnabled, isDisabled, isEditable and isChecked DO go through perform(), so a missing element makes them throw rather than return false.
  • Several readers silently apply `.first()`: isVisible, isHidden, getText, getAttribute, getInputValue. So getText on a locator matching ten rows returns row one rather than failing. getAllTexts, getCount and getOptionLabels operate on the whole match set.
  • Trimming is not uniform: getText, getAllTexts, getSelectedOptionText and getOptionLabels trim; getInputValue does not.
  • Timeout defaulting has three tiers. Most actions fall back to `environment.timeouts.action`. Navigation-flavoured waits use `environment.timeouts.navigation` (navigate, waitUntilLoaded, the URL wait in clickAndWaitForNavigation, clickAndWaitForResponse, downloadFile, waitForDownload, switchToNewTab). The three selectBy* methods pass `{ timeout: options.timeout }` straight to Playwright with NO framework default, so omitting the option falls back to Playwright's own default rather than the environment's.
  • perform() always records `options.timeout ?? this.environment.timeouts.action` in the UiActionError context, regardless of which timeout the action actually applied — the `timeout:` line on a navigation failure can therefore understate the real budget.
  • navigate() only waits for 'domcontentloaded' and does NOT wait for rootIndicator. open() is navigate() + waitUntilLoaded() and returns `this`, which is why every spec calls open() rather than navigate().
  • Route handlers from abortRequests and mockJsonResponse persist on the page for the remainder of the test; the network regression spec calls clearRoutes() explicitly at the end of each test that installs one.
  • getFrame() and frameByName() are synchronous and are not wrapped by perform(). getFrame never validates that the iframe exists; frameByName constructs and throws its own UiActionError listing every frame URL in `actual`.
  • Screenshot helpers are diagnostics, not assertions: they write into `PATHS.screenshots` (reports/screenshots) as `<name>.png`, `<name>-full.png` and `<name>-element.png` and return the Buffer. Visual baselines use `expect(...).toHaveScreenshot()` against tests/visual/__screenshots__ instead (tests/visual/login.visual.spec.ts).
  • saveDownload names the file from `download.suggestedFilename()` under reports/downloads, so two downloads suggesting the same name overwrite one another.
  • acceptDialog/dismissDialog register `page.once('dialog', …)` and capture the message inside the handler. If the trigger never opens a dialog the method resolves with an empty string rather than failing — assert on the returned message (dashboard.sanity.spec.ts compares it against test data).
  • clickAndWaitForNavigation defaults urlPattern to `/.*/`, which the CURRENT url already matches, so with no pattern the wait can resolve without a real navigation. Pass urlPattern whenever the destination matters.
  • clearAndFill performs four interactions (click, ControlOrMeta+a, Delete, fill) — it is not a silent drop-in for fill on inputs with click side effects. type() uses pressSequentially with a 25 ms default per-character delay.
  • getLocalStorageItem runs page.evaluate against the current origin, so it is only meaningful after navigating to the app (LoginPage.hasSessionToken reads 'pk.auth.token' this way).
  • rawPage is the sanctioned escape hatch and is used as such: `employeesAs.rawPage.waitForRequest(...)` in network.regression.spec.ts and `expect(loginPage.rawPage).toHaveScreenshot(...)` in login.visual.spec.ts.

BaseComponent

src/components/BaseComponent.ts
The two base classes— (abstract root class; implements no interface)77 ln4 props4 methods

BaseComponent is the root of the Component Object Model. A component owns a *region* of a screen — a header, a table, a modal, a toast region — and is scoped to a root Locator supplied at construction. Every internal locator descends from that root, so a markup change to a region is a one-file change no matter how many screens render it. It gives subclasses the same four collaborators BasePage gives Page Objects (page, log, environment, plus the root locator) and one protected wrapper, perform(), that logs `action -> target` and re-throws failures as an enriched UiActionError. docs/ARCHITECTURE.md states the relationship explicitly: pages *compose* components, they do not inherit from them.

OwnsAnchor a screen region to a single root Locator and give its subclasses uniformly logged, uniformly error-wrapped scoped interactions.

pro environment: ResolvedEnvironment Result of getEnvironment(); components use it mainly for `environment.timeouts.navigation` on response waits (SearchComponent) and for `environment.name` in the error context.
pub root: Locator PUBLIC readonly — the element the component is scoped to. The documented contract is that every internal locator descends from it. Being public is deliberate: pages assert on it and visual tests mask it.

internals1
pro protected async perform<T>(operation: string, target: string, action: () => Promise<T>): Promise<T> Logs `operation -> target` at DEBUG, awaits the callback, and on failure re-throws a UiActionError reading `Component action "<operation>" failed` with operation, target, page (constructor name), url and environment, preserving the cause.

pub public async isVisible(timeout = DEFAULT_TIMEOUTS.shortPoll): Promise<boolean> True when the component's root reaches state 'visible' within the timeout; catches and returns false. Bypasses perform(), so it neither logs nor throws.
pub public async waitUntilVisible(timeout = DEFAULT_TIMEOUTS.shortPoll): Promise<void> Web-first `expect(this.root).toBeVisible({ timeout })` inside perform(), logged with `String(this.root)` as the target; a timeout surfaces as a UiActionError.
pub public async waitUntilHidden(timeout = DEFAULT_TIMEOUTS.shortPoll): Promise<void> Web-first `expect(this.root).toBeHidden({ timeout })` inside perform(), logged the same way.
Used by

Extended by all eight components: src/components/DatePickerComponent.ts:13, HeaderComponent.ts:7, ModalComponent.ts:20, PaginationComponent.ts:14, SearchComponent.ts:21, SidebarComponent.ts:14, TableComponent.ts:27, ToastComponent.ts:10. Every one is constructed from a Page inside a Page Object constructor, never in a spec — LoginPage builds a ToastComponent; DashboardPage builds Header/Sidebar/Toast; ProfilePage builds Header/Sidebar; EmployeePage builds Header, Sidebar, Toast, TableComponent, SearchComponent, PaginationComponent, two ModalComponents and a DatePickerComponent (src/pages/EmployeePage.ts:61-73). The inherited protected perform() is the workhorse: it is called throughout HeaderComponent, SidebarComponent, ModalComponent, TableComponent, PaginationComponent, SearchComponent, ToastComponent and DatePickerComponent. The public `root` is consumed from pages and specs — `expect(this.header.root).toBeVisible()` (DashboardPage.expectLoaded), `expect(this.table.root).toBeVisible()` (EmployeePage.expectLoaded), `mask: [employeesAs.table.rows, employeesAs.pagination.summary]` (tests/visual/login.visual.spec.ts). Exported from the barrel src/components/index.ts.

Worth knowing9
  • perform() here is NOT the same method as BasePage.perform(). Its `target` is a plain string label (the convention across the repo is `'header.userName'`, `'table.rows'`, `'modal.title'`, `'sidebar."<label>"'`), it takes no options argument, and there is no timeout in the error context. Copying a BasePage perform() call into a component will not compile.
  • BaseComponent.perform's catch block calls `this.page.url()` directly, while BasePage guards the same read behind a private safeUrl() that returns '(page closed)'. If a component action fails because the page was already closed, building the error can itself throw and mask the original failure.
  • There are no abstract members. A subclass only has to call `super(page, root)`. The convention every subclass follows is to accept an options object with an optional `root` override and fall back to a testid or role locator (`super(page, options.root ?? page.getByTestId(options.testId ?? 'employee-table'))` in TableComponent), then derive every child locator from `this.root`.
  • The three inherited public methods all default to `DEFAULT_TIMEOUTS.shortPoll` (5 000 ms from src/constants/FrameworkConstants.ts) — a framework constant, never `environment.timeouts`. Only the subclasses' own response waits consult `this.environment.timeouts.navigation`.
  • As of this revision none of isVisible, waitUntilVisible or waitUntilHidden is called anywhere in src/ or tests/. Subclasses write their own web-first assertions instead (ModalComponent.expectOpen/expectClosed, SidebarComponent.expectAvailable) and call `this.root.isVisible()` — Playwright's Locator method, not the inherited one — for conditional branches. In practice, inheriting from BaseComponent buys page/log/environment/root plus perform().
  • `root` is public on purpose and is part of the component's contract: pages assert against it and visual tests mask it. Do not make it protected in a subclass.
  • isVisible swallows the timeout and returns false; waitUntilVisible/waitUntilHidden use web-first expect and therefore throw a UiActionError wrapping the assertion failure.
  • The log name comes from `createLogger(new.target.name)`, so it is the concrete component's class name, and the UiActionError context uses `this.constructor.name` for its `page` field — meaning a component failure reports the COMPONENT name (e.g. 'TableComponent') under the key `page`, not the screen it was composed into.
  • Components are constructed with a `Page`, never with a Page Object, which is what keeps them reusable across screens (ToastComponent is built independently by LoginPage, DashboardPage and EmployeePage).

EmployeePage

src/pages/EmployeePage.ts
Page ObjectsBasePage (abstract, src/pages/BasePage.ts)217 ln21 props18 methods

The employee management screen and the framework's richest page object. Its file header states the intent: it composes the table, search, pagination, modal, date-picker and toast components and exposes business-level workflows (`createEmployee`, `updateEmployee`, `deleteEmployee`) so specs read as workflows rather than DOM scripts. It owns two distinct modals — the add/edit form and the delete confirmation — and scopes every form field to the form modal's root so the filter bar's own "Department" control cannot be hit by accident.

OwnsTurn the employee directory's CRUD, search/filter and table interactions into named business workflows over composed components.

The exported `EmployeeFormInput` interface is re-exported from src/pages/index.ts.

Worth knowing11
  • Every form-field locator is scoped to `this.formModal.root`, which is evaluated at construction time as a Locator (lazy). They resolve nothing until the form modal is open — reading `nameInput` on a closed page will time out, not return empty.
  • `EmployeeFormInput extends EmployeeCreateRequest` (src/types/ApiModels.ts:84) and adds only `readonly active?: boolean`. So `name`, `email`, `department`, `designation` are required; `salary`, `joiningDate`, `status` optional — and `status` has no field on this form, it is silently ignored by `fillEmployeeForm`.
  • `attemptInvalidCreate` leaves the form modal OPEN and returns `''` rather than throwing when `getErrorMessage()` yields null. The regression spec closes it explicitly with `employeesAs.formModal.cancel()` afterwards.
  • `deleteEmployee` deliberately does NOT assert a success toast (unlike `createEmployee`/`updateEmployee`); specs assert `toast.expectSuccess('Employee deleted')` themselves right after the call.
  • `department` is set with `selectByValue`, i.e. matched against the option's **value** attribute, not its visible label.
  • `salary` is coerced with `String(input.salary)`; a number like `1_650_000` is typed as `1650000`, with no formatting.
  • `expectEmployeeRow` checks four columns only — Name, Email, Department, Designation. Salary and joining date are not verified by it.
  • `getEmployeeIdByName` throws a plain `Error`, not a `UiActionError`, so it will not carry the framework's page/URL/environment diagnostics.
  • `table.clickRowAction(rowText, actionName)` (used by `openEditForm`, `deleteEmployee`, `cancelDelete`) matches the row by `hasText` substring and the button by `new RegExp('^' + actionName, 'i')`. A name that is a substring of another employee's name can select the wrong row.
  • `path` is the literal `'/employees'` here, so `open()` ignores any environment override for this screen — unlike LoginPage and DashboardPage.
  • The two `ModalComponent` instances are both built from an explicit `root` test id rather than by role, because the screen can have two dialogs; do not assume `getByRole('dialog')` semantics.

The landing screen after sign-in: workforce KPI tiles, a recent-hires list, onboarding document upload, CSV export, a destructive workspace reset guarded by a native dialog, a link that opens employees in a second tab, and a compliance widget rendered inside an iframe. It is the page that demonstrates the framework's harder browser capabilities (downloads, native dialogs, multi-tab, iframes) behind business-named methods. It also exposes `openAndCaptureSource()`, which exists specifically so a metric assertion can be made against the exact payload the page rendered from rather than a second API call a parallel worker may have changed in between.

The sign-in screen. It owns every locator on the login form plus the four things a spec ever wants to do with it: submit credentials, sign in successfully, sign in as a named role, or submit credentials expecting rejection. Its file header states the design rule it enforces: credentials are never passed in from a spec as literals — a test names a role and the page resolves the secret through the environment (env vars / CI secrets) via `this.environment.credentialsFor(role)`. It is also the class the framework's session bootstrap runs through, so a stored storage-state file is produced exactly the way a real user produces one.

Worth knowing8
  • `login()` and therefore `loginAs()` will fail on bad credentials, because they wait for the dashboard URL. Negative paths must use `attemptInvalidLogin()` (or `submitCredentials()`), not `login()` inside a try/catch.
  • `rememberMe` only ever *checks*: the body is `if (rememberMe) await this.check(this.rememberMeCheckbox);`. Passing `false` does not untick an already-ticked box — it is a no-op.
  • `errorMessage` is not the toast. It is scoped to `getByRole('main')` precisely because the toast region also publishes `role="alert"`; use `loginPage.toast` for the transient notification and `loginPage.errorMessage` for the inline one. tests/visual/login.visual.spec.ts:29 calls `loginPage.toast.waitUntilCleared()` before screenshotting for exactly this reason.
  • `rootIndicator` and `heading` are the *same* Locator instance, not two locators that happen to match. Changing the heading selector changes what `waitUntilLoaded()` waits for.
  • `hasSessionToken()` hard-codes the key `'pk.auth.token'`. That matches `STORAGE_KEYS.token` in demo-app/public/app.js:3; it is not read from configuration.
  • `path` is *not* a literal on this class. Unlike EmployeePage and ProfilePage it is declared untyped-in-body and assigned from `environment.ui.loginPath` in the constructor, so it follows the environment JSON.
  • LoginPage composes only `ToastComponent`. It has no `header` or `sidebar` — those do not exist on the signed-out screen.
  • Every inherited BasePage action (`fill`, `click`, `check`, `getText`, `getLocalStorageItem`, …) runs through `perform()`, which logs `action -> target` and re-throws failures as `UiActionError` carrying operation, target, page class name, URL, environment and timeout.

EmployeePage itself wraps it in expectEmployeeVisible/expectEmployeeAbsent/expectEmployeeRow/getVisibleEmployeeNames/getEmployeeIdByName.

Worth knowing13
  • Options interface `TableOptions` (exported): `testId?: string` (test id of the table root), `root?: Locator` (explicit root when the table has no test id), `rowTestId?: string` (test id applied to each body row), `emptyState?: Locator` (the "no results" panel that replaces rows). All four are optional and readonly; the whole object defaults to `{}`.
  • Root locator strategy: `options.root ?? page.getByTestId(options.testId ?? 'employee-table')`. The 'employee-table' fallback is an application-specific default baked into a nominally generic component — a table on another screen must pass `testId` or `root`.
  • Row strategy branches on `rowTestId`: with it, rows are `root.getByTestId(rowTestId)`; without it, `root.locator('tbody tr')`, which would also pick up rows in a second/footer tbody.
  • Only 7 of the 21 public methods go through `perform` (getRowCount, getColumnCount, getHeaders, getCell, getCellByRowText, clickRowAction, sortByColumn). The rest — including every `expect*`, getRowData, getAllRowData, getColumnValues and isColumnSorted — emit no action log and surface raw Playwright errors rather than a UiActionError carrying page/url/environment.
  • `sortByColumn` returns the raw `aria-sort` attribute — 'ascending', 'descending' or 'none' — NOT 'asc'/'desc'. Callers must translate before feeding `isColumnSorted`, as the regression spec does with `first === 'ascending' ? 'asc' : 'desc'`. It also requires a <button> inside the <th> and asserts `aria-sort` matches /ascending|descending/, so a header that never publishes the attribute fails inside the component.
  • `expectRowMatching` is a subset + substring match, not equality: keys are lowercased on both sides and each value is tested with `String.includes`, so `{ Salary: '1' }` passes against a formatted `₹1,20,000`. A header key that does not exist compares against '' and therefore fails unless the expected value is empty.
  • `getColumnIndex` matches the trimmed header text case-insensitively but exactly — 'name' works, 'Employee Name' does not — and it is called outside the `perform` wrapper by getCell/getCellByRowText, so a missing column throws its own UiActionError ('Column not found', with `actual: available columns: …`) rather than a wrapped "Component action failed".
  • `isColumnSorted` compares the rendered strings, so a currency-, date- or badge-formatted column is judged by display text, not underlying value.
  • `getAllRowData` reads rows sequentially and `getRowData` re-fetches `getHeaders()` on every call — N+1 DOM round trips on a wide grid, and not an atomic snapshot if the grid re-renders mid-loop.
  • `getColumnValues` and `rowByColumnValue` address cells positionally with `td:nth-child(index + 1)`, assuming header count and <td> count line up (no colspan/rowspan). `rowByColumnValue` builds its `has:` sub-locator from `this.page`, but because `has:` is evaluated relative to each candidate row it still scopes correctly.
  • `isEmpty()` short-circuits to true as soon as the optional `emptyState` is visible; without an `emptyState` it is purely a row count. `expectEmpty()` asserts count 0 first and only then the panel, so an app that renders a "no results" placeholder *row* fails the count assertion.
  • `emptyState` is the only public property that can be `undefined` — guard before using it directly.
  • `TableRowData` is exported as `type TableRowData = Record<string, string>` — one row as a `header -> cell text` map.

Worth knowing8
  • It is the odd one out among the four: there is NO options interface. The constructor takes a positional optional Locator — `constructor(page: Page, root?: Locator)` — so you pass the root directly, not `{ root }`. The exported interface `PaginationState { readonly page: number; readonly totalPages: number; readonly totalRecords: number }` is a return shape, not constructor options.
  • Root locator strategy: `root ?? page.locator('.pagination')` — a CSS class selector, so it breaks on a stylesheet rename in a way a test id would not. All four child locators are test-id based: `pagination-summary`, `pagination-previous`, `pagination-next`, `page-size`.
  • `getState()` is a scrape of the rendered summary, not an API count. Its regex /Page\s+(\d+)\s+of\s+(\d+).*?(\d+)\s+\w+/i requires a trailing "<number> <word>" pair after the page counts (the app renders `Page 1 of 4 · 37 employees`). A summary that omits the record total, or renders the count after the noun, throws UiActionError with `expected: 'Page <n> of <n> · <total> records'` and the actual text in the message.
  • goToNextPage/goToPreviousPage are self-synchronising and need no explicit wait after them: each asserts the button is enabled, reads the state, clicks, then asserts the summary contains the new `Page <n> of`. The cost is two extra summary reads per navigation, and because `getState()` is called inside the `perform` block, a parse failure surfaces as `Component action "goToNextPage" failed` wrapping the parse error.
  • `goToPage(target)` walks one page at a time (the bar has only Previous/Next, no numbered links) and re-reads the state on every iteration, so moving to page 10 costs ten navigations. Out-of-range targets throw UiActionError with `expected: '1..<totalPages>'` before any click.
  • `setPageSize(size)` calls `selectOption(String(size))`, which matches the <option> VALUE — it fails on a select whose values are labels rather than numbers — and then asserts `Page 1 of`, so it doubles as the wait for the grid to reload. Pair it with a row-count assertion when you need a fixed table height, as the visual suite does.
  • isFirstPage()/isLastPage() read the buttons' `disabled` attribute rather than computing from `getState()`. An app that hides or greys the edge buttons instead of disabling them reports false, and neither method is wrapped in `perform`.
  • `totalRecords` counts what the app says it has under the current filters, so it changes when a department filter or search term is applied — the hybrid spec asserts `state.totalRecords` only with `toBeGreaterThanOrEqual` because other suites add records in parallel.

Worth knowing13

  • The day is clicked by accessible name equal to the full ISO date: `this.grid.getByRole('button', { name: isoDate, exact: true })`.   • `selectMonthAndYear` maps the name with `MONTH_NAMES.indexOf(monthName)`. An unrecognised or differently-cased name yields `-1`, and the resulting `selectOption('-1')` fails with a generic select error rather than a clear "unknown month" message. `MONTH_NAMES` are full English names, `'January'`…`'December'` (`src/utils/DateUtils.ts` lines 74-87).

  • `selectRange` is an instance method that drives a **second** component instance passed as `endPicker`; there is no single-picker range mode. It returns exactly the two strings it was given, without reading the values back from the DOM.

  • `getValue()` is the one method that skips `BaseComponent.perform` — no action log, no `UiActionError` wrapping.

  • Options interface `ModalOptions` (exported): `name?: string` (accessible name of the dialog, when a screen renders more than one), `role?: 'dialog' | 'alertdialog'`, `root?: Locator` (explicit root when the dialog cannot be addressed by role). All readonly and optional; the object defaults to `{}`.
  • Root locator strategy: `options.root ?? page.getByRole(options.role ?? 'dialog', options.name ? { name: options.name } : {})`. Note the ternary passes a bare `{}` rather than `{ name: undefined }` when no name is given.
  • The role default is `dialog` only. A confirmation dialog rendered as `role="alertdialog"` (as the demo app's confirm-modal is) is invisible to the default and needs `role: 'alertdialog'` or an explicit `root` — which is why EmployeePage passes explicit roots for both of its dialogs: the app keeps both modals mounted in the DOM, so a bare `getByRole('dialog')` would risk a strict-mode violation.

  • `close()`, `cancel()` and `dismissWithEscape()` are not bare clicks — each asserts the root becomes hidden afterwards, so they fail loudly when validation keeps the dialog open. Use `clickButton()` when you expect the dialog to stay open.
  • `clickButton(name)` matches with `exact: false` (substring, case-insensitive) and does NOT call `.first()`, so two buttons whose accessible names both contain the string produce a strict-mode violation.
  • `getErrorMessage()` uses `isHidden()`, which resolves immediately without waiting, so it returns null for an error that has not rendered yet. Wait for visibility first — EmployeePage.attemptInvalidCreate does `await expect(this.formModal.errorMessage).toBeVisible()` before reading it.
  • `dismissWithEscape()` presses Escape on `page.keyboard`, not on the dialog element; focus must already sit where the app's key handler listens.
  • `getTitle()` takes the first `heading` role inside the dialog regardless of level; callers that need an exact match tend to assert on the `title` locator directly (`await expect(this.formModal.title).toHaveText('Add employee')`, EmployeePage.ts:93).

Wraps the employee filter bar — the free-text search box, the department `<select>` and the Clear button — into one object. Worth knowing10

  • The default fragment is `'/employees?'` **including the question mark**, so it matches only URLs that already carry a query string. A caller pointing this component at an endpoint that is fetched without a query string must override `requestFragment`.
  • All three waits use `this.environment.timeouts.navigation` (30 000 ms by default via `DEFAULT_TIMEOUTS.navigation`), not the action or expect timeout.
  • `search()` calls `this.input.fill(term)` — one value set, not per-character typing. The application debounces `input` events by 200 ms (`demo-app/public/employees.html`, `searchTimer`), and the component absorbs that by awaiting the response instead of sleeping.
  • `getSearchTerm()` and `getAvailableDepartments()` are the only two methods that do **not** go through `BaseComponent.perform`. They emit no `log.action` line and their failures surface as raw Playwright errors rather than a `UiActionError` carrying operation/target/url/environment context.
  • `getAvailableDepartments()` returns option **labels**, trimmed — including the placeholder `All departments` option — not option `value` attributes. Do not treat the first entry as a real department.
  • `filterByDepartment()` passes a bare string to `selectOption`, which Playwright matches against both an option's value and its label.
  • The default root is a CSS locator, `page.locator('section[aria-label="Employee filters"]')`, not a role locator. Locators are lazy, so a page missing that section fails at the first interaction, never at construction.
  • `clearFilters()` does more than click: after the response it asserts `expect(this.input).toHaveValue('')`, so it doubles as a check that the app really reset the box.
  • Every `SearchOptions` field is optional and readonly; a different screen can be supported by passing `root` plus new test ids and a matching `requestFragment` without subclassing.

  • `waitForMessage` returns the toast's entire trimmed text, not the fragment that matched.
  • The toast region publishes `role="alert"` for error toasts and `role="status"` otherwise; LoginPage deliberately scopes its own `errorMessage` to `getByRole('main')` because of this overlap (LoginPage.ts:39-40).

  • `logout()` waits for the login URL but does nothing about storage state — it neither clears nor asserts the session token. Specs verify that separately (e.g. `expect(await loginPage.hasSessionToken()).toBe(false)` in `tests/ui/e2e/employee-lifecycle.e2e.spec.ts`).
  • The identity spans are populated by the app's `mountShell()` (`demo-app/public/app.js`), so both getters return an empty string until the shell has mounted; `DashboardPage.expectLoaded()` guards against reading too early.
  • All four methods route through `BaseComponent.perform`, so each emits a `log.action` line and failures arrive as `UiActionError` with operation, target, page class, URL and environment attached. This is the only one of the four components with no un-wrapped method.
  • The file imports `type { Locator, Page }` only — it does not import `expect`, so the component itself contains no assertions; callers assert against the exposed locators.

ApiClient

src/api/clients/ApiClient.ts
Talking to the API296 ln9 props12 methods

ApiClient is the only place in the framework that actually performs an HTTP call. It wraps a Playwright `APIRequestContext` and adds everything a test-grade HTTP client needs: base-URL resolution from the resolved environment, default JSON headers, bearer/API-key authentication, `:name` path-parameter substitution, query-string building, per-call timeouts, a retry policy scoped to idempotent verbs, envelope parsing into a typed `ApiResponse<T>`, and masked request/response logging. Domain services (AuthApi, EmployeeApi, UserApi) call it; specs are expected to go through those services and only reach for the raw client for transport-level negative tests.

OwnsTurn a path plus RequestOptions into a parsed, typed, logged ApiResponse<T> — owning URL, headers, auth, timeout, retry and parsing.

HTTP verbs5
pub public async get<T>(path: string, options: RequestOptions = {}): Promise<ApiResponse<T>> Delegates to send<T>('GET', path, options). Idempotent, so it uses the client's retry policy.
pub public async post<T>(path: string, options: RequestOptions = {}): Promise<ApiResponse<T>> Delegates to send<T>('POST', …). NOT in IDEMPOTENT_METHODS, so it defaults to a single attempt.
pub public async put<T>(path: string, options: RequestOptions = {}): Promise<ApiResponse<T>> Delegates to send<T>('PUT', …). Idempotent, so it retries.
pub public async patch<T>(path: string, options: RequestOptions = {}): Promise<ApiResponse<T>> Delegates to send<T>('PATCH', …). NOT idempotent by this client's list, so a single attempt.
pub public async delete<T>(path: string, options: RequestOptions = {}): Promise<ApiResponse<T>> Delegates to send<T>('DELETE', …). Idempotent, so it retries.
Internals4
pri private buildUrl(path: string, options: RequestOptions): string Substitutes each pathParams entry into its `:name` placeholder (URL-encoded), throws ApiRequestError('Unresolved path parameter') if any `:name` remains, then appends query entries, skipping values that are undefined or ''.
pri private buildHeaders(options: RequestOptions): Record<string, string> Merges defaultHeaders with options.headers, then adds Authorization: Bearer <token> or x-api-key (when useApiKey and environment.apiKey() resolves); with skipAuth it deletes both auth headers. Adds x-correlation-id when correlationId is supplied.
pri private async send<T>(method: HttpMethod, path: string, options: RequestOptions): Promise<ApiResponse<T>> Builds URL/headers, resolves timeout and attempt count, logs the masked request, runs request.fetch inside withRetry, converts any failure into ApiRequestError('API request failed'), and hands the raw response to parse() with the elapsed time.
pri private async parse<T>(raw: APIResponse, method: HttpMethod, url: string, durationMs: number): Promise<ApiResponse<T>> Builds the ApiResponse<T>: 204 becomes { success: true }, an empty body becomes { success: raw.ok() }, anything else is JSON.parse'd (throwing ApiRequestError('API response was not valid JSON') with the first 300 chars on failure); then fills status, ok, headers, body, data, error, meta, durationMs, requestId (from the 'x-request-id' header), url and method, and logs the masked response.
Used by

Instantiated in src/fixtures/api.fixture.ts as the `apiClient` fixture (unauthenticated) and the `adminApiClient` fixture (authenticated as ADMIN via AuthApi, cleared on teardown). Held as `client` by every BaseApiService subclass (AuthApi, EmployeeApi, UserApi). Called directly from tests/api/regression/employee-negative.api.spec.ts (data-driven transport scenarios, withToken, rawBody malformed-JSON test).

Worth knowing11
  • Retries are verb-scoped: `attempts = options.maxAttempts ?? (IDEMPOTENT_METHODS.includes(method) ? this.maxAttempts : 1)`, and IDEMPOTENT_METHODS (src/constants/ApiConstants.ts) is ['GET','HEAD','OPTIONS','PUT','DELETE']. POST and PATCH therefore get exactly one attempt unless you pass maxAttempts explicitly.
  • A retryable status (429/500/502/503, RETRYABLE_STATUS_CODES) is converted into a thrown ApiRequestError inside the retry body — but ONLY when `attempts > 1`. Consequence: a GET that returns 503 on every attempt exhausts the retries and then THROWS ApiRequestError('API request failed'); the same 503 on a POST is returned as a normal ApiResponse with status 503. Non-2xx responses are otherwise returned, never thrown.
  • withRetry also retries when the error is any ApiRequestError, or an Error whose message matches /ECONNRESET|ECONNREFUSED|socket hang up|timeout/i. Backoff is exponential with full jitter from environment.retries.apiBackoffMs; ApiClient does not pass maxDelayMs, so RetryUtils' default cap of 4000 ms applies.
  • `durationMs` is measured with `Date.now()` taken before withRetry, so it covers every retry attempt and every backoff sleep — a retried call inflates the number ResponseValidator.respondedWithin() checks.
  • skipAuth: true deletes the Authorization and x-api-key headers even when the caller passed them explicitly in options.headers — it is a hard strip, not just 'don't add the token'.
  • useApiKey only sets x-api-key when environment.apiKey() returns a value; if the environment declares no key the request goes out silently unauthenticated rather than failing.
  • The token is instance state shared by every service built on the client. AuthApi.authenticateClientAs() mutates it, which is exactly how tests re-identify (e.g. authenticateClientAs('EMPLOYEE') changes what employeeApi can do). withToken() clones instead of mutating, but the clone shares the same APIRequestContext and Logger instance.
  • `rawBody` is deliberately sent as `Buffer.from(options.rawBody, 'utf8')`: Playwright re-serialises a *string* body when the content type is JSON, which would silently repair the malformed payload a negative test is trying to send. Use rawBody, not body, for malformed-JSON tests.
  • Query values that are `undefined` or the empty string are dropped by buildUrl, so `query: { search: '' }` cannot send `?search=`.
  • Body logging is gated on frameworkConfig.verboseApiLogging (config/framework.config.ts, defaults to true off-CI); URLs, headers and bodies always pass through maskUrl/maskHeaders/maskValue first.
  • getEnvironment() is called once in the constructor, so a client does not pick up environment changes made after it was built.

ResponseValidator

src/api/validators/ResponseValidator.ts
Talking to the API— (generic class ResponseValidator<T>; the module also exports the factory function `verify`)210 ln3 props18 methods

A fluent, chainable assertion API over a parsed ApiResponse<T>. It bundles the checks every API test repeats — status, envelope success/failure, error codes and messages, headers, dot-path body properties and their types, array shape, pagination meta, response time, and JSON-Schema conformance — and attaches a failure message that names the endpoint (method + URL) and prints a 500-character preview of the payload, so a red test explains itself without a debugger. Every assertion returns `this`; `unwrap()` ends the chain and hands back the typed data.

Used by

Almost always via the exported factory `verify<T>(response)` (re-exported from src/api/validators/index.ts). Used throughout tests/api/smoke/platform.api.spec.ts, tests/api/regression/employee-crud.api.spec.ts, tests/api/regression/employee-negative.api.spec.ts, tests/api/contract/employee-contract.spec.ts and tests/hybrid/employee-hybrid.spec.ts. employee-negative.api.spec.ts also holds the returned validator in a variable to add a conditional assertion (`const validator = verify(response)…; if (expectedField) validator.hasValidationErrorForField(expectedField);`).

Worth knowing15
  • The intended entry point is the module-level factory `export function verify<T>(response: ApiResponse<T>): ResponseValidator<T>` — `new ResponseValidator(response)` works identically but no test in the repo does that.
  • Every assertion returns `this` except `unwrap()`, which returns T. Chains therefore read `verify(r).hasStatus(...).isSuccessful().unwrap()` and unwrap must be last.
  • matchesSchema validates `data`; matchesEnvelopeSchema validates the whole `body`. Error payloads have no `data`, so error contract checks must use matchesEnvelopeSchema (as employee-contract.spec.ts and employee-negative.api.spec.ts do).
  • isFailure() requires BOTH body.success === false and a defined error object. A 4xx with an empty body will fail it: ApiClient synthesises `{ success: raw.ok() }` for an empty payload, giving success=false but no error.
  • Conversely a 204 is synthesised as `{ success: true }` with no data — isSuccessful() passes but unwrap() will fail.
  • hasProperty asserts presence with toBeDefined() (which passes for null) and compares with toEqual (deep equality, not identity). Passing `expected: undefined` skips the comparison entirely, so it cannot be used to assert a field is absent.
  • The dot path in hasProperty / hasPropertyOfType indexes arrays too — employee-crud.api.spec.ts uses `.hasProperty('0.email', target.email)` on a list response.
  • hasPropertyOfType uses raw `typeof`, so 'object' also matches arrays and null, and there is no 'array' option — use isArray() for that.
  • everyItem falls back to `[]` when data is undefined, so it passes vacuously on a missing or empty payload; pair it with isArray({ minLength: n }).
  • hasHeader compares strings with toContain (substring match, e.g. 'application/json' matches 'application/json; charset=utf-8'), and lowercases the header name because Playwright returns lowercase keys.
  • hasValidationErrorForField only reads `error.details` when it is an Array; ApiErrorBody also permits a Record, in which case the field list is empty and the assertion fails while printing the raw details.
  • respondedWithin measures ApiClient's durationMs, which is timed around the whole send including retry attempts and backoff sleeps — a retried call can blow a budget that the single successful attempt would have met.
  • hasStatusIn's assertion is expressed as expect(expectedArray).toContain(actualStatus), so Playwright's default 'Expected/Received' output is inverted relative to intuition; rely on the custom message, which states both.
  • The failure label uses `response.url` verbatim — the unmasked URL, unlike ApiClient's log lines, which run it through maskUrl first.
  • hasStatusIn, hasPropertyOfType and the standalone hasHeader(name, expected) are available but not currently called by any spec (isJson() is the only hasHeader user).

pub public async createOrThrow(payload: EmployeeCreateRequest): Promise<Employee> create() plus a hard failure: throws ApiRequestError('Employee setup failed') when !response.ok || !response.data, otherwise logs and returns the created Employee. The standard way to seed a record.

Used by

Built by the `employeeApi` (unauthenticated client) and `adminEmployeeApi` (ADMIN client) fixtures in src/fixtures/api.fixture.ts; `deleteAll` is called by the `cleanup` fixture in teardown. Used in tests/api/regression/employee-crud.api.spec.ts, tests/api/regression/employee-negative.api.spec.ts, tests/api/contract/employee-contract.spec.ts, tests/api/smoke/platform.api.spec.ts, tests/hybrid/employee-hybrid.spec.ts, tests/ui/e2e/employee-lifecycle.e2e.spec.ts, tests/ui/regression/employee-management.regression.spec.ts and tests/ui/sanity/dashboard.sanity.spec.ts.

Worth knowing8
  • Only createOrThrow (and, transitively, createMany and waitUntilSearchable) throws. Every other method returns the envelope, so `await employeeApi.remove(id)` on a forbidden delete resolves with status 403 rather than rejecting.
  • deleteIfExists never throws and never signals a hard failure: a 403 or 500 during cleanup is only a warning in the log and a `false` return. Do not treat its boolean as 'the record is gone'.
  • list() always passes all six query keys; ApiClient drops the undefined ones, so `list()` with no argument sends no query string at all.
  • findByEmail relies on the server-side `search` matching the email and then filters client-side; it is capped at pageSize 100, so an email whose search returns more than 100 rows can miss a genuine match.
  • waitUntilSearchable returns `found as Employee` — a cast. pollUntil throws FrameworkError('Polled value never satisfied the condition') if the record never appears, so the cast is safe, but the failure surfaces as a framework error rather than an assertion.
  • countAll returns 0 both when the directory is genuinely empty and when `meta` is missing (including when the list call failed) — it cannot distinguish 'zero' from 'no answer'.
  • createMany is sequential and fails fast: if the third createOrThrow throws, the first two records already exist and have not been handed back for cleanup registration.
  • remove() is a DELETE, which IS in the client's IDEMPOTENT_METHODS list, so it participates in the retry policy; create() is a POST and does not.

Worth knowing7
  • login() sends skipAuth: true, so an already-authenticated client can still sign in as somebody else without the old Authorization header interfering.
  • The layering is deliberate: login() returns the envelope and never throws; loginAs() throws ApiRequestError on failure; authenticateClientAs() additionally mutates the shared client. Pick the one whose failure mode you want.
  • authenticateClientAs() has a side effect that reaches beyond this service — in the fixture graph, apiClient backs authApi, userApi AND employeeApi, so calling it re-identifies all of them for the rest of the test.
  • logout() calls clearAuthToken() unconditionally *after* awaiting the POST — the local token is dropped even if the server rejected the logout.
  • health() is typed `ApiResponse<{ status: string }>`, narrower than the HealthStatus wire type in src/types/ApiModels.ts (which also carries uptimeSeconds and employees). The smoke test still validates the full payload with matchesSchema(healthSchema).
  • loginAs()'s error message embeds `HTTP ${response.status} ${response.error?.code ?? ''}` — status and code only, never the credentials.
  • loginAs() is public but the current suite only reaches it indirectly through authenticateClientAs(); logout() is likewise unused by any spec today.

SoftAssertions

src/utils/AssertionUtils.ts
Errors and logging247 ln1 props4 methods

A collector for non-fatal checks. Instead of aborting on the first bad expectation, it records each failure as a string and fails once, at the end, with the whole list — so a report shows every broken expectation rather than only the first. Its own doc comment states exactly that. It is the only class in AssertionUtils; everything else in the file is a free function.

Exported from `src/utils/AssertionUtils.ts:221` but currently has NO call site anywhere in the repository — no import or instantiation in src/, tests/, config/, scripts/, docs/ or README.md. The only external reference is `eslint.config.js:93`, which registers the string `'assertAll'` in the `playwright/expect-expect` rule's `assertFunctionNames` list, so a test whose only assertion is `soft.assertAll()` still satisfies that lint rule.

Worth knowing7
  • `assertAll` uses the HARD `expect` imported from '@playwright/test' (line 8), not `expect.soft`. The softness is in the collecting, not in the final call — `assertAll` aborts the test at that line like any other failed assertion.
  • `assertAll` does not clear `failures`. Calling it twice on the same instance re-reports every earlier failure; create a new instance per step if you want independent batches.
  • `check` takes an already-computed boolean, so it does NOT get Playwright's web-first auto-retry — by the time the boolean exists the retry window is gone. `checkAsync` is the auto-retrying path: pass one of the file's `assertX` helpers (which wrap retrying `expect` matchers) as the callback.
  • `checkAsync` swallows the error entirely — it catches everything, keeps only the first line of `.message`, and discards the stack and any `FrameworkError` context. A multi-line FrameworkError message (which is the norm in this framework) is therefore truncated to its headline.
  • `checkAsync` casts the caught value with `(error as Error)`; a thrown non-Error would produce `undefined.split` at runtime. Every framework throw site raises a real Error, so this holds in practice.
  • The failure list is compared with `.toEqual([])`, so the assertion diff shows the collected strings — the second `expect` argument is the human-readable summary, the diff is the machine-readable one.
  • Note the file-level rule this class sits under (lines 4-5): assertions are Playwright's auto-retrying, web-first `expect`; these helpers "add business meaning and a consistent failure message, never a manual retry loop." SoftAssertions must not be used to build a poll loop.

The framework's single structured logger. Worth knowing12
  • Masking, exactly: the message goes through `maskString` (DataMasker.ts:36) which is REGEX-based only — it redacts `Bearer <token>`, JWT-looking `eyJ…` strings, `tkn_…` strings, JSON `"password"/"token"/"apiKey"/"api_key"/"secret": "…"` pairs, and `password=/token=/api_key=/secret=` query fragments. The payload goes through `maskValue` (DataMasker.ts:47), which deep-clones and replaces any value whose KEY is sensitive with `***REDACTED***`. Consequence a reader gets wrong: a bare secret interpolated into the message string that matches none of those patterns is NOT masked — put secrets in the payload object under a sensible key, never in the message.
  • `maskValue` turns an Error payload into `{ name, message }` (DataMasker.ts:56) — the stack is dropped. So `logger.error('...', error)` logs no stack trace; `Logger.step` is subject to this too.
  • Cyclic payloads do not throw: `maskValue` collapses a repeat reference to the string `'[Circular]'`.
  • Level filtering is decided ONCE at module load: `configuredLevel` (lines 58-60) reads `frameworkConfig.logLevel`, falling back to `'INFO'` when the value is not in `LOG_LEVELS`. `frameworkConfig.logLevel` itself is `process.env.LOG_LEVEL ?? (isCi ? 'INFO' : 'DEBUG')` (config/framework.config.ts:62). Changing `process.env.LOG_LEVEL` after import has no effect.
  • Because `action()` logs at DEBUG, every `BasePage.perform` / `BaseComponent.perform` trace line disappears on CI, where the default level is INFO.
  • Output routing differs by level: ERROR → `console.error`, WARN → `console.warn`, DEBUG and INFO → `process.stdout.write(line + '\n')` (not `console.log`).
  • Colour is applied to the console line only when `process.stdout.isTTY === true && process.env.NO_COLOR === undefined` (line 39), evaluated once at import. The line appended to the file is always the uncoloured one.
  • File logging state is MODULE-level, not per-instance: `logFilePath` and `fileLoggingBroken` are shared by every Logger. The path is `PATHS.logs/run-${frameworkConfig.runId}.log`, created lazily on first write. If `mkdirSync` or `appendFileSync` throws, file logging is disabled for the whole process and a `[Logger] file logging disabled: …` / `[Logger] file sink stopped: …` warning is printed once — console logging continues.
  • Scope rendering: `[this.scope.module, this.scope.test].filter(Boolean).join(' | ')`, falling back to the literal `'framework'` when both are absent. Note the order — module first, then test — which is the reverse of `createLogger(module, test)`'s ordering only in appearance; they match.
  • The level field is `level.padEnd(5)`, so DEBUG/ERROR are 5 chars and INFO/WARN are padded to 5 — columns line up.
  • A `payload` of `undefined` produces no payload segment at all; any other value, including `null`, is appended as ` ${JSON.stringify(maskValue(payload))}`.
  • `child()` and `step()` are exported API but have NO call site anywhere in the repository as it stands — every consumer uses `createLogger` plus the four level methods and `action`.

FrameworkError

src/utils/FrameworkError.ts
Errors and loggingError65 ln3 props0 methods

The base class for every error the framework raises itself. It exists so a failure never arrives as a bare message: the constructor folds a structured ErrorContext and the original cause into the rendered `message`, so the stack trace a runner prints already answers what was attempted, on what, where, in which environment and what actually happened. The file header states the intent — "Typed errors carrying debugging context (rule 26: never swallow, always explain)". The four subclasses (UiActionError, ApiRequestError, TestDataError, ValidationError) add no behaviour; they exist purely so a catch site can discriminate on the layer that failed.

Thrown directly in: `global-setup.ts:88` (environment unreachable) and `global-setup.ts:105` (browser launch failed); `src/utils/RetryUtils.ts:56, 72, 98`; `src/utils/FileUtils.ts:24, 42, 56, 67, 77, 117`; `src/fixtures/auth.fixture.ts:44`; `src/fixtures/AuthenticationManager.ts:71`. Extended by UiActionError, ApiRequestError, TestDataError and ValidationError in the same file. `src/integrations/jira/JiraClient.ts:188-191` deliberately opts OUT of this hierarchy for JiraApiError, documenting that it wants a one-line message rather than a multi-line dump.

Worth knowing7
  • ErrorContext (lines 3-12) is: `readonly operation: string` (the only required key), plus optional `target`, `page`, `expected`, `actual`, `environment`, `url` — all `string` — and an open index signature `readonly [key: string]: unknown`. The index signature is why call sites freely add ad-hoc keys such as `hint` (global-setup.ts:93), `timeout` (WaitUtils.ts:52), `attempts` (ApiClient.ts:232), `status` (ApiClient.ts:267) and `available` (JsonReader.ts:91) without a type change.
  • Message rendering (lines 44-49): the final message is `[message, renderContext(context), causeMessage ? ` cause: ${causeMessage}` : undefined].filter(Boolean).join('\n')`. So the first line is the caller's message; each context entry is its own line indented by exactly two spaces as ` key: value`; the cause, when present, is the last line as ` cause: <text>`. This is the shape `docs/ARCHITECTURE.md:132-139` documents.
  • `renderContext` (lines 27-31) skips entries whose value is `undefined` or the empty string — but NOT `null`, which renders as ` key: null`. String values are emitted raw; every other value goes through `JSON.stringify`, so an array context value like RetryUtils' `attempts: failures` becomes a JSON array on one line.
  • The cause text is derived by `describe` (lines 15-25) only when the cause is not an Error: strings pass through, number/boolean/bigint are `.toString()`d, everything else is `JSON.stringify`d, falling back to the literal `'unknown cause'` when stringify returns undefined and `'unserialisable cause'` when it throws. When the cause IS an Error, only its `.message` is interpolated — the cause's stack is reachable only via the native `.cause` property.
  • `this.name = new.target.name` means the name tracks the actual constructed class, including any subclass added later. Do not hardcode `name` in a subclass.
  • The rendered message is computed once at construction. Mutating `error.context` afterwards does not change `error.message`.
  • Because the context is embedded in `message`, anything you put in the context is printed to logs, reports and CI output. There is no masking here — unlike Logger, FrameworkError does not route through DataMasker, so never place a raw credential in an ErrorContext.

ExtentReporter

src/reporting/ExtentReporter.ts
The reportimplements `Reporter` from `@playwright/test/reporter` (no base class)335 ln5 props12 methods

The framework's custom Playwright reporter and the single integration point between a test run and the Extent-style HTML report. It listens to Playwright's reporter hooks, normalises every finished test into an `ExtentTest` row — suite, module, tags, project, timings, status including retries, flattened steps, error and copied artifacts — and at the end of the run assembles an `ExtentReportModel`, publishes outbound integrations, and writes `index.html` + `report.json` into a timestamped folder under `reports/extent/run-<stamp>/`, plus `latest.html` / `latest.json` one level up. Every string it touches is put through `maskString` first, so no password, token, cookie or Authorization header can reach a published artifact. It is the reason no test in the repo contains reporting code.

OwnsTurn Playwright's per-attempt reporter callbacks into one masked, de-duplicated report model per run and write it to disk.

Used by

Registered by path, never imported or instantiated by application code: `playwright.config.ts` line 65 adds `['./src/reporting/ExtentReporter.ts']` to the `reporter` array when `frameworkConfig.extentEnabled` is true (`EXTENT_REPORT` env var, default true — `config/framework.config.ts` line 64). Playwright constructs it. Its output is consumed by `scripts/open-extent-report.mjs` (the `npm run report:open` script) and documented in `README.md` and `docs/ARCHITECTURE.md`. The exported `latestReportSummary()` has no caller anywhere in the repo.

Worth knowing18
  • `onTestEnd` fires once per ATTEMPT, not per test. The class keys `testsById` by `test.id` so the last attempt overwrites the earlier one — otherwise a retried test would appear as both a FAIL row and a FLAKY row and skew total/failed/pass rate away from what Playwright itself reports.
  • The merge on overwrite is not a plain overwrite: `errorMessage`/`errorStack` fall back to the previous attempt's values (`row.errorMessage ?? previous?.errorMessage`), and attachments are CONCATENATED across attempts (`[...(previous?.attachments ?? []), ...row.attachments]`). So a test that failed then passed keeps the failing attempt's error text and every attempt's screenshots. Collision is avoided because attachment filenames are namespaced `<testId>-<retry>-<name>`.
  • `latest.html` / `latest.json` are only rewritten when `tests.length > 0`. A run that executed nothing (unknown `--project`, failed global setup, `--list`) still writes its own `run-<stamp>/index.html` and `report.json`, prints a message saying the previous `latest.html` is untouched, and returns early. Do not assume `latest.html` corresponds to the most recent invocation — only to the most recent invocation that executed a test.
  • The two copies of the HTML are rendered differently: the in-folder `index.html` uses `renderExtentHtml(model)` with an empty asset base, while `reports/extent/latest.html` sits one directory higher and is rendered as `renderExtentHtml(model, `${basename(this.reportDir)}/`)`. Without that prefix every screenshot, video and trace link in the `latest` copy would resolve to nothing.
  • FLAKY counts as a pass in the summary: `passRate = Math.round(((passed + flaky) / executed) * 100)` where `executed = total - skipped`, and it is `0` when `executed === 0`. `failed` is the count of FAIL + TIMEOUT + INTERRUPTED; FLAKY is tracked as its own bucket and is not in `failed`.
  • Integrations are awaited BEFORE the document is rendered, so their outcome lands in the artifact rather than only in the console — and they are skipped entirely when `tests.length === 0`. `publishIntegrations` never throws and resolves for every target, so a dead webhook cannot cost the report. When the array is empty the `integrations` key is omitted from the model altogether (`...(integrations.length > 0 ? { integrations } : {})`), which is what lets the report show an honest empty state instead of an invented row. `process.env.REPORT_URL` is likewise only spread in when set.
  • Masking is the file's contract: test name, description, every step title, every annotation description, error message, error stack and inlined text-attachment bodies all pass through `maskString`. Note the ORDER on the stack — it is masked first and truncated to 4000 chars afterwards (`maskString(stripAnsi(result.error.stack)).slice(0, 4000)`), so truncation can never expose an unmasked tail.
  • `test.titlePath()` slicing is positional and easy to misread: the display name is `titlePath().slice(3).join(' › ')` (drops the leading empty root, the project name and the file path, falling back to `test.title` when empty), while the fallback description is `titlePath().slice(1, -1).join(' › ')` (drops the root and the test's own title).
  • Tag collection deduplicates title tags then appends only the `test.tags` entries not already present in the title — `[...new Set(test.title.match(TAG_PATTERN) ?? [])].concat(test.tags.filter((tag) => !test.title.includes(tag)))`. Playwright puts title `@tags` into `test.tags` too, so without that filter every tag would be listed twice. `TAG_PATTERN` is a module-level `/g` regex, but it is only used with `String.prototype.match`, which resets `lastIndex`, so there is no shared-state bug.
  • `collectAttachments` iterates `result.attachments` TWICE — the first pass handles attachments with a real `path` that still exists on disk (copied with `copyFileSync`), the second inlines attachments with a `body` whose `contentType` starts with `text/`. An attachment carrying both would be recorded twice. A failed copy is caught, written to stderr as `[ExtentReporter] could not copy attachment …`, and skipped; it never aborts the run.
  • Artifact `kind` is inferred purely from a substring of the attachment NAME (`screenshot`/`video`/`trace`, else `other`), not from content type or file extension. A custom attachment named something else is classified `other`.
  • `config` is declared with a definite-assignment assertion and is only set in `onBegin`. `buildEnvironment` (called from `onEnd`) reads `this.config.workers`, `.projects` and `.version`, so any path that reaches `onEnd` without `onBegin` having run would throw a TypeError.
  • Only three of Playwright's reporter hooks are implemented — `onBegin`, `onTestEnd`, `onEnd`. `onTestBegin`, `onStepBegin`, `onStepEnd`, `onError`, `onStdOut`, `onStdErr`, `onExit` and `printsToStdio` are all absent, so run-level errors that never attach to a test (a global-setup failure, for instance) leave no row in the report; only `result.status` in `latest.json` and the console line reflect them. Step data comes from `result.steps` at test end, not from the step hooks.
  • `onEnd` is `async` and ends each branch with a no-op `await Promise.resolve()`; it returns `undefined`, so it never overrides Playwright's run status (the hook's return type allows `{ status }`).
  • The reporter writes two files unconditionally per run (`index.html`, `report.json`) plus an `attachments/` directory created in `onBegin`, and `latest.json`'s payload is `{ reportDir, status, summary }` — broader than the `{ reportDir: string }` type `latestReportSummary()` declares.
  • `scripts/open-extent-report.mjs`, the `npm run report:open` script the `latestReportSummary` doc comment refers to, does NOT call it — being plain `.mjs` it reads and parses `reports/extent/latest.json` itself. The exported function is currently dead code in this repo.
  • `reportDir` is stamped in the CONSTRUCTOR, not in `onBegin`, so the folder name reflects when Playwright instantiated the reporter, while `summary.startedAt` reflects `onBegin`.
  • Helper ordering matters for correctness in two places a reader could get backwards: `suiteFor` tests `/tests/api/contract/` before `/tests/api/` (a contract spec lives under both), and `moduleFor` tests `employee` before `user`, so a path containing both resolves to Employee Management.

ZephyrNotifier

src/integrations/zephyr/ZephyrNotifier.ts
Sending results elsewhereimplements Integration603 ln3 props10 methods

Publishes a finished run to a Zephyr Scale Cloud test cycle. One Playwright test becomes one Zephyr test execution **per Zephyr test-case key it carries**, so a test tagged `@QA-T1 @QA-T2` updates both cases. Tests without a key are counted and reported, never invented — `POST /testexecutions` cannot create a test case, and guessing a key would either 404 or write a result onto somebody else's case. It honours the two integration guarantees: it never throws (every path returns an `IntegrationResult`, because a reporter's rejection is attributed to the suite and turns a green run red) and it is bounded (the client's per-call timeout stops one hung request, `ZEPHYR_MAX_TOTAL_MS` stops a thousand merely-slow ones).

OwnsMap an ExtentReportModel onto Zephyr test executions inside one named cycle, and report exactly what was and was not published.

Registered as a lazy factory in the integration registry — `() => new ZephyrNotifier(),` in `FACTORIES` (src/integrations/index.ts:36) — and re-exported from that module (src/integrations/index.ts:134). `publishIntegrations` then calls `isEnabled()`, `disabledReason()` and `publish()` on it; `publishIntegrations` itself is called once from `ExtentReporter` (src/reporting/ExtentReporter.ts:205), only when the run produced at least one test. There are no unit or API tests referencing this class anywhere in the repo.

Worth knowing16
  • **Gated by three variables, all mandatory: `ZEPHYR_ENABLED` (truthy = one of `1`, `true`, `yes`, `on`, compared lower-cased), `ZEPHYR_API_TOKEN`, `ZEPHYR_PROJECT_KEY`.** A whitespace-only value counts as unset — the module-level `read` helper trims and maps empty to `undefined`. Optional variables: `ZEPHYR_BASE_URL`, `ZEPHYR_TEST_CYCLE_KEY`, `ZEPHYR_TEST_CYCLE_NAME`, `ZEPHYR_ENVIRONMENT_NAME`, `ZEPHYR_STATUS_PASS`, `ZEPHYR_STATUS_FAIL`, `ZEPHYR_STATUS_BLOCKED`, `ZEPHYR_STATUS_NOT_EXECUTED`, `ZEPHYR_MAX_CONCURRENCY`, `ZEPHYR_MAX_TOTAL_MS`.
  • **`ZEPHYR_ENABLED` is absent from `.env.example`.** That file documents only `ZEPHYR_API_TOKEN`, `ZEPHYR_BASE_URL`, `ZEPHYR_PROJECT_KEY`, `ZEPHYR_TEST_CYCLE_KEY` and `ZEPHYR_TEST_CYCLE_NAME` (lines 62–66), so following it alone leaves the integration silently off. README.md:443 does name the flag.
  • **The Zephyr key scan is deliberately not the shared one.** `ZEPHYR_KEY_PATTERN` is `/\b([A-Z][A-Z_0-9]+-T\d+)\b/g`, matched against tags **and** annotations flattened as `type:description`. The shared `issueKeysFor` cannot find these (its pattern needs digits straight after the hyphen), and is used only to tell "you tagged a Jira issue key instead" apart from "you tagged nothing".
  • **Keys naming another project are counted and dropped, never sent.** Only keys starting `${projectKey}-T` become targets; the rest raise `foreignKeys` / `foreignOnly` in the detail, because an execution posted against one `projectKey` could only 404.
  • **`FLAKY` maps to the pass status name on purpose.** Playwright reports flaky when a test *passed* on retry and Zephyr has no equivalent state; the retry count is written into the comment (`Passed on retry (N attempt(s) failed first).`) so the result is not laundered into a clean pass. Full map: PASS/FLAKY→pass, FAIL/TIMEOUT→fail, INTERRUPTED→blocked, SKIP→notExecuted. Defaults `Pass`, `Fail`, `Blocked`, `Not Executed`.
  • **A partially successful publish is reported as `failed`.** `incomplete = outcome.failures.length > 0 || outcome.unattempted > 0` — `published` is returned only when every single target landed. The detail still leads with `N/M execution(s) published`.
  • **No target means no network call and no cycle.** When the scan finds zero targets, `publishRun` returns `skipped` before constructing the client, so a run with no Zephyr tags never creates an empty cycle.
  • **The client is constructed inside `publishRun`, not in the constructor** — a malformed `ZEPHYR_BASE_URL` therefore becomes this run's `failed` result rather than an exception during reporter setup.
  • **The time budget starts at the top of `publish`, not at the first execution.** `deadline = startedAt + settings.maxTotalMs`, and `startedAt` is taken before settings are even read, so key validation, the status listing and cycle creation all consume it.
  • **The deadline is checked only before a target is dequeued and never aborts a request in flight.** Cancelling a POST that may already have appended a row would leave nobody able to say whether the row landed. Remaining targets are counted as `unattempted` and named in the detail — they are never quietly dropped, and never retried.
  • **Concurrency and budget are clamped, not rejected.** `ZEPHYR_MAX_CONCURRENCY` below 1 or non-numeric falls back to 4 and is capped at 10; `ZEPHYR_MAX_TOTAL_MS` non-numeric falls back to 120000, and any parsed number is raised to at least 5000 — so a negative value becomes 5000 rather than an error.
  • **`ZEPHYR_PROJECT_KEY` is uppercased for you**, then validated against `ZEPHYR_PROJECT_KEY_PATTERN`; failure returns a `failed` result quoting the normalised value, not an exception. `ZEPHYR_TEST_CYCLE_KEY` is validated as-is against `<PROJECT>-R<number>`.
  • **An unmapped status throws a plain `Error` from `toExecutionInput` — inside the worker's try**, so it is recorded as that one target's failure string rather than failing the run.
  • **`warnOnUnknownStatuses` stays silent on weak evidence.** It returns without warning when the status page is empty or `complete` is false, and it swallows its own lookup failure into a warning; a mismatch never prevents publishing.
  • **The result never carries a `url`.** The cycle's `self` link is an authenticated API endpoint that answers 401 in a browser, and this process does not know the tenant's Jira base URL — the cycle key in the detail is what a human can actually search for.
  • **Comments are sanitised three ways**: ANSI colour codes stripped, only the first non-empty error line kept, then `maskString` and a 1000-character clamp — because the string is written into a system other people read. `finish` masks the whole detail again on the way out.

ZephyrClient

src/integrations/zephyr/ZephyrClient.ts
Sending results elsewhere— (no base class, implements no interface)505 ln3 props4 methods

A deliberately minimal HTTP client for the Zephyr Scale Cloud v2 API, carrying exactly the three calls a finished Playwright run needs: create a test cycle, create a test execution, and list a project's execution statuses. It targets Zephyr **Scale** (formerly TM4J), not Zephyr Squad — Squad HMAC-signs a fresh JWT per request on a different host, so a static bearer token and every payload here is meaningless there. It chose the one-cycle-plus-one-execution-per-test path over a JUnit XML bulk upload because only that path carries a per-test comment, the real execution time and an environment label, and only that path lets shards and re-runs land in a cycle we named. The API token exists in exactly one place: a private field written into an `Authorization` header, never into a URL, a message, a thrown error or a log line.

OwnsTurn three validated Zephyr Scale v2 operations into HTTP requests and typed results, converting every possible failure into a single `ZephyrApiError` shape.

Used by

Instantiated in exactly one place in the repo: `ZephyrNotifier.publishRun` (src/integrations/zephyr/ZephyrNotifier.ts:354), which then passes the instance into its own private `warnOnUnknownStatuses`, `resolveCycleKey` and `publishExecutions`. The class is exported from ZephyrClient.ts but is NOT re-exported from src/integrations/index.ts, so nothing outside the zephyr folder can reach it through the package's public surface.

Worth knowing13
  • **The constructor throws.** `normaliseBaseUrl` runs during construction and throws `ZephyrApiError('…', 'configuration', 0)` when the base URL will not parse, or when it is not `https:` — plain `http:` is accepted only for the loopback hosts `localhost`, `127.0.0.1`, `[::1]`, `::1`. This is precisely why ZephyrNotifier constructs the client inside `publishRun` rather than in its own constructor.
  • **The class reads no environment variables at all.** `token`, `baseUrl` and `timeoutMs` are injected through `ZephyrClientOptions`. Every `ZEPHYR_*` variable is read by ZephyrNotifier and handed in. `ZEPHYR_BASE_URL` and `ZEPHYR_API_TOKEN` are named in the class's error text and HTTP hints, but never read here.
  • **`baseUrl` is rewritten, not stored verbatim.** `normaliseBaseUrl` returns `${parsed.origin}${parsed.pathname}` with trailing slashes stripped, so query string and fragment are dropped — a credential pasted into a query would otherwise ride along on every request.
  • **Nothing retries — not on 429, not on 503, not on a timeout.** `POST /testexecutions` appends a row every call, so a retry after a timeout silently doubles a result. The 429 hint in `HTTP_HINTS` says exactly this.
  • **`status === 0` is broader than the class doc suggests.** The doc comment on ZephyrApiError says `0` means the request never reached the API, but `asRecord`, `asCreatedResource` and the missing-cycle-key guard all throw with status `0` *after* a successful 2xx response. Read `0` as "no HTTP status is meaningful here", covering local validation, transport failure, timeout **and** an unusable success body.
  • **A cycle can be created and still throw.** `createTestCycle` throws `'cycle was created but the response carried no key'` (status 0) when the 2xx body has no non-blank string `key` — the cycle exists server-side at that point, so calling again creates a second one.
  • **A missing `self` does not throw.** `asCreatedResource` requires a numeric `id` but degrades a missing/non-string `self` to `''` rather than rejecting a successful write over a cosmetic field.
  • **`listExecutionStatuses` never throws on a malformed shape.** A payload whose `values` is not an array returns `{ names: [], complete: false }`. `complete` is `isLast === true || (typeof total === 'number' && total <= values.length)`. Archived statuses are filtered out because they cannot be assigned to a new execution. Only the first page (1000 rows) is read; there is no paging.
  • **Key validation is asymmetric.** `ZEPHYR_PROJECT_KEY_PATTERN` (`/^[A-Z][A-Z_0-9]+$/`) demands uppercase and at least two characters, but the client does **not** uppercase for you — ZephyrNotifier does that before calling. `ZEPHYR_TEST_CASE_KEY_PATTERN` is deliberately loose (`/^\S+-T\d+$/`, whitespace excluded only so a key cannot forge log lines) and does **not** check that the key belongs to `projectKey`; a cross-project key is validated fine here and 404s at the API.
  • **Values are silently normalised before sending.** Names are trimmed and clamped to 255 characters with a visible `...` suffix; `executionTime` is coerced with `Math.max(0, Math.round(…))` and dropped entirely when non-finite; `JSON.stringify` removes `undefined` fields so optionals are absent rather than explicitly `null`.
  • **The timeout covers the response body, not just the headers.** `await response.text()` sits inside the same `try` because an aborted body rejects from `text()`, not from `fetch`. A timeout is reported as `no complete response within {timeoutMs}ms`.
  • **Error text is masked and clipped.** `describeHttpFailure` runs the body through `maskString` and clamps it to 300 characters; the URL and token are never echoed. The 403 hint is load-bearing: Zephyr answers 403 for a mistyped path and an invalid token as well as for a genuine permission gap.
  • **There is no read/update/delete surface.** No method fetches an existing execution, updates one, or resolves a test case — `POST /testexecutions` cannot create a test case and answers 404 for an unknown one.

ZephyrApiError

src/integrations/zephyr/ZephyrClient.ts
Sending results elsewhereextends Error505 ln5 props0 methods

The single error shape every ZephyrClient failure leaves as, so a caller has exactly one thing to reason about. It carries two fields beyond a plain `Error`: the `endpoint` the call was aimed at (a method-and-path string such as `POST /testexecutions`, or the literal `configuration` for a base-URL problem) and a numeric `status`. `status` is `0` when no HTTP status is meaningful — a validation failure, a timeout, an unreachable host, or a 2xx body that could not be used — so a caller can tell "we sent something bad" from "they answered something bad" without parsing the message.

OwnsAttach a machine-readable endpoint and status to every Zephyr failure while keeping the token out of the message.

Used by

Thrown from ten sites inside src/integrations/zephyr/ZephyrClient.ts — `asRecord`, `asCreatedResource`, `requireName`, `requireMatch`, both branches of `normaliseBaseUrl`, the missing-cycle-key guard in `createTestCycle`, and the transport / non-OK / JSON-parse branches of `send`. Nothing in the repo catches it by `instanceof`: ZephyrNotifier's module-level `describeError` (src/integrations/zephyr/ZephyrNotifier.ts:599) reads only `error.message`, so `status` and `endpoint` currently reach no consumer.

Worth knowing6
  • **The message you pass is not the message you get.** `super(`${endpoint}: ${message}`, …)` prefixes it, so `new ZephyrApiError('response was not valid JSON', 'GET /statuses', 200).message` is `'GET /statuses: response was not valid JSON'`. Anything matching on the message must expect that prefix.
  • **`cause` is filtered.** `cause instanceof Error ? { cause } : undefined` — a thrown string, a `DOMException` subclass that does not extend `Error`, or a plain object is silently discarded rather than attached.
  • **`status: 0` does not reliably mean "never left the process".** The declaring comment says a `0` is a configuration, validation, timeout or unreachable-host failure, but `asRecord`, `asCreatedResource` and `createTestCycle`'s missing-key guard also throw `0` after a real 2xx response. Treat `0` as "no useful HTTP status", not as proof nothing was sent — which matters because a `0` from `createTestCycle` can mean a cycle *was* created.
  • **No `Object.setPrototypeOf` call.** `instanceof ZephyrApiError` works on the repo's ES2015+ target; it would break if this file were ever downleveled to ES5.
  • **It is exported from ZephyrClient.ts but not from src/integrations/index.ts**, so it is not part of the integrations package's public surface — a consumer outside the zephyr folder must import the module path directly to catch it by type.
  • **The endpoint string is a label, not a URL.** It never contains the host or the token; `'configuration'` is used for the two `normaliseBaseUrl` rejections, which happen before any credential is on the wire.
