Worth knowing13
  • The class declares seven members — two properties and five methods. report(), groupFailures(), summarise(), isAddressable(), commentLines(), bugLines(), failureLines() and listed() are module-level functions in the same file, not class members.
  • Its notion of 'failing' is narrower than the reporter's and narrower than Slack's: FAILING_STATUSES is exactly ['FAIL', 'TIMEOUT']. FLAKY is excluded because it passed on retry, and INTERRUPTED is excluded because it is a fact about the runner. SlackBlocks.ts, by contrast, treats INTERRUPTED as a failure.
  • JIRA_CLOUD_ID, JIRA_CREATE_ISSUE_ON_FAILURE, JIRA_MAX_COMMENTS and JIRA_ISSUE_KEY_PREFIXES are read here but documented nowhere in .env.example or README.md.
  • The call cap counts the credential preflight: `let budget = settings.maxCalls - 1` runs before verifyCredentials(). With JIRA_MAX_COMMENTS=1 no comment is ever written.
  • Two independent limits can truncate the report — the call cap and a 60_000ms wall clock that starts BEFORE the preflight — and a call is not started at all with less than MIN_CALL_MS (2_000) left. Either way the detail names what was left undone; issues are never dropped silently.
  • Note the interaction with the registry: MAX_TOTAL_MS here is 60_000, the same as DEFAULT_BUDGET_MS for the entire batch in src/integrations/index.ts, so a slow Jira can consume the whole batch budget and leave later integrations marked 'Not attempted'.
  • Result status is derived, not chosen: 'published' if any comment or issue was written, else 'failed' if any call failed, else 'skipped'. A run where every call failed and nothing was written reports 'failed'.
  • IntegrationResult.url is browseUrl(createdKey ?? commented[0]) — the created Bug wins, otherwise the first commented issue in sorted order. It is omitted when nothing was written.
  • There is no dedupe on issue creation. One Bug per run, with no search against previous runs (Jira has no idempotency key on create), so leaving JIRA_CREATE_ISSUE_ON_FAILURE on for per-commit runs files a new bug on every build for a recurring failure.
  • ISSUE_KEY_PATTERN is deliberately broad, so a tag like @CHROME-131 reads as an issue key and this integration WRITES. JIRA_ISSUE_KEY_PREFIXES narrows the match to the project prefixes a team files against; unset, every matched key is commented on.
  • A test naming several issue keys is added to every one of their buckets, so one failing test can cost several API calls against the cap.
  • maxCalls parsing uses Number.parseInt, so 'abc' falls back to DEFAULT_MAX_CALLS (20) and '5x' parses as 5; the result is then clamped to 1..MAX_MAX_CALLS (200).
  • Comments are posted sequentially on purpose — Jira rate-limits writes per issue and this reporter has no business retrying non-idempotent writes.

SauceNotifier

src/integrations/sauce/SauceNotifier.ts
Sending results elsewhereimplements Integration462 ln1 props9 methods

Points a finished report at the Sauce Labs jobs that produced it. It publishes **nothing** to Sauce: saucectl already stamps a job's name, build and tags at submit time, and rewriting a finished job's record from a reporter would leave the Sauce UI and the run's own report disagreeing about what happened. The hard part is attribution — Sauce has no "current run" concept, and `GET /rest/v1/{username}/jobs` returns that user's recent jobs whatever produced them, which on the shared machine account CI usually authenticates as means every other pipeline's jobs too. The only reliable key is the build name, so this notifier links jobs only when `SAUCE_BUILD_NAME` was also passed to `saucectl run --build`; without it the honest answer is `skipped` rather than guessing at "the newest few jobs".

OwnsFind this run's Sauce jobs by build name and hand the report one job link, stating how far the search actually reached.

Used by

Registered as a lazy factory in the integration registry — `() => new SauceNotifier(),` in `FACTORIES` (src/integrations/index.ts:37) — and re-exported from that module (src/integrations/index.ts:135). `publishIntegrations` calls `isEnabled()`, `disabledReason()` and `publish()` on it; that function is called once from `ExtentReporter` (src/reporting/ExtentReporter.ts:205). Its configuration module, SauceConfig.ts, is separately consumed by scripts/write-sauce-config.mts (the `npm run sauce:config` generator). No test in the repo references this class.

Worth knowing16
  • **`isEnabled()` does not include `SAUCE_BUILD_NAME`.** It gates on `SAUCE_USERNAME` + `SAUCE_ACCESS_KEY` (and a `SAUCE_REGION` that is either unset or valid). The build name is checked separately inside `publish`, which returns `skipped` with an explicit message. So the integration can report itself enabled and still link nothing on every run.
  • **`disabledReason()` is not always a disabled message.** When configuration is fine it returns `'Sauce Labs credentials are present.'` — the registry only calls it for non-enabled integrations, but `publish` reuses it for its own `skipped` result, so that sentence can appear as a skip reason.
  • **The region default is `eu-central-1`, not Sauce's own `us-west-1`.** `resolveSauceRegion` returns `DEFAULT_SAUCE_REGION` for an unset/blank value and `undefined` for a value that is set but unrecognised — a typo becomes a configuration message rather than API calls against the wrong continent, since access keys are per data centre.
  • **`us-east-4` can never produce a link.** `SAUCE_ENDPOINTS['us-east-4']` has no `appBaseUrl` (Sauce documents the API host only), so even a successful build match returns `skipped` with "Sauce documents no UI host for us-east-4" rather than an invented dashboard URL. `us-east-4` also has `supportsPlaywright: false`.
  • **There is no environment injection point.** Unlike ZephyrNotifier, this class takes no options; it calls `isSauceConfigured()`, `readSauceCredentials()`, `resolveSauceRegion()` and `sauceBuildName()` with no arguments, so they all default to `process.env` at call time.
  • **`full=true` is not an optimisation.** Without it the endpoint returns bare ids — no `build`, no `passed` — the build filter matches zero jobs, and the run silently looks as though it never reached Sauce. `buildFieldAbsent` exists precisely to name that symptom in the output.
  • **Bounded search, and it says so.** Up to `MAX_JOB_PAGES = 3` pages of `JOB_PAGE_SIZE = 100` (300 jobs) under a shared `LOOKUP_BUDGET_MS = 30_000`; each request gets `min(REQUEST_TIMEOUT_MS = 15_000, remaining)` with a floor of 1 ms. "Not found" is always phrased as "not found in the jobs I looked at".
  • **The paging loop has four exit conditions worth knowing.** A page adding no fresh ids means `skip` never moved the cursor, so it stops and sets `windowExhausted` only if that page was full; a short page means the account's list ended and the search was exhaustive; a page after the first match that carries no matches breaks early on the newest-first assumption and leaves `windowExhausted` as it was — so that result reads `all N job(s) on the … account`, where N is only what was scanned; and reaching the last allowed page sets `windowExhausted = true`.
  • **Sauce counts jobs, the report counts tests.** The detail deliberately states both (`N Sauce job(s) carry build "…"` … `this report covers M tests`) and appends "so the job count is a lower bound" when the window was exhausted. Do not read the job count as a test count.
  • **`passed` is tri-state.** `true`, `false`, or absent while a job is still running — the third bucket is reported as "still running or unreported", never folded into failed.
  • **The linked job is the newest by `creation_time`.** The wire field is snake_case `creation_time` and is mapped to `creationTimeSec`; jobs missing it sort as `0`. Only one job is ever linked, via `sauceJobPageUrl(region, id)` → `<appBaseUrl>/tests/<jobId>`; there is no documented build page URL to link instead.
  • **No retry on 429 — by design.** "a retry storm at the end of a run is what earns the limit in the first place". Likewise a 200 with a non-JSON body is reported as a proxy/SSO interception page and the body is explicitly **not** reproduced in the result.
  • **Non-2xx bodies are cancelled, not read.** `discardBody` calls `response.body?.cancel()` so an unread error page does not hold its socket.
  • **Timeout detection walks the cause chain.** `isAbort` descends up to four `cause` links because undici surfaces an aborted fetch either as the signal's `DOMException` or as a `TypeError: fetch failed` wrapping it. The message it produces always says `no response within 15s` (derived from `REQUEST_TIMEOUT_MS`), even when the actual abort fired earlier because the shared budget was nearly spent.
  • **Credential hygiene:** the access key only ever reaches `sauceBasicAuthHeader`, the username is URL-encoded into the path, and `redactUsername` rewrites only the `/rest/v1/<segment>` shape in error text — a blanket replace would corrupt unrelated words when the account is named something short. Error stacks are discarded; only `error.message` survives into a report.
  • **`await this.linkBuild(...)` is awaited inside the try on purpose** — returning the promise bare would settle it outside the try and hand the caller a rejection, which is exactly what rule 2 of the integration contract forbids.

JiraApiError

src/integrations/jira/JiraClient.ts
Sending results elsewhereextends Error434 ln3 props0 methods

The single error type JiraClient throws for any Jira call that did not succeed — a non-2xx response, a body that is not JSON, a response missing a field the caller is about to dereference, or a transport failure where no response arrived at all. It carries the HTTP status alongside the message so a caller can distinguish 'the credentials are wrong' from 'the network is wrong'. Its message is deliberately written as one readable line, because it is destined for an IntegrationResult.detail rendered in the report.

OwnsCarry a Jira call's failure as one human-readable line plus the HTTP status that caused it.

pub name: string Inherited from Error; the constructor sets it to the literal 'JiraApiError'.
pub message: string Inherited from Error; a single pre-composed line — status, the STATUS_HINTS explanation, an optional retry-after, and the rendered ErrorCollection body.
Used by

Thrown in four places inside JiraClient (JiraClient.ts lines 345, 360, 371, 431). Caught and narrowed once, by the Jira publish pipeline: src/integrations/jira/JiraNotifier.ts line 333 uses `error instanceof JiraApiError && error.status === 401` to tell a rejected credential apart from a site or network problem. Elsewhere in JiraNotifier it is flattened to a message by the module-level describe() helper.

Worth knowing5
  • status === 0 is not an HTTP status — it means the exchange never completed (timeout, DNS, TLS). Branching on `status >= 400` alone silently misses this case.
  • It is deliberately NOT a FrameworkError subclass. Its message is a single line meant for a result detail, not a multi-line diagnostic dump.
  • The constructor does nothing beyond super(message), setting name and assigning status — no captureStackTrace, no explicit prototype fix. The latter is unnecessary here because tsconfig.json targets ES2023, so instanceof works as written.
  • A thrown JiraApiError does not mean nothing happened. When it comes from the `requires` guard on a POST (line 371) the message ends with ' — the write may still have taken effect': the comment or issue may exist despite the error.
  • The message may already contain a hint from STATUS_HINTS (400/401/403/404/429) and a rendered ErrorCollection; do not re-decorate it with a second explanation of the same status.

JiraClient

src/integrations/jira/JiraClient.ts
Sending results elsewhere— (implements no interface)434 ln4 props6 methods

A hand-rolled, dependency-free client for the three Jira Cloud platform REST API v3 endpoints this framework needs: GET /myself, POST /issue/{key}/comment and POST /issue. It builds the Basic auth header once, picks the right host for the token flavour (tenant origin for a classic token, the Atlassian gateway for a scoped one), bounds every call with an AbortSignal timeout, and converts any non-success into a JiraApiError whose message is a single readable line. It is a transport only: it holds no policy about when to write or what to say.

OwnsPerform one authenticated, deadline-bounded Jira v3 request and either return its validated JSON body or throw a JiraApiError describing exactly why it did not.

Resolves the effective deadline, fetches with the Authorization/Accept/Content-Type headers and an AbortSignal.timeout, reads the body inside the same signal, and converts any transport failure into a JiraApiError with status 0.
Used by

Instantiated in exactly one place: the module-level report() function in src/integrations/jira/JiraNotifier.ts (line 314), which then calls verifyCredentials(), addComment() and createIssue(). The instance is also passed into summarise() (OutcomeInput.client, line 432) purely so browseUrl() can build the result's url. It is not exported from src/integrations/index.ts.

Worth knowing10
  • Rich text must be ADF. A plain string in a comment body or an issue description is a 400 — build one with the exported adfDocument(lines) helper. `summary` is the mirror image: a plain string that rejects ADF.
  • This client never retries a write. Jira offers no idempotency key, so retrying a timed-out POST duplicates the comment or files the bug twice; failures are reported for the caller to decide on.
  • The per-call timeoutMs argument can only SHORTEN the deadline, never lengthen it: `Math.max(1_000, Math.min(this.timeoutMs, options.timeoutMs ?? this.timeoutMs))`. Passing a value below 1_000 still yields 1_000.
  • cloudId is what selects the host, not a preference. A scoped API token 401s against the tenant origin and a classic token 401s against the gateway — the 401 hint in STATUS_HINTS points at exactly this.
  • browseUrl() does no validation: it is a string builder over siteUrl and will happily produce a link for a key the caller never confirmed exists.
  • The `requires` guard means a successful HTTP write can still throw. A 201 whose body lacks a usable `key` raises JiraApiError with ' — the write may still have taken effect', which is deliberate: reporting a write of unknown outcome is safer than denying one that happened.
  • 404 from the comment endpoint does not mean 'no such issue'. Jira reports 'not visible to this account' the same way, which is why verifyCredentials() exists as a preflight.
  • options.apiToken is used verbatim — only the email is trimmed when the auth header is built. A token pasted with surrounding whitespace fails as a 401.
  • normaliseSiteUrl keeps the pathname (a Server/DC install can sit under a context path) but strips userinfo, query and fragment, because siteUrl is the one piece of configuration that is published into the report.
  • adfDocument() bounds the whole document at MAX_DOCUMENT_CHARS (28_000) and each line at MAX_TEXT_NODE_CHARS (800); once one line overflows, every later line is dropped too and the count is stated inside the document as '[N further line(s) omitted...]' rather than lost.

SlackNotifier

src/integrations/slack/SlackNotifier.ts
Sending results elsewhereimplements Integration (src/integrations/IntegrationTypes.ts)342 ln7 props10 methods

Posts exactly one Block Kit run summary per Playwright run to a Slack incoming webhook. It is the transport half of the Slack integration: it resolves configuration from options-then-environment, decides whether this run is worth announcing, delegates payload construction to buildRunSummaryMessage in SlackBlocks.ts, POSTs it, and turns whatever comes back into an IntegrationResult. It never posts per failure — a per-test loop would breach Slack's one-request-per-second webhook limit and bury the signal — and it never throws, so a dead webhook cannot turn a green suite red.

OwnsOwn the Slack webhook exchange for a finished run and report its outcome as a single IntegrationResult, without ever leaking the webhook URL or failing the run.

Constructed lazily by the integration registry in src/integrations/index.ts (FACTORIES, line 34) and re-exported from that module (line 132). The registry's publishIntegrations() is the only caller of publish(), and it is invoked once per run by src/reporting/ExtentReporter.ts (line 205). No test file in the repo references this class.

Worth knowing12
  • Environment-variable drift: the code reads SLACK_NOTIFY_ON (line 146), but .env.example line 47 and README.md line 441 both document SLACK_NOTIFY. Setting the documented name has no effect — the run stays on the quiet 'failure' default.
  • SLACK_TIMEOUT_MS is read by the constructor but is documented nowhere outside this file.
  • The notifyOn option is not blank-checked and not lower-cased: only the environment path goes through resolveNotifyOn(). options.notifyOn is taken as-is via ??, so a caller must pass exactly 'always' or 'failure'.
  • isEnabled() only asks whether a webhook URL is present. A malformed or http:// URL still enables the integration, and publish() then returns status 'failed' (not 'skipped') with 'value withheld' — the URL is never echoed.
  • Under the default 'failure' mode the quiet check is summary.failed === 0 only. A run that is green but flaky posts nothing; the skip detail names the flaky count so this is visible rather than silent.
  • fetch is called with redirect: 'error'. A webhook that answers with a redirect fails the publish rather than being followed — following it would POST the run summary to an unvetted host.
  • Slack's webhook answers with the plain text 'ok', not JSON. A 2xx body that is anything else is still reported as 'published', with ' (unexpected response: ...)' appended — do not read that as a failure.
  • Redaction always runs before truncation (safeText), and covers three shapes: the full URL, the bare secret path, and any hooks.slack.com URL found in server text.
  • Webhook mode posts to the one channel chosen at app-install time. There is no channel field to set; retargeting means issuing a new webhook URL.
  • This class never sets IntegrationResult.url — a Slack incoming webhook returns no permalink to the posted message.
  • Timeout detection walks the error's cause chain up to MAX_CAUSE_DEPTH (5) looking for a TimeoutError/AbortError, because undici can wrap a connect-phase timeout as 'TypeError: fetch failed'.
  • All Block Kit construction, Slack's character/block ceilings and text escaping live in ./SlackBlocks.ts (buildRunSummaryMessage, clampText, escapeAndClamp, SLACK_LIMITS) — not on this class. Only clampText, buildRunSummaryMessage and DEFAULT_MAX_FAILURES are imported here.

Architecture

Configuration, environments and constants

This is the single layer that decides *what* a run targets and *how* it behaves. `config/environment.config.ts` reads `config/environments/<TEST_ENV>.json`, layers environment-variable overrides on top, and returns a `ResolvedEnvironment` whose `credentialsFor()`, `apiKey()` and `isEnabled()` resolve secrets and feature switches lazily — so no password or API key ever lives in a committed JSON file, only the *name* of the variable that carries it. `config/framework.config.ts` sits beside it and answers the orthogonal question of execution shape (headless, workers, retries, logging, run id), giving every knob a safe default plus an env-var override so the same config serves a laptop and a CI matrix with no conditional logic in tests. `src/constants/` holds the non-negotiable, environment-independent facts — absolute `PATHS` resolved from the module URL rather than `process.cwd()`, `VIEWPORTS`, the `SENSITIVE_KEYS` masking list, REST routes/status codes, and the tag/suite taxonomy.

Environment files4 — dev.json (55 lines), qa.json (39), uat.json (39), prod.json (38), all under config/environments/
VALID_ENVIRONMENTS['dev', 'qa', 'uat', 'prod'] — TEST_ENV defaults to 'dev'
Required keys asserted per environment file5 — name, ui.baseUrl, api.baseUrl, timeouts, retries
frameworkConfig tunables13 fields on FrameworkExecutionConfig
DEFAULT: headlessbool(HEADLESS, isCi) — false locally, true on CI
DEFAULT: slowMoMsint(SLOW_MO, 0)
DEFAULT: workersint(WORKERS, isCi ? 2 : Math.max(1, Math.min(6, Math.floor(cpus().length / 2))))
DEFAULT: retriesint(RETRIES, isCi ? environment.retries.ci : environment.retries.local)
DEFAULT: logLevelLOG_LEVEL ?? (isCi ? 'INFO' : 'DEBUG')
DEFAULT: logToFilebool(LOG_TO_FILE, true)
DEFAULT: extentEnabledbool(EXTENT_REPORT, true)
DEFAULT: reuseAuthStatebool(REUSE_AUTH_STATE, true)

DEFAULT: referenceAppPortint(DEMO_APP_PORT, 4321)
DEFAULT: verboseApiLoggingbool(VERBOSE_API_LOGGING, !isCi)
DEFAULT: runIdRUN_ID ?? new Date().toISOString().replace(/[:.]/g, '-')

PATHS entries19 absolute directories, all resolved from ROOT_DIR

qa/uat/prod timeoutstest 90000, action 20000, navigation 45000, expect 15000, api 30000 (all three files identical)
API retry profiledev: apiMaxAttempts 2 / apiBackoffMs 250; qa+uat: 3 / 500; prod: 3 / 750

PERFORMANCE_BUDGETSpageLoadMs 5000, apiResponseMs 2000, searchDebounceMs 400 — declared in TestConstants.ts but no consumer found elsewhere in the repo
HTTP_STATUS / API_ERROR_CODES15 status constants, 8 contracted error codes; RETRYABLE_STATUS_CODES = [429, 500, 502, 503]
IDEMPOTENT_METHODS['GET', 'HEAD', 'OPTIONS', 'PUT', 'DELETE'] — a non-idempotent method drops to 1 attempt in ApiClient
Roles configuredUserRole type has 5 values (ADMIN, MANAGER, EMPLOYEE, STUDENT, MENTOR); dev/qa/uat configure 3, prod configures 2 (no MANAGER)

TEST_DATA_PREFIX'pwauto' — prefixed onto every generated record by RandomUtils so cleanup can find its own data

How it runs
  1. Pick the environment name `resolveEnvironmentName()` reads `process.env.TEST_ENV`, applies `(raw ?? 'dev').trim().toLowerCase()`, and throws `EnvironmentConfigurationError('Unknown TEST_ENV "…". Expected one of: dev, qa, uat, prod.')` if it is not in `VALID_ENVIRONMENTS`. CI workflows set it (`playwright.yml` → 'dev', `regression.yml` → 'qa', `smoke.yml` → 'dev'); npm scripts set it via cross-env (`test:qa`, `test:prod`, …). config/environment.config.ts:23,45-53
  2. Check the per-process cache `getEnvironment(name)` looks the name up in `const cache = new Map<EnvironmentName, ResolvedEnvironment>()` and returns the hit immediately; only a miss calls `buildEnvironment(name)` and stores the result. Every worker process pays the file read exactly once per environment name. config/environment.config.ts:141-152
  3. Load .env once, without clobbering CI secrets `buildEnvironment` calls `loadDotEnvOnce()`, which is guarded by a module-level `dotenvLoaded` flag and only fires if `resolve(PATHS.root, '.env')` exists: `dotenv.config({ path: envFile, override: false, quiet: true })`. The `override: false` is the point — as the comment says, values already in `process.env` (CI secrets) always win over the local file. config/environment.config.ts:25-35,89
  4. Read and validate the JSON definition `readDefinition()` resolves `${name}.json` under `PATHS.environments`, throws `Environment file not found: …` if absent, and wraps a JSON parse failure as `Environment file … is not valid JSON: …`. `assertDefinitionShape()` then collects missing required keys — `name`, `ui.baseUrl`, `api.baseUrl`, `timeouts`, `retries` — and throws one message listing all of them. config/environment.config.ts:55-84
  5. Layer environment-variable overrides on the URLs `UI_BASE_URL ?? definition.ui.baseUrl` and `API_BASE_URL ?? definition.api.baseUrl`, each passed through `stripTrailingSlash = (url) => url.replace(/\/+$/, '')` so a trailing slash in either source cannot produce a double slash downstream. `isCi` is computed here as `process.env.CI === 'true' || process.env.CI === '1'`. config/environment.config.ts:86,92-94
  6. Return the definition spread with three lazy resolvers The returned object is `{ ...definition, ui: {…overridden baseUrl}, api: {…overridden baseUrl}, isCi, credentialsFor, apiKey, isEnabled }`. Nothing secret is read at build time — the resolvers close over `definition` and read `process.env` on call. config/environment.config.ts:96-138
  7. credentialsFor(role) — three-tier resolution 1) Look up `definition.roles[role]`; if the role is not configured, throw naming the file to fix (`Add it to config/environments/<name>.json`). 2) Read `process.env[source.usernameEnv]` and `process.env[source.passwordEnv]`; return them only when **both** are non-empty. 3) Only if `definition.allowInsecureDefaults && source.sandboxUsername && source.sandboxPassword`, fall back to the published sandbox pair. Otherwise throw, naming both env vars and pointing at `.env.example`. config/environment.config.ts:102-122
  8. apiKey() — same shape, optional result Returns `undefined` when the environment declares no `api.apiKeyEnv`; otherwise `process.env[keyEnv]` if set; otherwise `definition.api.sandboxApiKey` but only when `allowInsecureDefaults` is true; otherwise `undefined`. `ApiClient.buildHeaders` calls it and sets `x-api-key` only if a value came back. config/environment.config.ts:124-133; src/api/clients/ApiClient.ts:158-159
  9. isEnabled(feature) — default-false feature switches `return definition.features[feature as string] === true;` — a strict identity check, so a missing key, `undefined`, or any non-boolean value all read as disabled. `FeatureFlags` carries an index signature (`readonly [feature: string]: boolean | undefined`) so teams can add switches without touching the core. config/environment.config.ts:135-137; src/types/Environment.ts:44-50
  10. framework.config.ts resolves execution shape at import time `const environment = getEnvironment(); const isCi = environment.isCi;` run at module load, so importing `frameworkConfig` transitively resolves the default TEST_ENV environment. Each field then goes through `bool(value, fallback)` (accepts '1' | 'true' | 'yes' | 'on' after trim+lowercase; empty or undefined → fallback) or `int(value, fallback)` (`Number.parseInt(value ?? '', 10)`, fallback when not finite). config/framework.config.ts:13-24,46-72
  11. playwright.config.ts assembles the run from both modules Timeouts come from `environment.timeouts` (test/expect/action/navigation), `retries`/`workers`/`forbidOnly`/`headless`/`slowMo` from `frameworkConfig`, report output folders from `PATHS`, project viewports from `VIEWPORTS`, and the ExtentReporter is appended only when `frameworkConfig.extentEnabled`. playwright.config.ts:22-68
  12. The webServer block self-disables outside the sandbox `...(frameworkConfig.startReferenceApp ? { webServer: { command: 'node demo-app/server.mjs', url: `${environment.api.baseUrl}/health`, reuseExistingServer: !frameworkConfig.isCi, timeout: 30_000, env: { DEMO_APP_PORT: String(frameworkConfig.referenceAppPort) } } } : {})` — point an environment file at a deployed URL and the whole key vanishes from the config. playwright.config.ts:143-155
  13. global-setup fails fast on configuration before spending a browser Step 3 iterates `ROLES_TO_AUTHENTICATE = ['ADMIN','MANAGER','EMPLOYEE']` and calls `environment.credentialsFor(role)` purely for its throw, guarded by `if (environment.roles[role])` so prod's missing MANAGER is skipped rather than failing. Step 4 polls `${environment.api.baseUrl}/health` for 60 s, and its failure hint names `TEST_ENV`, `UI_BASE_URL`/`API_BASE_URL` and the reference app. global-setup.ts:32,149-155,88-94
  14. Tests receive the environment as a worker-scoped fixture `baseTest` exposes `environment: [async ({}, use) => { await use(getEnvironment()); }, { scope: 'worker' }]` and `execution` returning `frameworkConfig`; an auto fixture annotates each test with `${environment.displayName} (${environment.name})` and the UI base URL for the report. src/fixtures/base.fixture.ts:36-73
Design decisions21
Environment JSON files store the *names* of credential variables, never the credentials themselves.
A committed config file can be read by anyone with repo access, so putting a password in one is a leak by construction. Indirection lets the same JSON serve a laptop reading `.env` and CI injecting repository secrets.
`allowInsecureDefaults` is a per-environment escape hatch, true only in dev.json.
The framework ships with a bundled reference app so a fresh clone runs end to end with no setup — that needs *some* working credentials. Making it an explicit per-file boolean means the sandbox convenience physically cannot leak into a real environment: qa, uat and prod set it false and carry no sandbox values at all.
Sandbox credentials are used only when *both* env vars are absent — a partially-set pair is an error, not a silent fallback.
Returning the sandbox identity because someone set the username but forgot the password would run a suite as the wrong user and report a green pass. The check `if (username && password) return …` is deliberately all-or-nothing, and the throw names both variables.
`.env` is loaded with `override: false`, once, behind a module flag.
A developer's stale local `.env` must never win over a secret CI injected into the process. Loading once avoids repeated filesystem work when several modules import the config.
`getEnvironment()` memoises in a `Map` keyed by environment name rather than a single module-level constant.
The resolved object is stable per name, so the JSON read and validation happen once per process; keying by name still allows resolving a second environment in the same process without invalidating the first.
Feature flags read through `=== true` rather than truthiness.
An absent key, `undefined`, or a stray string must all mean disabled. Combined with the index signature on `FeatureFlags`, a typo in a flag name fails closed instead of accidentally enabling a suite.
Every execution tunable has a default plus an env-var override, so tests contain no `if (isCi)` branches.
Stated outright in the file header: one configuration must serve both a laptop and a CI matrix. The two coercion helpers (`bool`, `int`) make the override contract uniform.
`headless` defaults to `isCi` — headed locally, headless in CI — and the cost of watching a run is documented rather than hidden.
CI runners have no display server, so a headed launch simply fails; locally a visible browser is the point. The comment additionally warns that headed browsers inherit desktop display scaling (shifting visual baselines) and contend for the GPU.
`startReferenceApp` is double-guarded: the flag AND the UI base URL must actually mention the reference-app port.
Prevents the bundled demo server being launched (and a `webServer` health probe pointed) at a run that targets a deployed environment. As playwright.config.ts puts it, pointing an environment file at a deployed URL makes the block disable itself.
`workers` defaults to 2 on CI and to `Math.max(1, Math.min(6, Math.floor(cpus().length / 2)))` locally.
Shared CI runners are throttled and oversubscribing them produces flake; locally the framework uses half the cores, floored at 1 and capped at 6 so a large workstation does not launch an unbounded browser fleet.
Retries are read from the *environment file*, not hardcoded per CI/local in the execution config.
How flaky a target is, is a property of the target. dev tolerates 0/1, qa/uat/prod 0/2; the execution layer only picks which of the two the current run uses.
`ROOT_DIR` is resolved from `import.meta.url`, explicitly not from `process.cwd()`.
Playwright, saucectl, npm scripts and one-off `node --experimental-strip-types` scripts can all start from different working directories; deriving paths from the module's own location makes every entry in PATHS invariant.
Storage-state files are named `<environment>.<role>.<version>.json` via `authStateFileName()`.
Encoding the environment prevents a dev session being replayed against qa, and `STORAGE_STATE_VERSION = 'v1'` gives a single lever to invalidate every persisted session when the format changes.
`roles` is typed `Readonly<Partial<Record<UserRole, RoleCredentialSource>>>`, so an environment may legitimately omit a persona.
Production runs a read-only smoke and has no MANAGER account; making the record partial forces callers to guard rather than assume, which global-setup does explicitly before authenticating.
Production is fenced by data-shaped flags, not by test-side conventions.
`allowDestructiveTests: false` and `employeeDeletion: false` live in the environment file, so the guard travels with the target rather than depending on every author remembering to tag a spec.
`LOG_LEVEL` is taken as an unvalidated cast in the config and validated at the point of use.
The config layer stays a plain data assembly; the Logger owns the semantics and falls back to INFO for anything not in `LOG_LEVELS`, so a typo degrades gracefully instead of throwing during config load.
`verboseApiLogging` defaults on locally and off in CI, and never covers secrets.
Request/response bodies are what you want while debugging on a laptop and noise in a CI log. The masking is orthogonal and unconditional — bodies go through `maskValue` regardless.
`runId` defaults to a filesystem-safe ISO timestamp and is overridable with `RUN_ID`.
It names the per-run log file and is written into the report's run-context, so CI can pin it to a build number while a local run still gets a unique, sortable value.
tsconfig declares ten `@`-prefixed aliases with `baseUrl: "."`, and the alias for `src/types` is `@app-types/*` rather than `@types/*`.
Specs import across the tree without relative-path chains. Six of the ten are actually used today (`@constants` 17 imports, `@fixtures` 12, `@api` 9, `@data` 6, `@utils` 3); `@config`, `@pages`, `@components`, `@app-types` and `@reporting` are declared but currently unused in source.
`allowImportingTsExtensions: true` is enabled with an explanatory comment, alongside `noEmit`.
Node's `--experimental-strip-types` (used by `npm run sauce:config`) requires the explicit `.ts` specifier on relative imports; it is safe here only because nothing in the project is emitted.
The strictness dial is turned all the way up, including `noUncheckedIndexedAccess`.
Index access on the config records (features, roles, process.env) then yields `T | undefined`, which is precisely what forces the guarded reads in `credentialsFor` and `roles[role]`.
In the source
// playwright.config.ts:18-39 — the whole run derived from the two config modules
import { getEnvironment } from './config/environment.config';
import { frameworkConfig } from './config/framework.config';
import { PATHS, VIEWPORTS } from './src/constants/FrameworkConstants';

const environment = getEnvironment();

/** UI projects run everything except the API-only and visual suites. */
const UI_TEST_IGNORE = ['**/tests/api/**', '**/tests/visual/**'];

const sharedUse = {
  baseURL: environment.ui.baseUrl,
  actionTimeout: environment.timeouts.action,
  navigationTimeout: environment.timeouts.navigation,
  headless: frameworkConfig.headless,
  ignoreHTTPSErrors: false,
  testIdAttribute: 'data-testid',
  /* Diagnostics: captured only when a test fails, so a green run stays cheap. */
  screenshot: 'only-on-failure' as const,
  video: 'retain-on-failure' as const,
  trace: 'retain-on-failure' as const,
  launchOptions: { slowMo: frameworkConfig.slowMoMs },
};

// config/environment.config.ts:102-122 — the three-tier credential resolver
credentialsFor(role: UserRole): Credentials {
  const source = definition.roles[role];
  if (!source) {
    throw new EnvironmentConfigurationError(
      `Role "${role}" is not configured for environment "${definition.name}". ` +
        `Add it to config/environments/${definition.name}.json.`,
    );
  }
  const username = process.env[source.usernameEnv] ?? '';
  const password = process.env[source.passwordEnv] ?? '';
  if (username && password) return { username, password };

  if (definition.allowInsecureDefaults && source.sandboxUsername && source.sandboxPassword) {
    return { username: source.sandboxUsername, password: source.sandboxPassword };
  }
  throw new EnvironmentConfigurationError(
    `Credentials for role "${role}" are unavailable in environment "${definition.name}". ` +
      `Set ${source.usernameEnv} and ${source.passwordEnv} in your .env file or CI secrets. ` +
      `See .env.example.`,
  );
},
Architecture

Fixture chain, authentication and global setup/teardown

The framework never exposes raw `@playwright/test` to a spec. Instead four fixture files are chained by `extend` — base -> pages -> api -> auth — and `src/fixtures/index.ts` re-exports the last link in the chain as `test`, so a single import (`import { test, expect } from '@fixtures/index'`) hands a spec the resolved environment, ready-made Page Objects, authenticated API services, a cleanup tracker, and a browser page that is already signed in as a chosen role. Authentication is minted once per role through the real UI by `AuthenticationManager` and persisted to `storage/auth/`, so the suite pays for login once rather than once per test. `global-setup.ts` validates the environment, asserts test data, waits for health, and creates those sessions — but only when a browser-backed project was actually selected; `global-teardown.ts` deletes the session files afterwards because they contain live tokens.

Fixture layers in the chain4 (base -> pages -> api -> auth)

How it runs
  1. Playwright loads the config and runs globalSetup playwright.config.ts sets `globalSetup: './global-setup.ts'` and `globalTeardown: './global-teardown.ts'`. Setup captures `startedAt`, resolves `getEnvironment()`, computes `selectedProjects(config)` and logs environment, workers, projects and CI flag. playwright.config.ts:47-48, global-setup.ts:119-133
  2. Step 1 — create the directories the run writes into `ensureFrameworkDirectories(REQUIRED_DIRECTORIES)` creates storage/auth, reports/extent, reports/screenshots, reports/downloads and logs before anything else can fail on a missing path. global-setup.ts:136, src/constants/FrameworkConstants.ts:34-40
  3. Step 2 — fail fast on malformed test data `assertDatasetKeys` is called three times: 'login' must have validUsers/invalidScenarios/ui, 'employees' must have templates/departments/validation, 'api' must have endpoints/performance/negative. A missing key throws a TestDataError naming exactly what is missing. global-setup.ts:139-147, src/utils/JsonReader.ts:152-167
  4. Step 3 — fail fast on missing credentials, before any browser launch For each of ROLES_TO_AUTHENTICATE (['ADMIN','MANAGER','EMPLOYEE']) that the environment actually declares, `environment.credentialsFor(role)` is invoked purely for its throw-on-missing behaviour. global-setup.ts:150-152, config/environment.config.ts:102-122
  5. Step 4 — the target must actually be up `waitForEnvironment(environment.api.baseUrl)` polls the absolute URL `${baseUrl}/health` (absolute deliberately: a leading-slash path against a baseURL would drop the API prefix) for up to 60s, 1s between attempts, 5s per request. global-setup.ts:63-95, 155
  6. Step 5 — decide whether a browser is needed, then mint sessions `if (projects.some(requiresBrowser))` launches chromium via `launchSessionBrowser()`, filters ROLES_TO_AUTHENTICATE down to roles the environment declares, and calls `createStorageStates(browser, roles)` in a try/finally that always closes the browser. Otherwise it logs 'no browser-backed project selected — skipping session state creation' and launches nothing. global-setup.ts:162-174
  7. Inside createStorageState — reuse or re-login `hasFreshStorageState(role)` short-circuits to the existing file when it exists, reuseAuthState is on, and it is younger than MAX_STATE_AGE_MS. Otherwise a fresh context drives `new LoginPage(page).open()` then `loginAs(role)` and persists `context.storageState({ path: file })`; failures are rewrapped as a FrameworkError carrying operation, role, environment, page.url() and the expectation, and the context is closed in `finally`. src/fixtures/AuthenticationManager.ts:49-85
  8. Step 6 — write run metadata for the reporter `writeJsonFile(resolve(PATHS.reports, 'run-context.json'), {...})` records runId, startedAt, environment block, execution block (ci, workers, retries, headless, projects) and `process.version`. global-setup.ts:177-194
  9. Per worker — base and api worker fixtures resolve once `environment` and `execution` (base layer) and `apiRequestContext` (api layer) are `{ scope: 'worker' }`, so one resolved environment and one APIRequestContext serve every test that worker runs; the context is disposed after `use`. src/fixtures/base.fixture.ts:37-49, src/fixtures/api.fixture.ts:48-58
  10. Per test — the chain resolves top-down through four layers baseTest gives testData/log plus the auto `runContext` fixture that pushes environment, project and ui-base-url annotations; pageTest builds LoginPage/DashboardPage/EmployeePage/ProfilePage on `page`; apiTest builds apiClient + services, and adminApiClient which calls `new AuthApi(client).authenticateClientAs('ADMIN')` before `use` and `client.clearAuthToken()` after; authTest resolves the `role` option and the authenticated context/page. src/fixtures/base.fixture.ts:63-73, src/fixtures/page.fixture.ts:21-33, src/fixtures/api.fixture.ts:60-89
  11. Per test — authenticated context is built from the stored session `contextForRole(browser, role)` calls `storageStatePath(role)`; if the file is absent it calls `createStorageState(browser, role)` on demand so a single-spec run still works, throws a FrameworkError if it is still absent, then returns `browser.newContext({ storageState: statePath })`. Teardown closes the context and the page. src/fixtures/auth.fixture.ts:37-66
  12. Per test teardown — CleanupTracker removes what the test created The `cleanup` fixture's code after `await use(tracker)` runs as fixture teardown, which Playwright executes whether the test passed, failed or timed out. If any ids were registered it logs the count and calls `adminEmployeeApi.deleteAll(employeeIds)`, which loops `deleteIfExists` — 204 counts as cleaned, 404 is tolerated, anything else is warned, never thrown. src/fixtures/api.fixture.ts:91-108, src/api/services/EmployeeApi.ts:106-122
  13. Run end — teardown finalises the report and deletes sessions If reports/run-context.json exists it is re-written with `finishedAt` and `durationMs`. Then, unless KEEP_AUTH_STATE is '1'/'true'/'yes', `clearStorageStates(ROLES)` deletes the session file for all five roles ('ADMIN','MANAGER','EMPLOYEE','STUDENT','MENTOR'); when it is set, a warning says the files were left under storage/auth. global-teardown.ts:27-53
Design decisions14
Chain the fixtures in a fixed order base -> pages -> api -> auth, and export only the last link
Playwright's `extend` composes one layer onto the previous one, so a later layer may depend on an earlier layer's fixtures but not vice versa. The order encodes the real dependency graph: `testData` needs `environment` (base), `apiRequestContext` needs `environment` (api on base), `cleanup` needs `adminEmployeeApi` (api), and `authenticatedContext` needs `browser` plus everything below it. Exporting `authTest as test` means a spec gets the whole stack from one import and can never accidentally pick up a half-built layer.
Scope `environment`, `execution` and `apiRequestContext` to the worker; everything else to the test
Config resolution and an HTTP context are expensive and stateless across tests, so they are paid for once per worker process. Anything that carries per-test state — logger bound to testInfo, Page Objects bound to a page, the cleanup list, the admin client whose token is cleared after use — must be test-scoped so parallel tests cannot see each other's state.
Make the CleanupTracker an ordinary fixture whose teardown does the deleting, rather than an afterEach hook
Fixture teardown runs on failure and on timeout, so records created by a test that blew up mid-way are still removed and the next run is not polluted. Deletion goes through the ADMIN-authenticated client, so cleanup cannot fail for lack of permission, and `deleteIfExists` swallows 404 so a record the test already deleted does not turn teardown into a second failure.
Expose the role as a Playwright test option (`role: ['ADMIN', { option: true }]`) instead of a login helper
An option can be set per describe-block with `test.use({ role })` and is resolved before the fixture that consumes it, so choosing a persona is declarative and the storage state is selected — not a UI login performed — at the top of the test. ADMIN is the default so the common case needs no declaration, and specs that must exercise the login screen simply take the plain `page` fixture instead of `authenticatedPage`.
Sessions are minted through the real UI login, not by injecting a token
A storage state produced by driving LoginPage is byte-for-byte the state a real user produces — cookies, localStorage and whatever else the app sets — so reusing it cannot mask an auth bug that a token injection would paper over.
Cap session reuse at MAX_STATE_AGE_MS = 45 minutes, gated additionally by frameworkConfig.reuseAuthState
A persisted session holds a real token that the application will eventually expire; reusing a stale file would produce a confusing mid-suite 401 rather than a clean login. The mtime check bounds reuse below any plausible token lifetime, and REUSE_AUTH_STATE=false turns reuse off entirely for debugging.
Name session files `<env>.<role>.v1.json` and key the path on the current environment
A dev session must never be handed to a qa run, and a schema change to what the framework stores can be forced to invalidate every existing file by bumping one constant instead of asking engineers to delete files.
Read the --project flags from process.argv rather than trusting config.projects
Playwright passes global setup the entire FullConfig, not the run's selection, so `config.projects` still lists all nine projects during `--project=api`. Without parsing argv, setup would always think a browser project was selected and would always launch a browser.
Default-safe browser detection: a project needs a browser unless it opts out, and an unrecognised --project name falls back to the full list
Getting this wrong in the permissive direction only wastes a browser launch; getting it wrong in the restrictive direction means UI tests start with no session files. So the opt-out is an explicit `!== false` check on project metadata, and an unmatched flag falls back to every project rather than assuming less work is needed.
Regenerate a missing storage state on demand inside the auth fixture instead of only in global setup
Running one spec in isolation (or via the Playwright UI/debug flows) may not have gone through the same setup path that produced a given role's file; on-demand creation keeps a single-spec run working, and a still-missing file after that attempt is a hard FrameworkError rather than a confusing `newContext` failure.
Teardown deletes every session file by default; keeping them requires an explicit opt-in
The files contain live authentication tokens. Leaving them behind on a shared CI agent or a laptop is a credential-leak surface, so the safe behaviour is the default and KEEP_AUTH_STATE is a deliberate local-debugging escape hatch that logs a warning when used. The same reasoning gitignores the directory.
Teardown clears all five UserRole values, while setup only authenticates three
Setup mints only the personas the suite currently reuses, but teardown must not leave a file behind that some other code path (or an older run) created. Deletion is idempotent — `remove` uses `rmSync(target, { recursive: true, force: true })` — so listing extra roles costs nothing and closes the gap.
Translate a raw chromium launch failure into a FrameworkError that names the fix
A fresh clone that has not run `playwright install` gets an opaque Playwright error; wrapping it turns the most common first-run failure into an instruction, and explicitly notes that API-only runs do not need browsers at all.
The ADMIN API client authenticates before `use` and clears its token after
Setup and seeding need privileged calls, but the underlying APIRequestContext is worker-scoped and shared, so leaving an admin token bound after the test would leak elevated auth into the next test in that worker.
In the source
// tests/hybrid/employee-hybrid.spec.ts — one import, a declared role, and tracked cleanup
import { expect, test } from '@fixtures/index';

test.describe('Employee hybrid journeys @hybrid', () => {
  test.use({ role: 'ADMIN' });

  test.beforeEach(({}, testInfo) => {
    testInfo.annotations.push({ type: 'module', description: MODULES.employeeManagement });
  });

  // ... first test elided ...

  test(`A UI-created record is correct in the backend ${TAGS.hybrid}`, async ({
    employeesAs,
    adminEmployeeApi,
    cleanup,
  }) => {
    const payload = buildEmployee({
      templateKey: 'engineer',
      overrides: { joiningDate: '2024-02-29' },
    });

    await test.step('Create the record through the UI', async () => {

      await employeesAs.createEmployee({ ...payload, active: true });
    });

    await test.step('The API returns exactly what the form submitted', async () => {

Architecture

Page Objects and UI components (src/pages + src/components)

This is the framework's UI abstraction layer: a two-tier Page Object / Component Object Model. `BasePage` is a 974-line abstract class holding every reusable browser interaction — navigation, clicks, input, dropdowns, waits, data extraction, uploads/downloads, native dialogs, tabs, iframes, screenshots, scrolling, network interception and localStorage — organised into 16 banner-delimited sections, so a concrete page owns nothing but locators and business workflows. `BaseComponent` is the parallel root for reusable screen *regions* (header, sidebar, table, modal, toast, pagination, search, date picker), each scoped to a root `Locator` that every internal locator descends from; pages compose these instances instead of duplicating their selectors. The unifying mechanism in both tiers is a `perform()` wrapper that logs `action -> target` at DEBUG and, on any failure, rethrows a `UiActionError` carrying the operation, target, page class, URL, environment and timeout — so a CI failure is diagnosable from the log alone without reproducing it.

BasePage.ts size974 lines, 31,633 bytes — the largest file in src/pages
Public members on BasePage77 public methods, plus the `rawPage` getter and the abstract `rootIndicator` property
BasePage sections16 banner-delimited sections: internals, navigation, clicks, input, dropdowns, checkbox/radio, element state, data extraction, mouse, file transfer, browser interaction, frames, screenshots, scrolling, network, storage

How it runs
  1. A fixture constructs the Page Object The spec declares `{ employeePage }` (fresh page) or `{ employeesAs }` (stored session for the role in `test.use({ role })`); the fixture does `await use(new EmployeePage(page))`. No spec ever calls `new` on a page or builds a locator. src/fixtures/page.fixture.ts:28 and src/fixtures/auth.fixture.ts:72
  2. The constructor builds locators and composes components BasePage's constructor stores the page, calls `getEnvironment()` and `createLogger(new.target.name)` — so the logger is named after the concrete subclass. The subclass then assigns its Locators and instantiates its components: EmployeePage creates HeaderComponent, SidebarComponent, ToastComponent, TableComponent({testId:'employee-table', rowTestId:'employee-row', emptyState}), SearchComponent, PaginationComponent, two ModalComponents (`employee-modal`, `confirm-modal`) and a DatePickerComponent. src/pages/BasePage.ts:57 and src/pages/EmployeePage.ts:54-86
  3. Form fields are scoped to the component that owns them `const form = this.formModal.root;` then `form.getByLabel('Full name')` etc. The comment states why: "Form fields are scoped to the dialog: the filter bar also renders a 'Department' label." LoginPage does the same for its error: `page.getByRole('main').getByRole('alert')`, because the toast region also publishes role="alert". src/pages/EmployeePage.ts:77-85, src/pages/LoginPage.ts:39-40
  4. The spec calls open() `open()` = `navigate()` + `waitUntilLoaded()`. navigate() composes `${environment.ui.baseUrl}${path}` and goes there with waitUntil 'domcontentloaded' and the environment's navigation timeout; waitUntilLoaded() waits for the abstract `rootIndicator` to be visible. src/pages/BasePage.ts:140-159
  5. The spec calls a business workflow, not DOM steps `createEmployee(input)` = openCreateForm() → fillEmployeeForm(input) → submitForm() → formModal.expectClosed() → toast.expectSuccess('Employee created'). fillEmployeeForm only touches fields the caller supplied, routing joiningDate through `joiningDatePicker.selectDate()` and `active` through `setChecked`. src/pages/EmployeePage.ts:103-128
  6. Each primitive delegates to perform() `click()` resolves the Target to a Locator and calls `.click({ timeout: options.timeout ?? this.environment.timeouts.action, force: options.force ?? false, clickCount: options.clickCount ?? 1, … })` inside `this.perform('click', target, …)`. There are no sleeps anywhere — the class header states Playwright auto-waiting is the waiting strategy. src/pages/BasePage.ts:199-214
  7. perform() logs the action It computes a label (options.description, else the selector string, else String(locator)) and calls `this.log.action(operation, label)`, which writes `${action} -> ${target}` at DEBUG. src/pages/BasePage.ts:84-88, src/utils/Logger.ts:91
  8. A raw Playwright failure is converted into a UiActionError The catch block throws `new UiActionError(`UI action "${operation}" failed`, { operation, target: label, page: this.constructor.name, url: this.safeUrl(), environment: this.environment.name, timeout: options.timeout ?? this.environment.timeouts.action }, error)`. `safeUrl()` returns '(page closed)' instead of throwing when the page is gone. src/pages/BasePage.ts:91-113
  9. FrameworkError renders the context into the message Non-empty context entries become indented `key: value` lines, the cause's message is appended as `cause: …`, the original Error is kept as the ES `cause` option, and `this.name = new.target.name` so the class shows as UiActionError. src/utils/FrameworkError.ts:37-52
  10. Component calls take the same path with component context BaseComponent.perform has the narrower `(operation, target: string, action)` signature and throws `Component action "${operation}" failed` with operation/target/page/url/environment. TableComponent.clickRowAction, PaginationComponent.getState and SidebarComponent.ensureVisible all raise UiActionError through it. src/components/BaseComponent.ts:33-54
  11. Domain-specific failures throw UiActionError directly, with expected/actual TableComponent.getColumnIndex throws with `actual: 'available columns: …'`; PaginationComponent.getState throws with `expected: 'Page <n> of <n> · <total> records'` and the actual summary text; BasePage.frameByName throws listing every frame URL. src/components/TableComponent.ts:65-72, src/components/PaginationComponent.ts:34-41, src/pages/BasePage.ts:859-868
  12. Assertions are delegated back to the components `employeePage.expectEmployeeRow(input)` forwards to `table.expectRowMatching({Name, Email, Department, Designation})`; `deleteEmployee` drives confirmModal then the spec asserts `toast.expectSuccess('Employee deleted')`. The spec never names a CSS selector. src/pages/EmployeePage.ts:152-203
Design decisions19
Route every browser interaction through one `perform()` wrapper instead of calling Playwright directly
It buys uniform DEBUG logging and error enrichment for free on all 77 methods, so a CI failure is diagnosable from the log without reproducing it locally — and it can never silently swallow a failure, because the catch always rethrows.
Accept `Target = Locator | string` on every action and normalise internally
Callers can pass a ready-made semantic Locator (the normal case) or an ad-hoc selector string without a second API, and page objects never need a `page.locator()` call of their own.
Two abstract members — `path` and `rootIndicator` — are the entire subclass contract
They let generic `navigate()`, `open()`, `waitUntilLoaded()` and `isLoaded()` work for any screen without the base class knowing anything about the application.
No arbitrary sleeps; every wait is either Playwright auto-waiting, a web-first assertion, or a wait on the real backing response
Sleeps are the classic source of flake and of tests that pass for the wrong reason. Waiting on the business request also makes the wait self-documenting.
Prefer role- and label-based locators; use `data-testid` for elements with no accessible semantics
Role/label locators assert accessibility as a side effect and survive markup churn; test ids cover the plumbing (metric tiles, table rows, toasts) where no meaningful role exists. `testIdAttribute` is configured once so `getByTestId` resolves the app's own attribute.
Scope ambiguous locators to a container rather than adding `.first()` or a brittle CSS path
Two regions of the same screen legitimately expose the same role or label; scoping states which one is meant and keeps the failure honest if the intended one disappears.
Components are scoped to a root Locator and composed into pages, never inherited
A header change is made once no matter how many screens render it; the same class serves any screen because it never knows which one opened it.
Components are configurable by an options object with defaults, so one class covers several instances on one page
EmployeePage needs two different dialogs from the same class; the table needs a non-default row test id and an empty-state locator.
The responsive difference lives in the component, not in the spec
The same UI spec runs on the chromium, tablet-ipad, mobile-chrome and mobile-safari projects; if the test had to branch on viewport the suite would double.
Boolean state queries never throw; explicit waits do
Conditional flows need a safe probe (`isVisible`, `isLoaded`, `isHidden` catch and return false), while `waitForVisible`/`waitUntilLoaded` must fail the test loudly. Keeping them as separate methods stops a swallowed timeout from hiding a defect.
Force-clicking is available but explicitly discouraged in the doc comment
Bypassing actionability checks can mask a real overlay/regression defect, so the API makes the trade-off visible at the call site.
Domain errors carry `expected` and `actual`, not just a message
The ErrorContext type has dedicated `expected`/`actual` fields, so a parse or lookup failure prints what it wanted and what it got instead of a generic 'not found'.
Assertion failures include the rendered state in the failure message
A bare 'expected true, got false' on a row match is useless in CI; dumping every rendered row turns a screenshot hunt into a read.
Table header matching is case-insensitive
A stylesheet `text-transform` can change the header text the DOM reports, which would otherwise break a correct assertion.
The logger is named from `new.target.name` while the error context uses `this.constructor.name`
Both resolve to the concrete subclass (LoginPage, TableComponent…) rather than the base, so log lines and error payloads name the real screen or region.
Credentials are resolved inside the page object from the environment, never passed as literals by a spec
Keeps secrets out of test source and lets the same journey run against dev/qa/uat with CI-supplied values.
Downloads and screenshots are written to framework-owned directories via `ensureDirectory(PATHS.…)`
Artefacts land in a predictable place (reports/downloads, reports/screenshots) regardless of the process working directory — PATHS is resolved from the module URL, not `process.cwd()`.
Page objects can capture the exact payload the page rendered from, instead of re-querying the API
Suites run `fullyParallel: true`, so a second API call can legitimately return a different total than the one the tiles were built from — comparing against the captured response removes that whole class of false failure.
Network interception is a first-class page capability, and tests clean it up
Empty and error states are hard to produce with real data; `mockJsonResponse` makes them deterministic, and `clearRoutes()` (unrouteAll with behavior 'ignoreErrors') keeps the stub from leaking.
In the source
/* tests/ui/e2e/employee-lifecycle.e2e.spec.ts — the spec reads as the workflow, not as DOM steps */

const employee = buildEmployee({ templateKey: 'engineer' });
const promotion = { designation: 'Lead Automation Engineer', salary: 1_650_000 };

await test.step('3. Open employee management', async () => {
  await dashboardPage.navigateToEmployees();
  await employeePage.expectLoaded();
});

await test.step('4. Create the employee', async () => {
  await employeePage.createEmployee({ ...employee, active: true });
});

await test.step('5. Find the new employee', async () => {
  await employeePage.searchFor(employee.email);
  await employeePage.expectEmployeeRow(employee);
  cleanup.employee(await employeePage.getEmployeeIdByName(employee.name));
});

await test.step('9. Remove the employee', async () => {
  await employeePage.deleteEmployee(employee.name);
  await employeePage.toast.expectSuccess('Employee deleted');
  await employeePage.expectEmployeeAbsent(employee.name);
});

/* src/pages/EmployeePage.ts — what `createEmployee` actually is: components, composed */

/** Creates an employee through the UI and waits for the success toast. */
public async createEmployee(input: EmployeeFormInput): Promise&lt;void&gt; {
  await this.openCreateForm();
  await this.fillEmployeeForm(input);
  await this.submitForm();
  await this.formModal.expectClosed();
  await this.toast.expectSuccess('Employee created');
}
Architecture

API testing layer (src/api)

The API layer is a four-tier stack: `ApiClient` is the single HTTP entry point (URL building, headers/auth, retries, parsing, masked logging); domain services (`AuthApi`, `UserApi`, `EmployeeApi`) extending `BaseApiService` wrap it so specs never assemble raw HTTP; `ResponseValidator` (reached via `verify()`) offers a fluent, self-describing assertion chain over the parsed response; and `SchemaValidator` runs AJV JSON-Schema contract checks against the typed schemas in `src/api/models/schemas.ts`. Every response is normalised into an `ApiResponse<T>` that carries not only status/body but the diagnostics validators and reports need — `durationMs`, `requestId`, `url` and `method` — which is what lets a failed assertion name the exact endpoint it was checking. It exists so that a test expresses intent (`adminEmployeeApi.list({ pageSize: 5 })`, `verify(r).isSuccessful().matchesSchema(...)`) rather than transport mechanics, and so secrets never reach a log line or CI artifact.

A fixture builds the client `apiRequestContext` is worker-scoped (`playwrightRequest.newContext({ baseURL: environment.api.baseUrl, ignoreHTTPSErrors: false })`). `apiClient` is unauthenticated; `adminApiClient` calls `new AuthApi(client).authenticateClientAs('ADMIN')` before use and `client.clearAuthToken()` after. src/fixtures/api.fixture.ts:48-81

Constructor resolves environment defaults baseUrl = `options.baseUrl ?? environment.api.baseUrl` with trailing slashes stripped (`.replace(/\/+$/, '')`); timeout = `environment.timeouts.api`; maxAttempts = `environment.retries.apiMaxAttempts`; defaultHeaders start as Accept + Content-Type `application/json`. src/api/clients/ApiClient.ts:63-75
  3. A test calls a domain service, never a raw path e.g. `EmployeeApi.list()` passes `API_ROUTES.employees.root` with a `query` object of search/department/page/pageSize/sortBy/sortOrder; `getById` uses `API_ROUTES.employees.byId(id)`, which itself does `encodeURIComponent(id)`. src/api/services/EmployeeApi.ts:21-36
  4. buildUrl substitutes path params, then fails loudly on leftovers Each `pathParams` entry replaces `:name` with `encodeURIComponent(String(value))`. It then runs `/:([A-Za-z_][A-Za-z0-9_]*)/` over the result and throws `ApiRequestError('Unresolved path parameter')` naming the missing key — so a typo becomes an explicit error, not a 404. The path is joined to baseUrl through `new URL(...)`, adding a leading `/` if absent. src/api/clients/ApiClient.ts:130-146
  5. buildUrl appends the query string, skipping empties `for (const [key, value] of Object.entries(options.query ?? {})) if (value !== undefined && value !== '') url.searchParams.set(key, String(value));` — undefined and empty-string values are dropped, which is why services can pass a full optional-query object unconditionally. src/api/clients/ApiClient.ts:147-150
  6. buildHeaders picks exactly one auth scheme Defaults merge with per-call headers. If `skipAuth` is falsy: `useApiKey` sets `x-api-key` from `environment.apiKey()` (only when that returns a value), else a stored bearer token sets `Authorization: Bearer <token>`. If `skipAuth` is true it actively `delete`s both `Authorization` and `x-api-key`, so a header inherited from defaultHeaders cannot leak into an unauthenticated negative test. `correlationId` becomes `x-correlation-id`. src/api/clients/ApiClient.ts:153-170
  7. send() decides the attempt budget from the method `options.maxAttempts ?? (IDEMPOTENT_METHODS.includes(method) ? this.maxAttempts : 1)`. IDEMPOTENT_METHODS is `['GET', 'HEAD', 'OPTIONS', 'PUT', 'DELETE']` — POST and PATCH get one attempt unless the caller overrides. src/api/clients/ApiClient.ts:180-181
  8. The outbound line is logged with everything masked `this.log.debug('-> ' + method + ' ' + maskUrl(url), { headers: maskHeaders(headers), body: frameworkConfig.verboseApiLogging ? maskValue(options.body) : undefined })`. The body is only rendered when verbose logging is on (default `!isCi`). src/api/clients/ApiClient.ts:183-186
  9. The fetch runs inside withRetry `request.fetch(url, { method, headers, timeout, ...data })`. Data is `Buffer.from(options.rawBody, 'utf8')` when rawBody is set, else `JSON.stringify(options.body)` when body is set, else nothing. If the response status is in RETRYABLE_STATUS_CODES (429, 500, 502, 503) **and** `attempts > 1`, it throws `ApiRequestError('Retryable status received')` to trigger a retry. src/api/clients/ApiClient.ts:189-214
  10. withRetry backs off with full jitter, or gives up with a wrapped error `retryOn` accepts an `ApiRequestError` or an Error whose message matches `/ECONNRESET|ECONNREFUSED|socket hang up|timeout/i`; baseDelayMs is `environment.retries.apiBackoffMs`; delay is `Math.round(Math.random() * Math.min(maxDelayMs, baseDelayMs * 2 ** (attempt - 1)))` capped at 4000ms. Any final failure is re-wrapped as `ApiRequestError('API request failed')` carrying operation, target, environment, timeout and attempts. src/api/clients/ApiClient.ts:215-236, src/utils/RetryUtils.ts:28-76
  11. parse() normalises the response into ApiResponse 204 becomes `{ success: true }` without reading the body; an empty body becomes `{ success: raw.ok() }`; otherwise `JSON.parse(text)`. A parse failure throws `ApiRequestError('API response was not valid JSON')` with the first 300 characters as `actual`. It then flattens `body.data`, `body.error` and `body.meta` onto the result alongside `durationMs`, `requestId` (from the `x-request-id` header), `url` and `method`, and logs the `<- status method url (Nms)` line. src/api/clients/ApiClient.ts:241-295

The test asserts through verify() `verify(response)` wraps it in `ResponseValidator`, whose `label` getter is `${method} ${url}` — every failure message names the endpoint, and most also append `payloadPreview` (`JSON.stringify(body).slice(0, 500)`). Each check returns `this`; `unwrap()` ends the chain by asserting data is defined and returning it as `T`. src/api/validators/ResponseValidator.ts:21-27, 197-209

Contract checks go through AJV `matchesSchema(schema)` calls `assertSchema(this.response.data, schema, label + ' data')`; `matchesEnvelopeSchema(schema)` validates `this.response.body` instead. `compile()` caches by `schema.title ?? JSON.stringify(schema)` in a module-level Map, so each schema is compiled once per process; `formatErrors` renders each AJV error as ` <instancePath or (root)> <message>` on its own line. src/api/validators/ResponseValidator.ts:179-187, src/api/validators/SchemaValidator.ts:15-53

Teardown deletes what the test created The `cleanup` fixture collects ids via `cleanup.employee(id)` and, after `use`, calls `adminEmployeeApi.deleteAll(ids)`, which routes each id through `deleteIfExists` — 204 logs a cleanup, 404 returns false silently, anything else logs a warning rather than failing teardown. src/fixtures/api.fixture.ts:91-108, src/api/services/EmployeeApi.ts:106-122
Design decisions18
rawBody is sent as a Buffer, not a string, so malformed JSON survives the trip
Playwright re-serialises a *string* `data` when the content type is JSON, which would silently repair the broken payload the negative test is trying to send — the test would then pass for the wrong reason.
Only idempotent methods are retried; POST and PATCH default to a single attempt
Retrying a create would duplicate records. The framework's own retry doc states retries must not mask defects, so the budget is derived from the verb rather than applied uniformly.
A retryable status only throws when there is a retry budget left
It keeps a 429/503 on a POST (or on a single-attempt call) as an ordinary, assertable `ApiResponse` instead of an exception — the retry machinery is opt-in via the attempt budget, never a hidden failure mode.
skipAuth deletes credential headers rather than merely not adding them
Credentials can arrive from `options.defaultHeaders` or per-call `headers`, so simply skipping the add would let a 401 test accidentally authenticate.
An unresolved `:param` throws instead of being sent
A literal `:id` in a URL would produce a confusing 404 from the server; failing at build time names the exact missing key.
Every logged URL, header bag and body passes through DataMasker first
Passwords, tokens, cookies, Authorization headers and API keys must never appear in a log line, an Extent report or a CI artifact.
Bodies are only logged when verbose API logging is enabled, which defaults off in CI
Keeps CI logs small and reduces the surface for accidental payload disclosure, while local debugging still shows full traffic.
Compiled AJV validators are cached in a module-level Map keyed by schema title
Avoids recompiling the same schema for every assertion in a run; the `title` also doubles as the default label in failure messages.
AJV runs with `allErrors: true, strict: false, allowUnionTypes: true` plus ajv-formats
allErrors lists every violation in one failure rather than stopping at the first; ajv-formats is what makes `format: 'email'` and `format: 'date-time'` in the schemas actually enforce anything.
Schemas are typed TypeScript objects, not loose JSON files
A schema change fails compilation when the matching TypeScript model is not updated alongside it, keeping wire types and contracts in lockstep.
Most schemas set `additionalProperties: true`, but paginationMetaSchema sets `false`
Payloads may grow new fields without breaking contract tests, whereas pagination meta is a closed, fully specified shape where a stray key signals a real contract drift.
Three schema entry points with different failure modes: assert, throw, or report
A test should fail via Playwright's expect; a service that must not proceed needs an exception; a conditional/reporting check must not fail at all.
`AuthApi.login` returns the raw envelope while `loginAs` throws
Negative tests need to assert a rejected login as data; setup code needs a hard failure with context so a bad precondition is not mistaken for a later assertion failure.
Every validator failure message carries the endpoint and a payload preview
A bare `expected 200, got 500` in a suite of dozens of API calls does not identify which call failed or why.
`withToken` clones the client onto the same APIRequestContext
Role impersonation needs a second identity without paying for a second HTTP context; the clone copies baseUrl, defaultHeaders, timeout, maxAttempts and logger.
`deleteIfExists` never fails teardown
A record the test already deleted, or one the API protects, must not turn a passing test red during cleanup.
Eventual consistency is handled by polling, not by sleeping
A record created through the API may not be searchable immediately; `pollUntil` retries the read on a fixed interval and throws with the last observed value if it never appears.
`BaseApiService` names its logger from `new.target.name`
Log lines are attributed to the concrete service (AuthApi, EmployeeApi) without each subclass repeating its own name.

Architecture

Reporting and outbound integrations (Extent report + Slack/Jira/Zephyr/Sauce)

The reporting layer is a Playwright `Reporter` implementation that normalises every test result into a plain data model (`ExtentReportModel`) and renders it to a single self-contained HTML document plus a JSON twin, in a timestamped folder under `reports/extent/`. Collection (`ExtentReporter.ts`) is kept strictly apart from presentation (`ExtentHtml.ts`) so a styling change can never disturb result gathering, and every string that reaches the model passes through `maskString` first, so no password, bearer token or API key can be published in an artifact. Hanging off the end of the run is a small integration registry: four opt-in outbound targets — Slack, Jira, Zephyr Scale and Sauce Labs — that turn the finished model into an action elsewhere. Their outcomes are folded back into the model as `IntegrationResult` rows so the report itself records what was published, and the whole batch is written so it can never fail the suite it is reporting on.

Text-bodied attachments are separately written out masked as `<testId>-<retry>-<name>.txt`. src/reporting/ExtentReporter.ts:283
