Design decisions38
Retried tests are collapsed in a Map keyed by test id rather than appended to an array
Playwright fires onTestEnd once per attempt, so a retried test would contribute several rows and appear as both FAIL and FLAKY, skewing total, failed and pass rate away from what Playwright itself reports.
The failing attempt's error and artifacts are carried forward onto the winning row
The latest attempt decides the outcome, but the earlier attempt's evidence is what explains a flake. Concatenation is collision-free because attachment files are namespaced `<testId>-<retry>-<name>`.
An empty run refuses to advance latest.html / latest.json
latest.html is what `npm run report:open` opens. A run that reported nothing — unknown --project, failed global setup, --list — would otherwise replace the last real report with an empty one and leave the reader believing the suite had zero tests.
latest.html is rendered a second time with the run folder as an assetBase prefix
Attachment paths in the model are relative to the run folder that owns the files; latest.html sits one level above it, so without the prefix every screenshot, video and trace link resolves to a path that does not exist.
Masking is applied in the reporter, not in the renderer
It makes one file the choke point: the reporter's stated contract is that nothing reaches the report raw, so the HTML layer can assume the model is already clean.
The report is a single self-contained file — no CDN, no web font, no external reference
It is opened straight off disk over file:// and mailed around as one attachment, so an external link would leave a client staring at an unstyled page on a locked-down laptop.
Tabs, filter toolbar and animations degrade to a readable stacked document without JavaScript
A script-less viewer must get every section including the test list, not a blank shell; the donut and bars animate from CSS keyframes so the final geometry is the element's own resting style.
TIMEOUT and INTERRUPTED are failures everywhere in the document
So a run can never present two different failure counts across headline, donut, group tables and filters.
Skipped tests are excluded from the pass-rate denominator
They never ran, so they are not part of any pass-rate population; flaky tests count toward the numerator because they ultimately passed.
Integrations run before the HTML is rendered, and the field is omitted entirely when empty
Their outcome becomes part of the artifact rather than something only the console saw; and a run with nothing configured shows an honest empty state instead of inventing rows.
Integrations are constructed from factories, not held as module-level instances
Constructing a notifier reads the environment, and a throw there would take down the module import — and with it the entire reporter.
A disabled integration still returns a row carrying disabledReason()
The report says why a target was inactive rather than silently omitting it; disabledReason() is itself wrapped so even a throwing reason produces a sentence.
publishIntegrations defends against a publish() that throws even though the contract forbids it
Trust but verify: an unhandled rejection at the end of a run would be attributed to the suite that just went green.
The whole integration batch is bounded by a 60s wall-clock budget
An unresponsive endpoint must not hold a CI job open after the tests have finished; targets past the deadline are reported as not attempted rather than dropped.
Slack sends exactly one run-summary message, never one per failure
A per-test loop would breach Slack's one-request-per-second webhook limit and bury the signal; the summary names the first few failures and defers the rest to the report.
The Slack webhook URL is treated as the credential and scrubbed before truncation
SLACK_WEBHOOK_URL embeds the workspace/app/secret path segments — there is no Authorization header. Scrubbing must run before clamping because half a leaked URL is still a leaked credential and no longer matches the pattern that would have caught it.
Slack's fetch uses redirect: 'error' plus AbortSignal.timeout
A webhook answering with a redirect is either misconfigured or intercepted, and following it would POST the run summary to an unvetted host; the signal caps request, response and body stream together.
Slack clamps on code points, and escapes before clamping
Cutting between the halves of a surrogate pair leaves a lone surrogate that Slack treats as a malformed payload; and escaping after clamping could exceed the limit because `&` grows to five characters.
A run with zero tests is announced to Slack as ':warning: reported no tests', not as passed
Zero failures out of zero tests is what a bad --grep, an unknown --project or a crashed global setup looks like; calling that green would teach the channel to trust nothing.
Jira groups failures per issue: one comment per issue, and at most one Bug for the unlinked remainder
A comment per failing test turns a five-failure regression into five notifications on the same ticket, and a ticket is read by people.
Jira requires JIRA_ENABLED on top of all four credentials
Default-deny: a fork or a CI job without secrets makes no network call at all, and this integration writes to other people's tickets.
JIRA_ISSUE_KEY_PREFIXES narrows the broad issue-key regex
ISSUE_KEY_PATTERN also matches a browser tag like @CHROME-131 or a stray TODO-4 — and this integration writes, so a false positive posts a comment on a stranger's ticket.
Jira comments are posted sequentially, never in parallel, and writes are never retried
Jira rate-limits writes per issue, and POST has no idempotency key — retrying a timed-out write duplicates the comment or files the bug twice.
Jira excludes FLAKY and INTERRUPTED from the failing set
FLAKY passed on retry, so reopening a ticket conversation for a test that went green is noise; INTERRUPTED is a fact about the runner, not the code under test.
Jira's credential preflight spends one of its own call budget slots
An expired token would otherwise surface as a 404 from the comment endpoint, which reads as 'wrong issue key' and sends the reader hunting in the wrong place. Only a 401 is reported as a credentials problem.
Truncation is always named in the Jira detail line
Whenever the call cap or the time budget cuts the report short, the operator is told how many issues were left uncommented instead of the work being silently dropped.
Zephyr needs ZEPHYR_ENABLED as a third flag beyond token and project key
Executions are append-only, so a stray local run silently doubles a real project's history and there is no undo.
Zephyr uses its own key regex, and reuses issueKeysFor only to diagnose mis-tagging
A Zephyr Scale test case is `QA-T123`, which the shared pattern (digits straight after the hyphen) cannot find. issueKeysFor then distinguishes 'you used the wrong key' from 'you forgot'.
Zephyr maps FLAKY to the pass status name but records the retry count in the comment
Playwright reports flaky when the test passed on a retry and Zephyr has no equivalent state — so the result is not silently laundered into a clean pass.
Zephyr's time budget is checked before dequeuing and never cancels a request in flight
Aborting a POST that appends a row leaves nobody able to say whether the row landed.
Zephyr emits no url in its IntegrationResult
The cycle's `self` link is an authenticated API endpoint that answers 401 in a browser, and the tenant's Jira base URL is not something this process knows — so the cycle key in the detail is what a human can actually search for.
Zephyr warns once per run about unknown status names instead of failing
Status names are per-project strings an administrator can rename, and an unrecognised one is a 400 on every single execution — finding out once up front beats reading the same 400 per test. A partial status page warns about nothing at all.
Sauce publishes nothing to Sauce; it only links back
saucectl already stamps a job's name, build and tags at submit time, and rewriting a finished job's record from a reporter would make the Sauce UI and the run's own report disagree about what happened.
Sauce refuses to link anything without SAUCE_BUILD_NAME
Sauce has no 'current run' concept and the jobs endpoint returns the whole account's recent jobs — on a shared CI machine account that means other pipelines' jobs. Guessing 'the newest few jobs' would put someone else's run in this report.
Sauce's job lookup states its own search boundary in every message
limit/skip page newest-first over unbounded history, so 'not found' only ever means 'not found in the jobs I looked at'; promoting an empty window into a conclusion about the run would be a confident wrong answer.
Sauce region drives both hosts and is never defaulted on a typo
An EU access key answers 401 against api.us-west-1, and the US UI host has no region segment (app.saucelabs.com), so the naive `app.${region}.saucelabs.com` template produces a dead link. A set-but-unrecognised SAUCE_REGION returns undefined so the typo shows up as a configuration message.
Sauce credentials never leave the environment, and a non-JSON 200 body is dropped rather than quoted
.sauce/config.yml deliberately contains neither variable because saucectl reads both from the environment; and a proxy or SSO interception page is not information a report should carry.
report:open spawns the platform opener without a shell and with a percent-encoded file:// URL
With shell: true Node concatenates arguments unescaped, so a checkout under a path containing spaces reaches cmd's `start` as several tokens and nothing opens; `start` also needs an empty first argument or it reads the URL as a window title.
In the source
/*
 * `latest.*` is what `npm run report:open` opens, so only a run that actually executed
 * something advances it. A run that reported nothing — an unknown `--project`, a failed
 * global setup, `--list` — would otherwise replace the last real report with an empty one
 * and leave the reader believing the suite had zero tests.
 */
if (tests.length === 0) {
  process.stdout.write(
    `\nExtent report: ${htmlPath}\n` +
      `  no tests were executed (run status: ${result.status}) — ` +
      `reports/extent/latest.html still points at the previous run\n\n`,
  );
  await Promise.resolve();
  return;
}

/*
 * `reports/extent/latest.html` always points at the most recent run. It lives one directory
 * above the attachments, so it is rendered with the run folder as the asset prefix — without
 * it every screenshot, video and trace link in this copy would resolve to nothing.
 */
writeTextFile(
  resolve(PATHS.extentReport, 'latest.html'),
  renderExtentHtml(model, `${basename(this.reportDir)}/`),
);
Architecture

Test data and utilities (src/utils, src/data/factories, src/types/TestData.ts, test-data/)

This subsystem is the framework's data and plumbing layer: every functional value a test needs lives as JSON under `test-data/`, is read through `JsonReader` (which deep-merges an environment override over a shared `common` baseline and caches per process), and is typed by `TestDataRegistry` in `src/types/TestData.ts` so a call site needs no type annotation. `EmployeeFactory` turns a JSON template into a unique, parallel-safe create payload by layering `RandomUtils`/`DateUtils` values on top. Around that sit ten single-purpose utility modules — a structured `Logger` that pipes every message and payload through `DataMasker` before printing, a `FrameworkError` hierarchy that carries `operation`/`target`/`expected`/`actual`/`hint` plus the original cause, and helpers for retry, waiting, assertions, dates, files and randomness. The design intent stated repeatedly in the file headers is fail fast with an explanatory error, never leak a secret, and never let a test hard-code a functional value.

Utility modules in src/utils/10 (AssertionUtils 247, JsonReader 181, WaitUtils 150, Logger 140, FileUtils 123, RetryUtils 104, DateUtils 87, DataMasker 86, RandomUtils 71, FrameworkError 65 lines)

How it runs
  1. A test (or fixture) asks for a dataset by name `readTestData('employees', { environment: 'qa' })` — the generic `K extends TestDataName` makes the return type `EmployeeTestData` without an annotation. Tests reach it either directly (`import { readTestData } from '@utils/JsonReader'`) or through the `testData` fixture, whose `get()` supplies `environment.name` automatically. src/utils/JsonReader.ts:110, src/fixtures/base.fixture.ts:54
  2. Cache lookup `readJson` builds `cacheKey = `${environment ?? 'none'}::${datasetName}`` and returns the memoised value unless `options.fresh` is set. The cache is a module-level `Map<string, unknown>`, so it is per Node process (per Playwright worker). src/utils/JsonReader.ts:74-76
  3. Resolve the two candidate files `commonFile = resolve(PATHS.testData, 'common', `${datasetName}.json`)` and, when an environment was given, `envFile = resolve(PATHS.testData, environment, `${datasetName}.json`)`. `PATHS.testData` is derived from `ROOT_DIR`, itself resolved from `import.meta.url` rather than `process.cwd()`, so resolution does not depend on where the run was started. src/utils/JsonReader.ts:78-84, src/constants/FrameworkConstants.ts:6-15
  4. Fail loudly when neither file exists Throws `TestDataError('Test dataset not found')` with `operation: 'resolveDataset'`, the dataset name as `target`, both attempted paths as `expected`, and `available: availableDatasets().join(', ') || '(none)'` — the error tells you what you could have asked for. src/utils/JsonReader.ts:86-93
  5. Parse each file with a typed failure `parseFile` separates the two failure modes: a read failure becomes `TestDataError('Unable to read test-data file', { operation: 'readFile' }, error)` and a parse failure becomes `TestDataError('Test-data file is not valid JSON', { operation: 'parseJson' }, error)` — in both cases the original error is kept as the cause. src/utils/JsonReader.ts:40-60
  6. Deep-merge the environment override over the common baseline `deepMerge(base, override)` recurses only where both sides are plain objects; anything else (including arrays) is replaced wholesale — the header comment states 'arrays are replaced, not concatenated'. So `test-data/qa/employees.json` declaring only `pagination` inherits `templates`, `departments`, `validation` and `search` from common, while `test-data/dev/api.json` overrides only the two performance budgets. A dataset with no override file for that environment (e.g. `dashboard` anywhere, `employees` in dev) simply returns the common file. src/utils/JsonReader.ts:29-38, 95-96
  7. Log and cache the merged result `log.debug('dataset resolved', { dataset, common: hasCommon, environmentOverride: hasEnv, environment })` records which layers actually contributed, then the merged object is stored under the cache key and returned. src/utils/JsonReader.ts:98-106
  8. Global setup fails the whole run before a browser starts if data is incomplete Step 2 of `globalSetup` (after creating required directories, before credential resolution, reachability check and session minting) calls `assertDatasetKeys` three times against the resolved environment: `login` must have `validUsers, invalidScenarios, ui`; `employees` must have `templates, departments, validation`; `api` must have `endpoints, performance, negative`. Each reads the merged dataset, filters `requiredKeys` for `dataset[key] === undefined`, and on any miss throws `TestDataError('Test dataset is missing required keys')` with `expected: requiredKeys.join(', ')` and `actual: 'missing: …'`. global-setup.ts:137-147, src/utils/JsonReader.ts:152-167
  9. The factory selects a template from the merged dataset `dataset()` calls `readTestData('employees', { environment: resolveEnvironmentName() })` — the factory resolves the environment itself from `TEST_ENV` rather than taking it as a parameter. `selectTemplate(key)` finds the template by `key`, or takes `templates[0]` when no key is given, and throws `TestDataError('Employee template not found')` listing every available key when the lookup fails. src/data/factories/EmployeeFactory.ts:26-41
  10. Unique runtime values are layered over the template `buildEmployee` takes `department`, `designation`, `salary` and `status` verbatim from JSON, but replaces identity fields with generated ones: `uniqueName(template.namePrefix)`, `uniqueEmail(template.emailPrefix)`, and `joiningDate: toIsoDate(addDays(new Date(), -30))`. Caller `overrides` are spread last so any field can be pinned (e.g. forcing a duplicate email to test the 409). src/data/factories/EmployeeFactory.ts:44-56
  11. Uniqueness is worker-aware `uniqueEmail`/`uniqueName` build on `uniqueToken()` = worker index (`TEST_PARALLEL_INDEX` ?? `TEST_WORKER_INDEX` ?? '0') + `Date.now().toString(36)` + `randomInt(1000, 9999)` from `node:crypto`, and `uniqueEmail` prefixes `pwauto` so cleanup can find suite-created records. `uniqueName` uppercases the last six characters of the token. src/utils/RandomUtils.ts:12-36
  12. Negative cases come from the same JSON `buildInvalidEmployee(scenario)` finds the matching entry in `dataset().validation`, spreads its `overrides` over a valid payload, and returns `expectedStatus`, `expectedErrorCode` and `expectedField` alongside — so the assertion values live beside the data that produces them. An unknown scenario throws `TestDataError` listing every declared scenario joined by ' | '. src/data/factories/EmployeeFactory.ts:72-94
  13. Every log line is masked on the way out `Logger.write` drops the message if `LEVEL_WEIGHT[level] < LEVEL_WEIGHT[configuredLevel]`, then applies `maskString(message)` and `JSON.stringify(maskValue(payload))` before composing `timestamp | LEVEL | scope | message payload`. ERROR goes to `console.error`, WARN to `console.warn`, everything else to `process.stdout.write`; the undecorated line is also appended to `logs/run-<runId>.log` when file logging is on. src/utils/Logger.ts:108-131
  14. Masking is applied at the other leak points too `ApiClient` masks the URL, headers and (only under `verboseApiLogging`) request/response bodies on both the '->' and '<-' log lines and inside its error contexts; `ExtentReporter` masks step titles, test names, descriptions, annotation descriptions, error messages, stacks and text attachments; the Zephyr client and notifier mask body snippets and comment text. src/api/clients/ApiClient.ts:183-291, src/reporting/ExtentReporter.ts:85-314
  15. A failure anywhere in the subsystem surfaces as a self-describing error The `FrameworkError` constructor joins the message, the rendered context (one ` key: value` line per defined, non-empty entry) and ` cause: <message>`, sets `this.name = new.target.name` so the subclass name shows up, and passes `{ cause }` to `super` only when the cause is a real Error. src/utils/FrameworkError.ts:27-52
Design decisions18
Environment datasets are deltas, not copies — the environment file is deep-merged over the common file and arrays are replaced rather than concatenated.
So an environment only has to declare what actually differs, which stops four near-identical copies of the same dataset drifting apart. Array replacement is chosen so an override can shrink or reorder a list rather than only ever growing it.
Dataset names are a closed, typed set: `TestDataRegistry` maps each name to its parsed type and `TestDataName = keyof TestDataRegistry`.
The call site gets full typing with no annotation and no cast, and a typo in a dataset name is a compile error rather than a runtime `undefined`. `readJson<T>` is kept as the untyped escape hatch for anything not in the registry.
Missing test data fails the entire run in global setup, before credentials are resolved, before the environment is probed and before any browser is launched.
A malformed dataset would otherwise surface as N confusing per-test failures deep into a run. Ordering the check second — after only directory creation — makes the cheapest, most deterministic check the first thing that can fail.
`assertDatasetKeys` reports every missing key at once, and `readPath` throws with the exact segment that stopped traversal instead of returning `undefined`.
One run tells you everything that is wrong, and a missing nested value names itself rather than showing up later as a cryptic `undefined` in an assertion.
Resolution is anchored to a repo-root derived from `import.meta.url`, not `process.cwd()`.
Dataset lookup works identically whether the run is started from the repo root, a subdirectory, or an IDE runner.
Datasets are cached per process keyed by `<environment>::<dataset>`, with a `fresh` opt-out and a `clearCache()` used only for testing the reader itself.
A dataset is read repeatedly (module load in specs, per test via the fixture, per factory call) and re-reading and re-merging JSON each time is wasted work; keying by environment keeps two environments from sharing an entry in the same process.
The factory splits functional values (JSON) from identity values (generated) rather than storing whole records in JSON.
Functional data stays reviewable and environment-overridable in JSON, while name/email/joining date are generated per call so records never collide across parallel workers or repeated runs.
Uniqueness embeds the Playwright worker index and stamps every value with the `pwauto` prefix.
The worker index removes cross-worker collisions that a timestamp alone would not (two workers can start in the same millisecond), and the prefix makes suite-created records identifiable for cleanup.
Negative-test expectations (`expectedStatus`, `expectedErrorCode`, `expectedField`) are stored in JSON next to the overrides that trigger them, and returned together by `buildInvalidEmployee`.
The spec then contains no magic numbers — adding a validation scenario is a JSON edit, and the expectation cannot drift away from the input that produces it.
Masking sits inside the logger rather than at each call site — every message and payload is redacted unconditionally on the way out.
A caller cannot forget to mask. The Logger header states the guarantee directly: a secret cannot reach a log line even if someone passes one in.
Redaction matches on both key names (normalised, substring-tolerant) and value patterns.
Key matching catches the ordinary `{ password: '…' }` case; the five regexes catch secrets embedded in free text or in a field whose name looks harmless. Normalising the key (lowercase, strip `- _` and whitespace) plus a substring test means `Access-Token`, `access_token` and `userAccessToken` all match the same entry.
`maskValue` tolerates cycles and unwraps Errors instead of throwing.
The masker runs on the failure path, where the payload is often an Error or a live object graph; a masker that throws would destroy the diagnostic it was supposed to protect.
Errors carry a structured `ErrorContext` (required `operation`, optional `target`/`page`/`expected`/`actual`/`environment`/`url`, plus an open index signature) that is rendered into the message, with the original cause always preserved.
The message alone is enough to act on — what was attempted, against what, what was expected versus seen — and the open index signature lets a call site add `hint`, `timeout` or `attempts` without changing the interface. `new.target.name` means the subclass name is on the error even though no subclass defines a constructor.
Four thin subclasses (`UiActionError`, `ApiRequestError`, `TestDataError`, `ValidationError`) with empty bodies rather than an error-code enum.
The class name is the category, so `instanceof` filtering and readable stack traces come for free with no extra ceremony; behaviour stays entirely in the base.
Retry is opt-in per failure: `retryOn` defaults to a function that always returns false.
So retries cannot quietly mask a real defect — a caller must name what is transient. When retries do happen, every attempt's message is folded into the final error so the flakiness is visible.
Waiting helpers exist only for conditions Playwright's auto-waiting cannot express, and assertion helpers wrap web-first `expect` rather than looping.
To keep arbitrary sleeps and hand-rolled retry loops out of the suite while still supporting computed conditions and debounced values.
File logging degrades instead of failing: a `fileLoggingBroken` latch disables the sink after the first write or mkdir error.
An unwritable `logs/` directory (a read-only CI filesystem, say) should not take down the run or spam a warning on every line.
Upload fixtures are generated at runtime rather than committed as binaries.
Keeps binaries out of the repository; only a genuinely irreproducible document justifies a committed file.
In the source
/**
 * Employee data factory.
 *
 * Implements the test-data lifecycle (rule 29): the JSON template is the source of functional
 * values, and unique runtime values (email, name, joining date) are layered on top so records
 * never collide across parallel workers.
 */

function dataset(): EmployeeTestData {
  return readTestData('employees', { environment: resolveEnvironmentName() });
}

function selectTemplate(key?: string): EmployeeTemplate {
  const templates = dataset().templates;
  const template = key ? templates.find((candidate) => candidate.key === key) : templates[0];
  if (!template) {
    throw new TestDataError('Employee template not found', {
      operation: 'selectTemplate',
      target: key ?? '(first template)',
      expected: `one of: ${templates.map((candidate) => candidate.key).join(', ')}`,
    });
  }
  return template;
}

/** Builds a unique, valid create payload from a JSON template. */
export function buildEmployee(options: BuildOptions = {}): EmployeeCreateRequest {
  const template = selectTemplate(options.templateKey);
  return {
    name: uniqueName(template.namePrefix),
    email: uniqueEmail(template.emailPrefix),
    department: template.department,
    designation: template.designation,
    salary: options.randomSalary ? randomSalary() : template.salary,
    joiningDate: toIsoDate(addDays(new Date(), -30)),
    status: template.status,
    ...options.overrides,
  };
}

/* --- and how a spec uses it (tests/api/regression/employee-negative.api.spec.ts) --- */

const original = await adminEmployeeApi.createOrThrow(buildEmployee());
cleanup.employee(original.id);

const duplicate = await adminEmployeeApi.create(
  buildEmployee({ overrides: { email: original.email } }),
);
verify(duplicate).hasStatus(HTTP_STATUS.CONFLICT).isFailure(API_ERROR_CODES.duplicateEmail);
Architecture

Test suites and the execution model (playwright.config.ts projects, tag taxonomy, npm script surface, and the nine spec files under tests/)

The execution model is a single `defineConfig` in `playwright.config.ts` that declares nine projects over one `testDir: './tests'`, and a tag taxonomy (`src/constants/TestConstants.ts` `TAGS`) that the npm scripts `--grep` to carve suites out of that same body of specs. Suite membership is folder-driven — the `api` project narrows to `./tests/api` and declares `metadata: { requiresBrowser: false }` so a browserless run skips session creation entirely; the seven UI projects share `testIgnore: ['**/tests/api/**', '**/tests/visual/**']` and therefore pick up `tests/ui` plus `tests/hybrid`; the `visual` project narrows to `./tests/visual` and pins `--force-device-scale-factor=1`. Nothing environment-specific is hardcoded: timeouts, retries and base URLs come from `config/environments/<env>.json` via `getEnvironment()`, and execution knobs (workers, headless, retries) come from `frameworkConfig`. A `webServer` block starts the bundled dependency-free reference app (`demo-app/server.mjs`) only when the target actually is that local sandbox, which is what lets the whole framework run end to end with no external environment.

How it runs
  1. Resolve the environment before any project is defined `const environment = getEnvironment();` reads `config/environments/<TEST_ENV>.json` (default `dev`). Every baseURL, timeout and retry count in the config is read off it — the config file's own header says "There is no business logic here (rule 11) and nothing environment-specific is hardcoded." playwright.config.ts:22
  2. Build the shared `use` block `sharedUse` sets baseURL to `environment.ui.baseUrl`, actionTimeout/navigationTimeout from the environment, `testIdAttribute: 'data-testid'`, and failure-only diagnostics: `screenshot: 'only-on-failure'`, `video: 'retain-on-failure'`, `trace: 'retain-on-failure'` — commented "captured only when a test fails, so a green run stays cheap." playwright.config.ts:27-40
  3. Set run-level timeouts, parallelism and retries `timeout: environment.timeouts.test` (dev 60000 ms, qa/uat/prod 90000 ms), `expect: { timeout: environment.timeouts.expect }` (dev 10000, others 15000), `fullyParallel: true`, `forbidOnly: frameworkConfig.isCi`, `retries: frameworkConfig.retries` (dev 0 local / 1 CI; qa, uat, prod 2 on CI), `workers: frameworkConfig.workers` (2 on CI, else `Math.max(1, Math.min(6, Math.floor(cpus().length / 2)))`), `maxFailures: frameworkConfig.isCi ? 25 : 0`, `reportSlowTests: { max: 5, threshold: 60_000 }`. playwright.config.ts:50-58
  4. Point visual baselines away from failure screenshots `snapshotPathTemplate: '{testDir}/__screenshots__/{projectName}/{testFileName}/{arg}{ext}'` — with the visual project's `testDir: './tests/visual'` this resolves to the on-disk `tests/visual/__screenshots__/visual/login.visual.spec.ts/login-page.png`. The spec header notes baselines are "separate from the failure screenshots in `reports/`, so a diff is never confused with a diagnostic capture." playwright.config.ts:45
  5. Declare nine projects that carve the one testDir into suites `api` (testDir './tests/api', `metadata: { requiresBrowser: false }`, `use: { baseURL: environment.api.baseUrl }`); `chromium`, `firefox`, `webkit` (Desktop devices + `viewport: VIEWPORTS.laptop`); `edge` (`channel: 'msedge'`, "selected explicitly, never by default"); `tablet-ipad` (`devices['iPad (gen 7)']`, `viewport: VIEWPORTS.tablet`, `isMobile: false`); `mobile-chrome` (`devices['Pixel 7']`); `mobile-safari` (`devices['iPhone 14']`); `visual` (testDir './tests/visual'). All seven browser UI projects share `testIgnore: UI_TEST_IGNORE`. playwright.config.ts:71-138
  6. UI_TEST_IGNORE decides what a UI project actually runs `const UI_TEST_IGNORE = ['**/tests/api/**', '**/tests/visual/**'];` — so each UI project runs tests/ui/{smoke,sanity,regression,e2e} plus tests/hybrid, and never the API-only or baseline suites. This is why every UI project collects exactly 31 tests. playwright.config.ts:25
  7. The visual project forces the device scale factor `launchOptions: { ...sharedUse.launchOptions, args: ['--force-device-scale-factor=1'] }`, commented: without it Chromium "inherits the desktop DPI and reports devicePixelRatio 1.0000000123 rather than 1, which rounds a 1440px viewport up to 1441 and fails every baseline by one column of pixels." playwright.config.ts:126-135
  8. Conditionally attach the webServer for the bundled reference app Spread in only when `frameworkConfig.startReferenceApp`: `command: 'node demo-app/server.mjs'`, `url: `${environment.api.baseUrl}/health``, `reuseExistingServer: !frameworkConfig.isCi`, `timeout: 30_000`, `stdout: 'ignore'`, `stderr: 'pipe'`, `env: { DEMO_APP_PORT: String(frameworkConfig.referenceAppPort) }` (default port 4321). The flag itself is `bool(process.env.START_REFERENCE_APP, environment.name === 'dev') && environment.ui.baseUrl.includes(String(referenceAppPort))`, so pointing an environment file at a deployed URL disables the block. playwright.config.ts:140-155 (flag at config/framework.config.ts:64-66)
  9. Global setup reads the --project flags off argv to decide if a browser is needed "Playwright hands global setup the whole configuration rather than the selection, so `config.projects` still lists all nine projects during a `--project=api` run." `selectedProjects()` parses `--project=x` and `--project x`; `requiresBrowser(project)` returns `project.metadata.requiresBrowser !== false` (default-safe). Only `if (projects.some(requiresBrowser))` is chromium launched to mint storage states for ADMIN, MANAGER, EMPLOYEE — otherwise it logs "no browser-backed project selected — skipping session state creation". global-setup.ts:36-60, 163-179
  10. Global setup fails fast before spending time Order is: ensure directories → `assertDatasetKeys` on login/employees/api datasets → `environment.credentialsFor(role)` for each role "before a browser is launched" → `waitForEnvironment(environment.api.baseUrl)` polling `/health` for 60 s → storage states → write `reports/run-context.json`. global-setup.ts:130-197
  11. npm scripts select projects, then grep a tag Nine scripts use --grep: `test:smoke` and `test:regression`, `test:critical`, `test:negative` run `--project=api --project=chromium --grep @<tag>`; `test:sanity` and `test:e2e` are chromium-only; `test:security` is `--project=api --grep @security`; `test:prod` is `TEST_ENV=prod ... --grep @smoke`; `test:headed` is `--headed --grep @e2e`. `test:contract` selects by path instead (`--project=api tests/api/contract`), and `test:visual` / `test:visual:update` select the `visual` project (the latter with `--update-snapshots`). package.json:11-53
  12. Specs opt into an authenticated session rather than logging in `test.use({ role: 'ADMIN' })` at the top of the sanity, hybrid, network and employee-management suites resolves the `role` option (default `'ADMIN'`), which backs the `dashboardAs` / `employeesAs` Page Object fixtures built on a context created with `storageState: statePath`. Only `tests/ui/smoke/login.smoke.spec.ts` and the visual login baselines use the plain `loginPage` — its header calls it "The one place the framework deliberately signs in through the UI on every run". src/fixtures/auth.fixture.ts:53-78; tests/ui/sanity/dashboard.sanity.spec.ts:13
  13. Teardown removes live tokens `globalTeardown` stamps `finishedAt`/`durationMs` onto `reports/run-context.json` and calls `clearStorageStates(ROLES)` unless `KEEP_AUTH_STATE` is set, because "Session files carry live tokens." global-teardown.ts:27-51
Design decisions13
The API project declares `metadata: { requiresBrowser: false }` instead of the setup guessing from the project name
So a `--project=api` run never launches or requires a browser binary — a fresh clone can get API signal without `playwright install`. The check is written default-safe: a project needs a browser unless it explicitly opts out.
Suite membership is expressed as one shared `testIgnore` constant rather than per-project globs
Every browser project must run exactly the same body of UI + hybrid specs; a single named constant makes 'what a UI project runs' one line instead of seven.
The visual project pins `--force-device-scale-factor=1`
Pixel comparison must not depend on the host's display scaling; without it a 1440px viewport rounds to 1441 and every baseline fails by one column of pixels.
Visual baselines are stored beside the spec, under a project-scoped folder, via snapshotPathTemplate
A baseline diff must never be confused with an only-on-failure diagnostic screenshot, and two projects must not share one baseline.
The webServer block is spread in conditionally and disables itself against a deployed URL
The bundled reference app is a local sandbox convenience, not something that should try to boot when the run targets qa/uat/prod.
Diagnostics are failure-only across every project
Keeps a green run cheap while still producing a trace, video and screenshot for anything that fails.
Negative/validation cases are generated from JSON arrays inside `for` loops at module load
"adding a case is a data change rather than a code change" — and each scenario still surfaces as its own named test in the report rather than as one looping test.
Tests never assert against a global count of shared state ("Rule 22")
Suites run `fullyParallel: true` across up to six workers against one directory, so a parallel worker creating or deleting a record must not make a correct assertion fail.
The visual employees baseline pins the page size and masks the row data
Other suites add and remove records in parallel; masking hides what rows say but not how many there are, so the table height has to be fixed. The eight seeded reference records cannot be deleted, guaranteeing a full first page.
Only the login smoke suite signs in through the UI; everything else reuses storage state
Paying for a UI login per test is the dominant cost in a UI suite; the login flow itself still needs real coverage, so exactly one suite keeps it.
The hybrid suite uses the API for setup/teardown/verification and the UI only where the user experience is under test
Speed and reliability for the parts that are not the subject of the test, while still proving the two surfaces agree — and proving that authorisation is a server-side boundary, not a hidden button.
`edge` is declared but never selected by default
It needs Microsoft Edge installed on the runner, so making it part of a default run would break clean machines.
`maxFailures` is 25 on CI and 0 locally, and `forbidOnly` only on CI
CI should abandon a hopeless run rather than burn the full matrix, while a local run should report everything it can.
In the source
// playwright.config.ts — the carving of one testDir into nine projects
/** UI projects run everything except the API-only and visual suites. */
const UI_TEST_IGNORE = ['**/tests/api/**', '**/tests/visual/**'];

  projects: [
    {
      name: 'api',
      testDir: './tests/api',
      /* Browserless: global setup skips session creation when only this project is selected. */
      metadata: { requiresBrowser: false },
      use: { baseURL: environment.api.baseUrl },
    },
    {
      name: 'chromium',
      testIgnore: UI_TEST_IGNORE,
      use: { ...devices['Desktop Chrome'], ...sharedUse, viewport: VIEWPORTS.laptop },
    },
    // …firefox, webkit, edge (channel: 'msedge'), tablet-ipad, mobile-chrome, mobile-safari…
    {
      name: 'visual',
      testDir: './tests/visual',
      use: {
        ...devices['Desktop Chrome'],
        ...sharedUse,
        viewport: VIEWPORTS.laptop,
        /*
         * Pixel comparison must not depend on the host's display scaling. Without this Chromium
         * inherits the desktop DPI and reports devicePixelRatio 1.0000000123 rather than 1, which
         * rounds a 1440px viewport up to 1441 and fails every baseline by one column of pixels.
         */
        launchOptions: {
          ...sharedUse.launchOptions,
          args: ['--force-device-scale-factor=1'],
        },
      },
    },
  ],
Architecture

CI/CD, tooling and the bundled reference application

Three GitHub Actions workflows tier the feedback loop by cost: `Smoke` on every push, `Playwright CI` as the pull-request gate (static checks first, then API and a three-browser UI matrix), and `Regression` nightly on cron across five device projects sharded in two. Four Node scripts back the local developer loop — `verify-framework.mjs` runs the same PR gate in cheapest-first order and prints one verdict, `clean.mjs` deletes generated artifacts while preserving visual baselines and `.gitkeep` skeletons, `open-extent-report.mjs` opens the latest Extent HTML, and `write-sauce-config.mts` regenerates `.sauce/config.yml` from a typed TypeScript object so the saucectl file and the framework's own Sauce reasoning cannot drift. ESLint runs typed linting on `.ts`/`.mts` only, banning `any`, floating promises and implicit member accessibility, and layers `eslint-plugin-playwright` on `tests/**` with an explicit registry of 40 assertion function names. The reference application is a dependency-free `node:http` server on port 4321 serving five HTML pages and a 7-path REST API under `/api/v1`, with three seeded users, five departments and eight seeded employees whose deliberate behaviours — protected seeded records, 422 field-level validation, role-gated delete and user listing — are exactly what the negative and security suites assert against.

How it runs
  1. A push to main or develop fires the Smoke workflow One `smoke` job on ubuntu-latest, 20-minute timeout: checkout, setup-node 22 with npm cache, `npm ci`, `npx playwright install --with-deps chromium`, then `npm run test:smoke`. Concurrency group `smoke-${{ github.ref }}-${{ inputs.environment || 'dev' }}` with cancel-in-progress. Uploads reports/extent for 14 days, and test-results + logs for 7 days only `if: ${{ failure() }}`. .github/workflows/smoke.yml:24
  2. A pull request against main or develop fires Playwright CI, which gates on static checks first The `static-checks` job runs `npm run typecheck`, `npm run lint` and `npm run format:check` as three separate steps with a 10-minute timeout. Both test jobs declare `needs: static-checks`, so nothing installs a browser until types, lint and formatting are clean. .github/workflows/playwright.yml:29
  3. The API and UI jobs run in parallel behind that gate `api-tests` runs `npx playwright test --project=api` with no browser install at all (15-minute timeout). `ui-tests` is a `fail-fast: false` matrix over `[chromium, firefox, webkit]`, installs only its own browser with `npx playwright install --with-deps ${{ matrix.project }}`, and runs `--grep "${{ inputs.grep || '@smoke|@sanity' }}"` — so a PR runs the tagged fast subset, not everything. .github/workflows/playwright.yml:47
  4. Both jobs upload reports, and the UI job additionally uploads diagnostics only on failure Reports go up under `if: ${{ !cancelled() }}` (so a failed run still publishes results) with 14-day retention; `diagnostics-${{ matrix.project }}` collects `test-results/**/*.png`, `*.webm`, `trace.zip` and `logs` under `if: ${{ failure() }}` with 7-day retention. .github/workflows/playwright.yml:108
  5. publish-summary downloads every reports-* artifact and writes a markdown table into the job summary It deliberately omits `merge-multiple`, because every artifact carries `extent/latest.json` at the same relative path and flattening would leave only the last download. It finds each `latest.json`, takes the job name from `cut -d/ -f2`, and prints total/passed/failed/flaky/skipped/passRate; if none are found it writes "No Extent summary found". .github/workflows/playwright.yml:130
  6. On weeknights at 20:00 UTC the Regression workflow runs the full matrix `cron: "0 20 * * 1-5"` (commented as 01:30 IST, weeknights), env `TEST_ENV: qa` and `RETRIES: "2"`, concurrency `regression-${{ inputs.environment || 'qa' }}` with `cancel-in-progress: false` so a nightly is never killed by a dispatch. .github/workflows/regression.yml:5
  7. Regression fans out to ten UI jobs plus one API job `ui-regression` is a matrix of `project: [chromium, firefox, webkit, mobile-chrome, tablet-ipad]` x `shard: [1, 2]`, each running `npx playwright test --project=<p> --shard=<s>/2` with a 45-minute timeout after `npx playwright install --with-deps` (all browsers, unlike the PR workflow). `api-regression` runs the api project alone at 25 minutes. Artifacts are kept 30 days, diagnostics 14. .github/workflows/regression.yml:57
  8. A notify job summarises both results with if: always() It echoes the environment heading and `needs.api-regression.result` / `needs.ui-regression.result` into $GITHUB_STEP_SUMMARY, with a trailing comment marking the Slack/Teams webhook extension point. .github/workflows/regression.yml:105
  9. Locally, npm run verify reproduces the same gate in one command `scripts/verify-framework.mjs` walks a five-entry `steps` array with `spawnSync(..., { stdio: 'inherit', shell: process.platform === 'win32' })`, timing each, then prints a `──────── verification summary ────────` block of PASS/FAIL lines and exits 1 if any step failed. Crucially it does NOT stop at the first failure — every step runs so you see all breakage at once. scripts/verify-framework.mjs:8
  10. Any suite starts the reference application through Playwright's webServer block `playwright.config.ts` conditionally adds `webServer: { command: 'node demo-app/server.mjs', url: `${environment.api.baseUrl}/health`, reuseExistingServer: !isCi, timeout: 30_000, env: { DEMO_APP_PORT: … } }` — but only when `frameworkConfig.startReferenceApp` is true, which is derived from whether the environment's UI baseUrl contains the reference-app port. Point an environment file at a deployed URL and the block disables itself. playwright.config.ts:143
  11. The server boots, seeds in memory, and listens on 4321 `PORT = Number(process.env.DEMO_APP_PORT ?? 4321)`, `API_PREFIX = '/api/v1'`. `seed()` is called at module scope, filling the `employees` Map with eight rows. Sessions live in a `Map` of token -> userId, so every restart invalidates all tokens and resets all data — each run starts from the same eight records. demo-app/server.mjs:17
  12. Every request gets permissive CORS and is split between the API and static routers The handler sets `access-control-allow-origin: *`, allows `content-type, authorization, x-api-key, x-correlation-id` and the GET/POST/PUT/PATCH/DELETE/OPTIONS methods, short-circuits OPTIONS with a 204, then routes on `url.pathname.startsWith(API_PREFIX)`. The returned promise is caught centrally, logging and emitting a 500 INTERNAL_ERROR if headers are not yet sent. demo-app/server.mjs:374
  13. Inside handleApi, /health and POST /auth/login are answered before authentication `/health` returns `{ status: 'UP', uptimeSeconds, employees: employees.size }` unauthenticated. Login validates username+password, matches the email case-insensitively, and on success mints `tkn_${randomUUID()}` into the sessions Map, returning `{ token, expiresIn: 3600, user }`. Only after these does `authenticate(req)` run and reject with 401 UNAUTHORIZED plus a `details.reason`. demo-app/server.mjs:167
  14. Authenticated routes then apply their own role and record checks GET /users is ADMIN-only (403 FORBIDDEN otherwise). DELETE /employees/:id requires ADMIN or MANAGER, and even then refuses a `seeded` record with 409 PROTECTED_RECORD before deleting. Successful delete replies 204 with no body. demo-app/server.mjs:215
  15. The negative and security suites assert exactly those refusals `tests/api/regression/employee-negative.api.spec.ts` authenticates as EMPLOYEE, confirms listing is permitted, then asserts the delete is FORBIDDEN with `.hasErrorMessageContaining('role required')` and re-reads the record to prove it survived; a separate test asserts a duplicate email is CONFLICT / DUPLICATE_EMAIL. The codes are mirrored in `API_ERROR_CODES`. tests/api/regression/employee-negative.api.spec.ts:85
  16. npm run clean resets the workspace without destroying baselines It rm -rf's twelve targets (the six reports subfolders plus reports/downloads and reports/run-context.json, test-results, playwright-report, logs, storage/auth), then recreates `logs`, `storage/auth` and `reports` and writes a `.gitkeep` into each. `tests/visual/__screenshots__` is never in the target list, so visual baselines survive. scripts/clean.mjs:11
  17. npm run report:open surfaces the last Extent run It refuses with an exit-1 message if `reports/extent/latest.html` is missing, prints the summary line from latest.json inside a try/catch (a truncated file must not block the open), converts the path with `pathToFileURL`, and spawns the platform opener detached with no shell. scripts/open-extent-report.mjs:19
  18. npm run sauce:config regenerates the saucectl YAML from TypeScript `node --experimental-strip-types scripts/write-sauce-config.mts` imports SAUCECTL_CONFIG with an explicit `.ts` specifier, writes `toSaucectlYaml(SAUCECTL_CONFIG)` to `.sauce/config.yml`, and echoes the suite names plus `saucectlRunCommand()`. scripts/write-sauce-config.mts:14
Design decisions48
The PR workflow makes the test jobs depend on a cheap static-checks job
Lint, type and format failures are found in minutes without ever provisioning a browser, so no runner minutes are spent on a PR that cannot compile.
The PR UI matrix installs only the browser it is about to use
`--with-deps` for all three engines is the slowest step in the job; per-matrix install cuts it to a third. The nightly, which is not latency-sensitive, installs everything.
publish-summary deliberately does not use merge-multiple when downloading artifacts
Every artifact contains extent/latest.json at the same relative path, so flattening them into one directory would leave only the last download and the table would report a single unlabelled job.
Report uploads use `if: ${{ !cancelled() }}` while diagnostics use `if: ${{ failure() }}`
A failing run is exactly when you need the report, so it must still publish; heavy artifacts (videos, traces, screenshots) are only worth storing when something actually broke, and get a shorter retention.
Regression sets `cancel-in-progress: false` while smoke and PR CI set it true
A superseded PR or push run is worthless, but a half-finished nightly regression is not — killing it would lose the only full-matrix signal of the night.
Sauce-level retries are pinned to 0
Playwright already retries inside the run; a second retry layer at the Sauce level would double-count results.
verify-framework runs every step even after one fails, rather than exiting early
One command should surface all the breakage in a change, not just the first thing that broke — the summary table is the deliverable, the exit code is secondary.
verify-framework orders its five steps cheapest-first
TypeScript, ESLint and Prettier are seconds; the API suite is browserless; only the last step launches Chromium. The expensive step is reached last.
clean.mjs recreates a .gitkeep skeleton after deleting
The directories themselves are tracked in git so a fresh clone can write into them; only their generated contents are disposable.
Visual baselines are excluded from clean by construction
Deleting baselines would silently turn every visual test into a first-run snapshot write instead of a comparison.
open-extent-report spawns the opener without a shell, using a percent-encoded file:// URL
With `shell: true` Node concatenates arguments unescaped, so a checkout under a path containing spaces reaches cmd's `start` as several tokens and nothing opens — which is exactly this repo's own layout.
The Windows opener is invoked as `cmd /c start '' <url>` with an empty first argument
`start` reads its first quoted argument as the window title, so without the empty placeholder the URL is consumed as a title and no browser opens.
A missing opener is handled with an explicit 'error' listener
Without one, a missing `xdg-open` surfaces as an unhandled 'error' event (a crash) rather than an actionable message telling the user the report's path.
The Extent summary read is wrapped in try/catch and only warns
The summary line is a convenience; a truncated or half-written latest.json must not stop you from opening the HTML report.
.sauce/config.yml is generated from a typed object rather than hand-edited
The region written into the YAML and the region the Sauce REST lookups use must not drift apart; one TypeScript object is the single source.
The YAML is emitted by a hand-written serialiser that quotes every scalar
The framework takes no YAML dependency for one generated file, and unquoted values would let regex `testMatch` strings and a version like `1.61.1` be reinterpreted as numbers or dates.
.sauceignore is treated as a security control, not a size optimisation
saucectl zips the whole of rootDir ('./') and ships it to a Sauce VM; without exclusions the archive would carry the local .env and storage/auth session files — real credentials and live tokens — off the machine.
Typed linting is scoped to .ts/.mts, with .js/.mjs explicitly de-type-checked
Tooling scripts have no tsconfig project to type against; running the type-aware rules on them would only produce noise.
The disableTypeChecked rules are spread before the block's own rules
A bare `rules` key on that config object would replace, not merge, and silently discard everything disableTypeChecked turns off.
no-explicit-any is an error while the no-unsafe-* family is switched off
The rule enforced is that developers never write `any` themselves; the unsafe-* rules fire on inference from third-party types and would drown the signal.
explicit-member-accessibility is required everywhere except constructors
Every class member declares public/private/protected as documentation, but `public` on a constructor is noise since it is the only legal modifier there.
no-floating-promises and await-thenable are errors alongside require-await
In an async test framework an un-awaited promise is a silently passing test; these three catch the forgotten await, the pointless await, and the async function that never awaits.
Empty catch blocks are banned outright
Swallowing an exception hides a real failure behind a green test.
no-console is an error framework-wide but disabled for four specific paths
All framework logging must go through the Logger sink; the reporter, the ops scripts and the demo app are the legitimate places that print directly.
no-empty-pattern is turned off in two separate places
Playwright requires a hook's first argument to be an object destructuring pattern, so `({}, testInfo)` is the supported idiom for a hook that only needs testInfo — the default rule would flag correct code.
playwright/expect-expect is configured with an explicit 40-name assertFunctionNames registry
A test 'asserts' when it calls expect, an API validator, or a Page Object / component assertion method; the rule matches only the final identifier of the call, so custom helpers must be registered or the rule reports a real test as assertion-free.
playwright/no-wait-for-timeout is an error while no-force-option and no-skipped-test are only warnings
An arbitrary sleep is always wrong and makes a suite flaky; a forced click or a conditionally skipped test can be legitimate, so they nag rather than block.
eslint-config-prettier is applied last in the flat config array
It exists to switch off stylistic rules that would fight the formatter, which only works if nothing re-enables them afterwards.
Prettier forces double quotes for JSON and YAML via an override
The repo-wide style is single quotes, but single-quoted keys are invalid JSON and are needlessly unusual in YAML.
The reference application takes zero dependencies and holds all state in memory
The framework must be executable, demonstrable and verifiable end to end without an external environment; a Map that resets on restart also guarantees a known-identical starting state for every run.
Seeded employees are flagged `seeded: true` and refused deletion with 409 PROTECTED_RECORD
The eight reference rows must survive any suite that deletes records, otherwise a parallel or repeated run would erode the fixture data the UI and visual tests depend on. It also gives the negative suite a deterministic 409 to assert.
Seeded ids are derived deterministically from the email rather than randomised
A test can address a known seeded record by id across restarts without first listing.
Two authentication schemes coexist: bearer session tokens and a single x-api-key
Bearer exercises the real login/session/logout lifecycle and carries the caller's role; the API key is a machine door that resolves straight to the ADMIN user, so setup and teardown can act without logging in.
The 401 response carries a machine-readable `details.reason`
It distinguishes a bad token from a bad API key from no credentials at all, so a negative test can assert which failure mode occurred rather than just 'unauthorized'.
Validation failures return 422 with a per-field details array, not a flat 400
It separates 'the JSON did not parse' (400 MALFORMED_JSON) from 'the JSON parsed but the fields are wrong' (422 VALIDATION_ERROR), and gives tests field-level assertions.
PATCH validates with `{ partial: true }` while PUT validates fully
The two methods must behave differently: a PUT is a full replacement so required fields must be present, a PATCH is a merge of only the supplied keys.
Department is validated against a closed list of five values
It gives the suite a guaranteed 422 case with an enumerable message, and keeps the UI department filter and the API in lockstep.
Delete requires ADMIN or MANAGER, and user listing requires ADMIN — with the role check before the existence check
Three roles give the security suite a real permission boundary to probe; checking the role first means an unauthorised caller cannot use 403-vs-404 to discover which ids exist.
The users list strips the password field by destructuring it away
The endpoint must never leak credentials even though they live on the same in-memory objects.
Demo credentials are env-overridable with literal defaults
The suite runs out of the box with no .env, yet CI can inject the same secrets the workflows pass (ADMIN_USERNAME, API_KEY, …) so the framework and the app agree on identity.
The static router refuses any path that escapes PUBLIC_DIR
Path traversal protection for a server that maps URL segments onto the filesystem.
Every response is sent with `cache-control: no-store` and a fresh `x-request-id`
No test can be poisoned by a cached response, and each response carries a correlation id the framework's logging can pick up.
The dashboard bundles upload, download, native dialog and iframe into one page
It gives the UI suite a single real surface for the four browser interactions that are otherwise hard to exercise without an external app.
The employee form uses a hand-built date picker over a readonly input instead of type="date"
A native date input is driven by fill(); a popup of `button[data-date]` cells forces the Page Object to model a real component interaction, which is the point of the exercise.
The employee search input is debounced by 200ms
It makes the table genuinely asynchronous, so a test that types and immediately asserts will fail unless it waits properly — the framework's waiting strategy has to be real.
Every interactive element carries a data-testid, matched by the config's testIdAttribute
Locators bind to a stable contract rather than to CSS or copy, so restyling or rewording the app cannot break the suite.
demo-app/public/** is excluded from ESLint entirely while demo-app/** is exempted from no-console
The browser-side inline scripts are neither Node nor part of the typed framework; the server file is still linted, just allowed to print.
The rendered table is accessible by construction — caption, scope, aria-sort, aria-live, role=alertdialog
The reference app has to be a fair target for accessibility-aware locators (getByRole) rather than a div soup that forces CSS selectors.
In the source
// demo-app/server.mjs — the deliberate behaviours the negative and security suites assert against:
// role gate before existence check (no 403-vs-404 id probing), then the protected-seed refusal.

    if (method === 'DELETE') {
      if (!['ADMIN', 'MANAGER'].includes(currentUser.role))
        return fail(res, 403, 'FORBIDDEN', 'ADMIN or MANAGER role required to delete an employee');
      if (!existing) return fail(res, 404, 'NOT_FOUND', `Employee ${id} was not found`);
      if (existing.seeded)
        return fail(res, 409, 'PROTECTED_RECORD', 'Seeded reference records cannot be deleted');
      employees.delete(id);
      res.writeHead(204).end();
      return;
    }

    await test.step('Deleting is refused', async () => {
      verify(await employeeApi.remove(target.id))
        .hasStatus(HTTP_STATUS.FORBIDDEN)
        .isFailure(API_ERROR_CODES.forbidden)
        .hasErrorMessageContaining('role required');
    });

    await test.step('The record survives the refused delete', async () => {
      verify(await adminEmployeeApi.getById(target.id))
        .hasStatus(HTTP_STATUS.OK)
        .isSuccessful();
